### Description

Step 3 of the layout in #86562, after #130348 (step 2).

- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs-cmake` and `contrib/chdig-cmake` get one-line wrapper crates (`pub use delta_kernel_ffi;`, `pub use chdig;`), imported through the workspace manifest like the other six.
- One environment for every member (`clickhouse_config_crate_env`: OpenSSL variables, `CFLAGS` with `-I contrib/openssl/include`, `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): build scripts track their environment, so any difference rebuilds shared crates every build.
- `resolver.feature-unification = "workspace"`: corrosion runs one `cargo rustc` per package, and cargo otherwise resolves features per package.
- The workspace manifest is also a root package, `_ch_rust_workspace`, with one feature per member. `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace/CMakeLists.txt` builds it with the enabled members' features before their runs, which then compile only their wrapper. Not with LTO, where each member's run does its own code generation. The wrappers are plain libraries imported with `OVERRIDE_CRATE_TYPE <crate>=staticlib`, so the root run writes no unused archives.
- `Cargo.lock` is resolved offline from `contrib/rust_vendor` (no `rust_vendor` change); delta-kernel-rs and chdig take the workspace's semver-compatible versions.
- The `aws-lc-sys` `LDFLAGS` workaround goes: the crate left the graph.
- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` moves to the merge commit of ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#22: the pin of #130062 plus `crate-type = ["lib"]`.

Rust-only cold build, `-j48`: Debug 200 s / 1027 s CPU on master, 108 s / 779 s here. With ThinLTO 13.2 min on master, 18.4 min here: the members' LTO runs queue on the one target directory.

Validation, x86_64 Debug:
- 1240 compile units in 3 target directories before, 799 in one after, no crate built with two feature sets.
- Build and link pass; a no-op build compiles nothing, also alternating between members; the member archives are the same cargo units as without the root package.
- Delta Lake stateless tests 77/77; prql, pco, polyglot, vortex and wasm tests 98/99 (the other fails on master too); `chdig --help` works.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comment.body:
Done in 11f1c0bf81cceab19c601128b601b899a88cbfe3: the root package `_ch_rust_workspace` is built through corrosion with the features of the enabled members and the same environment (`clickhouse_config_crate_env`, which now also sets `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`), before the run of every member.

Rust-only cold build, x86_64 Debug, `-j48`, cargo targets only, same host:
- master: 200 s wall, 1027 s CPU
- previous commit: 265 s, 797 s
- this commit: 108 s, 779 s; each member's run compiles one unit, its wrapper

Two differences from your prototype, both measured:
- The wrappers are plain libraries, imported with `OVERRIDE_CRATE_TYPE <crate>=staticlib`. With `["staticlib", "lib"]`, cargo also writes each wrapper's staticlib when it is a dependency of the root package: eight unused archives, 3.0 GiB in Debug.
- The root package's `src/lib.rs` refers to none of its dependencies, so rustc links none of them into its archive: 21 MiB instead of 2.4 GiB in Debug, which corrosion also copies into the build directory.

With LTO (`release-thinlto`, used by amd_release and arm_release) the root run does not help: each member's run does the code generation of its whole graph itself and recompiled 339 of the units the root run had built. That was 19.3 min with 45% more CPU, against 18.4 min without it, so the root package is skipped there. This profile stays slower than master (13.2 min): delta-kernel-rs and chdig no longer run their LTO in their own target directories, in parallel with the others. I have not tried to change that in this PR.

The Rust integration guide and the `update-contrib` skill now list the root package's feature and dependency for a new member.

issue.title: Faster builds: no-op rebuild 21 s → 1.4 s, header edits up to −72%, clean build −21% (10 build-system, include and PCH patches)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Build system (CMake, compilation, platform builds).

issue.body:
### Describe the situation

Small edits rebuild far more than they need: each ClickHouse build reruns cargo and rewrites the Rust archives, so clickhouse relinks, and settings files and core headers pull thousands of files into the rebuild. These patches remove most of that work; precompiled headers speed up clean builds.

Median seconds from an edit (or empty tree) to a linked clickhouse, RelWithDebInfo: master + patch 1 vs patches 1–9, 2–3 interleaved pairs.

| Scenario | x86, 32 vCPU: before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] | ARM, 16 vCPU: before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| No-op rebuild | 20.8 → 1.36 | **−93.4%** [−93.5%, −93.4%] | 23.5 → 1.76 | **−92.5%** [−93.1%, −92.0%] |
| Edit a leaf `.cpp` (getClusterName.cpp) | 23.5 → 11.8 | **−49.8%** [−52.2%, −48.6%] | 27.9* → 15.6 | **−44.1%** [−73.0%, −13.1%] |
| Edit `Settings.cpp` | 53.9 → 26.6 | **−50.7%** [−51.9%, −49.3%] | 71.0 → 34.6 | **−51.2%** [−51.8%, −50.8%] |
| Edit `ServerSettings.cpp` | 47.7 → 33.9 | **−28.9%** [−30.1%, −27.3%] | 60.2 → 44.5 | **−26.1%** [−29.2%, −24.5%] |
| Edit `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` | 39.9 → 19.6 | **−51.0%** [−52.4%, −48.9%] | 51.3 → 24.9 | **−51.5%** [−56.4%, −44.9%] |
| CMake re-run (touch `CMakeLists.txt`) | 34.1 → 9.60 | **−71.8%** [−76.8%, −68.2%] | 47.5* → 11.8 | **−75.2%** [−92.6%, −45.6%] |
| Edit `ProtocolDefines.h` | 311 → 155 | **−50.2%** [−51.0%, −49.3%] | 441 → 203 | **−53.9%** [−59.4%, −47.7%] |
| Edit `FormatSettings.h` | 1,546 → 440 | **−71.5%** [−71.5%, −71.5%] | 2,290 → 631 | **−72.4%** [−78.5%, −64.6%] |
| Edit `ISerialization.h` | 1,543 → 1,142 | **−26.0%** [−26.3%, −25.7%] | 2,324 → 1,678 | **−27.8%** [−33.1%, −22.1%] |
| New build directory, warm ccache | 437 → 275 | **−37.2%** [−41.3%, −32.7%] | 564 → 443 | **−21.5%** [−43.2%, +8.4%] |
| Clean build, empty ccache | 3,104 → 2,446 | **−21.2%** [−21.8%, −20.6%] | 4,641 → 3,689 | **−20.5%** [−25.5%, −15.2%] |

Before: master with patch 1, the link fix that master needed to link in these builds; after: all default-build patches (1–9). Change is the ratio of the medians; brackets give the 95% interval of the paired geometric-mean ratio. * On ARM the first master run after an idle period was slow (cold page cache: 42.3 s for the leaf edit, 93.0 s for the CMake re-run); the medians use all runs. Costs of the precompiled headers (patch 9) alone: a CMake re-run takes about 1 s longer (x86 8.6 → 9.5 s; ARM 10.8 → 12.2 s) and a new build directory with a warm ccache 4% longer on x86 (264.6 → 274.7 s; no measurable change on ARM), and 0.9 GB of PCH files in the build directory; with all patches applied no scenario got slower. Patch 10 adds an opt-in `-DSPLIT_DWARF=ON` (default off): on x86 a leaf edit took 13.0 → 10.1 s (−22%) and a `Settings.cpp` edit 43.4 → 40.1 s (−8%) compared with the same tree without it; split builds keep file and line in stack traces but show no inlined frames in-process (`addressToLineWithInlines` gave 45 frames for 45 stack addresses, against 118 in a default build).

<details><summary>What each patch changes, per-patch measurements and checks</summary>

1. **Link fix.** In our default RelWithDebInfo builds with clang/lld 21.1.8, master's `clickhouse` failed to link: `localize_rust_c_symbols.sh` rewrites the Rust archives with `llvm-objcopy` (`llvm-objcopy-21`, the `CMAKE_OBJCOPY` of these builds), which leaves `.llvm_addrsig` sections with `sh_link=0` in the objects where it localizes a symbol; lld's `--icf=safe` warns about them and `--fatal-warnings` fails the link. #126478 alone does not fix these builds: it makes CMake pass the LLVM objcopy instead of GNU objcopy, and these builds already used it. With `-Wl,--no-fatal-warnings` in the linker flags the link succeeds; we did not try CI's toolchain. The patch removes `.llvm_addrsig` there, as `strip_rust_symbols.sh` does since #122904; this works with GNU objcopy too. Patch 1 is a link fix that both measured trees contain; it is not measured on its own.
2. **Build system and settings.** Today every build runs the cargo builds and rewrites the copied Rust archives in place (`localize_rust_c_symbols.sh`, `strip_rust_symbols.sh`), so the copy never matches cargo's output, is rewritten again and `clickhouse` relinks even when nothing changed; every library linking a crate also waits for all cargo builds before compiling anything. The patch (a) runs each post-processing step as a custom command that writes a new archive only when its input changed (the approach of #119121); (b) builds the workspace crates with one `cargo build`, so they no longer wait for each other on cargo's target-directory lock, and skips cargo when no input of the Rust libraries changed (`cmake/cargo_if_changed.sh`, which checks cargo's dep-info files and falls back to running cargo); (c) links the crates through imported targets without the cargo dependency, so C++ compiles run in parallel with cargo and only the sources including `delta_kernel_ffi.hpp` wait for the delta-kernel build; (d) on a CMake re-run, rewrites configure-time generated files only when their content changes, lists licenses without a fork per vendored crate and keeps `git status` out of submodule work trees; (e) for the settings files, replaces per-setting template code with table-driven accessors in `BaseSettings.h` and shared field operations, includes `FormatFactorySettings.h` only where it is used and moves the disk checks of `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` to `MergeTreeSettingsDisks.cpp` (no more `MergeTreeData.h`, `ZooKeeper.h`, `ASTFunction.h`). Measured separately on x86, part (a) alone took the no-op rebuild from 21.1 to 4.4 s and the rest of the build-system changes to 1.3 s; part (e) alone took a `Settings.cpp` edit from 42.8 to 28.2 s. One `cargo build` for all workspace crates unifies the features of the dependencies they share, as `cargo build --workspace` does, so the linked Rust code changes slightly: on an earlier master this change alone made the binary 0.3 MB smaller, while the 136 exported Rust FFI symbols and the outputs of PRQL, polyglot, PCO and Vortex smoke queries stayed identical; skim and wasmtime were linked but not run.
3. **ProtocolDefines.h and friends.** The parallel-replicas protocol versions move to `ParallelReplicasProtocolDefines.h`, so `RequestResponse.h` (and everything including it) no longer depends on `ProtocolDefines.h`; `FileCachePolicy` moves to `Core/FileCachePolicy.h`, so `FileCache_fwd.h` no longer includes `SettingsEnums.h`; `ActionsDAG.h` and `IQueryPlanStep.h` are replaced by forward declarations where one suffices. A `ProtocolDefines.h` edit recompiles 115 files instead of 278.
4. **Direct includes.** 87 files that used `FormatSettings` (and a few other headers) through transitive includes include them directly. Patch 4 only adds the direct includes that patch 5 needs; it is not measured on its own.
5. **FormatSettings.h out of common headers.** `ReadHelpers.h`, `WriteHelpers.h`, `FormatFactorySettings.h`, `SettingsEnums.h` and `Context.h` included the whole `FormatSettings.h`. The CSV/JSON enums they need move to `FormatSettingsEnums.h` and the JSON number writers to `writeJSONNumber.h`/`WriteHelpers.cpp`: a `FormatSettings.h` edit recompiles 1,203 files instead of 3,222.
6. **FormatSettings.h out of the remaining wide headers.** `NativeWriter.h`, `DateTimeTransforms.h`, `FunctionBinaryArithmetic.h`, `convertFieldToType.h`, `convertColumnToType.h`, `VirtualColumnUtils.h` and a few others stop including it: 708 files instead of 1,203.
7. **Operators.h and IDataType.h.** `IO/Operators.h` no longer includes `IO/ReadHelpers.h` (a `ReadHelpers.h` edit: 1,338 files instead of 2,002, 1,147 → 933 s (−19%) when measured alone), and `IDataType.h` no longer includes `ISerialization.h`; the substream types it needs move to `SerializationSubstream.h` (an `ISerialization.h` edit: 2,286 files instead of 3,218, 1,516 → 1,267 s (−16%) alone).
8. **Unit-test include.** One unit test used `ISerialization.h` through `IDataType.h`. Patch 8 only adds an include to one unit test; it is not measured on its own.
9. **Precompiled headers.** `cmake/precompiled_headers.cmake` adds per-target PCHs of stable standard-library, fmt, magic_enum, `base/` and third-party headers to the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries, with `-fno-pch-timestamp` so ccache still hits in a new build directory. Earlier attempts found little gain: #9162 (2020) measured a clean build of 74 minutes with PCH against 76 without, and the `dbms`-only PCH listed in #96721 saved 5.9 s, about 3% of CPU time, at 192 cores. Patch 9 covers far more of the build, including the contrib sources that mostly parse their library headers: on these 16-core hosts it cut clean-build CPU time by 19% (x86) and 18% (ARM) and wall time by 18.8% and 17.5%, with the same `.text` size. Compiler caches stay correct: after a change of only the PCH content, sccache 0.19, chcache and ccache 4.9.1 all missed, because the headers inside the PCH are part of what each cache hashes; ccache gets the `pch_defines,time_macros` sloppiness it needs only for the targets with a PCH. We did not measure CI builds with sccache, where every fresh build directory builds the PCHs again.
10. **Opt-in SPLIT_DWARF.** A `SPLIT_DWARF` CMake option (`-gsplit-dwarf -gno-gnu-pubnames`) keeps most debug information out of the objects the linker reads. `Dwarf.cpp` accepts the skeleton units (`DW_TAG_skeleton_unit`) so stack traces keep file and line, and one test that reads the binary's DWARF is skipped in split builds, as it is for `-g0`.

Each patch measured on its own on x86 (interleaved pairs; "before" is the tree with the earlier patches, for patch 10 the same tree built without the option; IDs name host, patch and scenario):

| Patch | Scenario ID | Before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] | Pairs |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| 2 | x86-BS3-noop | 20.6 → 1.34 | **−93.5%** [−93.8%, −93.2%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-leaf | 23.7 → 13.1 | **−44.8%** [−46.3%, −41.7%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-serversettings | 48.1 → 34.3 | **−28.6%** [−32.3%, −24.2%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-settings | 54.8 → 27.4 | **−50.0%** [−52.4%, −46.6%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-mtsettings | 39.9 → 21.4 | **−46.4%** [−48.2%, −43.9%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-cmake | 34.0 → 8.61 | **−74.7%** [−75.2%, −74.1%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-warmfresh | 443 → 266 | **−40.0%** [−48.0%, −30.9%] | 2 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-formatfactorysettings | 197 → 105 | **−46.5%** [−54.2%, −37.6%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-protocoldefines | 300 → 163 | **−45.7%** [−47.5%, −43.9%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-settingsenums | 1,079 → 772 | **−28.4%** [−29.7%, −27.2%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-actionsdag | 799 → 711 | **−11.0%** [−19.8%, −1.2%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-iqueryplanstep | 490 → 292 | **−40.3%** [−42.4%, −38.3%] | 2 |
| 5 | x86-FSb-formatsettings | 1,517 → 797 | **−47.4%** [−48.2%, −46.7%] | 2 |
| 6 | x86-H4-formatsettings | 797 → 478 | **−40.0%** [−43.9%, −35.8%] | 2 |
| 7 | x86-H56-readhelpers | 1,147 → 931 | **−18.8%** [−19.7%, −17.9%] | 2 |
| 7 | x86-H56-iserialization | 1,518 → 1,265 | **−16.7%** [−18.3%, −15.1%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-clean | 3,012 → 2,446 | **−18.8%** [−19.3%, −18.2%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-warmfresh | 265 → 275 | **+3.8%** [−6.2%, +14.9%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-leaf | 12.8 → 11.9 | **−7.1%** [−11.0%, −3.0%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-settings | 27.1 → 26.3 | **−3.0%** [−9.7%, +4.1%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-cmake | 8.56 → 9.53 | **+11.3%** [+4.1%, +19.0%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-formatsettings | 477 → 441 | **−7.5%** [−11.4%, −3.4%] | 2 |
| 10 | x86-U6-leaf | 13.0 → 10.1 | **−22.4%** [−28.0%, −17.2%] | 3 |
| 10 | x86-U6-settings | 43.4 → 40.1 | **−7.5%** [−10.7%, −5.6%] | 3 |

Checks: master and patched binaries return identical `system.settings`, `system.server_settings`, `system.merge_tree_settings`, `system.licenses`, `system.formats`, `system.functions` and `system.table_engines`, sample values and Native output on both hosts; `system.build_options` differs only in the git fields. `unit_tests_dbms` passes with all patches on both hosts (x86: 30,289 tests, 25,497 passed, the rest skipped, none failed; ARM: 30,265 tests, 25,469 passed, 4,796 skipped, none failed, the same counts as master). Clean, new-directory and incremental builds all succeeded, every incremental scenario recompiled the edited file and relinked, and each binary answered a query. The binaries are not byte-identical: the header cuts move code between translation units, the single cargo build of patch 2 unifies Rust dependency features (see patch 2), and the PCHs change debug type information (with and without patch 9: same `.text`, `.rodata` and `.data` sizes on x86 and same `.text` size on ARM; `.debug_info` 3.6% (x86) and 3.8% (ARM) smaller from fewer duplicated type entries; equivalent symbolization of 3,000 sampled functions on ARM). On ARM, Time/DateTime conversions, uniqExact and general queries ran at the same speed with and without the patches (within ±0.7%, except a +1.8% uniqExact difference of the size that rebuilding identical sources also produces).

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?

<details><summary>Tested versions and source commits</summary>

Measured on master 64576f956c6b (2026-11-03) with the patches applied in order. A three-way merge of the patches onto master 46ab3dad27eb (2026-11-07) conflicts only in `FormatSettings.h` and `ActionsDAG.cpp`, next to edited lines. Since the base, upstream changed only other lines of the build files these patches edit (source lists in `src/CMakeLists.txt`, OSS-Fuzz options in `CMakeLists.txt`), not the Rust, cargo, license or PCH steps. We did not rebuild on the newer master: new code that relies on an include these patches remove would need a direct include, as in patch 4.

</details>

### How to reproduce

<details><summary>Hosts, configuration and measurement procedure</summary>

- Hosts: x86, AWS r6i.8xlarge (16 cores / 32 vCPU, 247 GiB); ARM, AWS r7g.4xlarge (16 vCPU Graviton3, 123 GiB); Ubuntu 24.04.
- Toolchain: clang/lld 21.1.8 from apt.llvm.org, CMake 3.28.3, Ninja 1.11.1, ccache 4.9.1, Rust nightly-2026-03-22 as pinned by `contrib/corrosion-cmake`.
- Configuration (both arms): `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-21 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-21`, then `ninja -C build clickhouse` (default parallelism, ccache through `COMPILER_CACHE=auto`). Patch 10 is measured with `-DSPLIT_DWARF=ON` against the same tree without it.
- Trees: one source checkout and one `CCACHE_DIR` per arm, never shared. Before each incremental run the tree is synced with two no-op `ninja` runs.
- Scenarios, each timed from the edit to the finished `clickhouse` binary:
  - no-op: `ninja` on the synced tree;
  - leaf, `Settings.cpp`, `ServerSettings.cpp`, `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` and header edits: append a unique comment line to the file, `ninja`, then restore the file (the next sync rebuilds it);
  - CMake re-run: `touch CMakeLists.txt`, `ninja`;
  - new build directory with warm ccache: delete the build directory, `cmake` + `ninja`;
  - clean build: delete the build directory and the arm's ccache directory, `cmake` + `ninja`.
- Order: arms interleaved per scenario (A,B,B,A or A,B,B,A,A,B), 2 pairs for scenarios over 5 minutes, 3 for the others; the table shows medians and the 95% interval of the paired geometric ratio. The arm for patch 9 alone (all patches except 9 vs all patches) was interleaved with the same runs on x86.
- Patch application: 1 → 9 in order on master 64576f956c6b; patch 10 applies on top.

</details>

### Expected performance

<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A rebuild should cost about as much as the change: no cargo run, archive rewrite or relink when no Rust input and no object changed; after a header edit, recompiling only the files that use the header; after a CMake re-run with no real change, no regenerated file that forces recompiles. Clean builds should not parse the same large third-party headers in every translation unit.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests

<details><summary>Related work</summary>

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/96721 collects build-speed work. Patches 3 and 5–7 cut transitive header dependencies so that a header edit recompiles fewer files, which Algunenano suggested there for local development; patch 9 extends the `dbms`-only PCH commit listed there (not merged) to per-target PCHs for the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/9162 (2020, closed) tried CMake's precompiled headers and measured a clean build of 74 minutes with them against 76 without; the description of patch 9 says what differs here.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122904 removed `.llvm_addrsig` in `strip_rust_symbols.sh`; patch 1 does the same in `localize_rust_c_symbols.sh`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126478 (open) fixes the same link error where CMake picks GNU objcopy, by passing the LLVM objcopy instead; patch 1 removes the section, so it also fixes builds like ours that already use `llvm-objcopy-21`, and the two changes do not conflict.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/124645 took the cargo builds out of Ninja's console pool; as it notes, the workspace crates still wait for each other on cargo's target-directory lock, which patch 2(b) removes by building them with one `cargo build`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/119121 by @al13n321 made the Rust archive post-processing incremental; it was closed without merging on 2026-10-29. Patch 2 contains that approach (part (a)), and our earlier measurements are in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/119121#issuecomment-6440742891.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128815 (open) also changes `contrib/corrosion-cmake/CMakeLists.txt`: if it lands first, the single `cargo build` environment of patch 2 needs the same target-scoped `RUSTFLAGS`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129767 and https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110548 (open), and draft https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129961, add workspace crates. Their own steps rewrite Corrosion's copy of the archive in place: `strip_rust_symbols.sh`, and in #110548 also a localization of the lz4 and zstd symbols. With patch 2 the binaries link the post-processed archive of the single `cargo build` instead, so those steps would process a copy that is no longer linked. Whichever change lands second must turn them into `clickhouse_postprocess_rust_lib()` calls, as patch 2 does for prql, polyglot, pco and vortex.

</details>

### Additional context

<details><summary>Patches</summary>

Apply patches 1 to 9 in this order on master 64576f956c6b; patch 10 is optional and applies on top. Patches 1, 8, 9 and 10 are below; patches 2 to 7 follow in five comments because of GitHub's size limit (comment 1: patch 2; comment 2: patches 3 and 4; comment 3: patch 5; comment 4: patch 6; comment 5: patch 7).

@groeneai could you take a look? If the analysis and patch hold up, feel free to open a PR if it fits.

**Patch 1: link fix for the localized Rust archives**

```diff
diff --git a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
index 61cf95aa9c8..4ef48524c02 100755
--- a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
+++ b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
@@ -125,12 +125,15 @@ if [ -s "$LOCALIZE_FILE" ]; then
     # Some Rust archives contain non-ELF members (e.g. debug metadata objects)
     # that cause llvm-objcopy to fail.  In that case, fall back to extracting
     # individual members, processing only valid ELF objects, and repacking.
-    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
+    # Also drop .llvm_addrsig: objcopy leaves its sh_link at 0, and lld --icf=safe then warns that it ignores it
+    # (an error with --fatal-warnings). Without the table lld treats these objects conservatively, as it does
+    # when it ignores the table. See strip_rust_symbols.sh.
+    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
         WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
 
         (cd "$WORK_DIR" && "$AR" x "$LIB_PATH")
         for obj in "$WORK_DIR"/*.o; do
-            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
+            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
         done
         "$AR" rcs "$LIB_PATH" "$WORK_DIR"/*.o
     fi
```

**Patch 8: unit-test include**

```diff
diff --git a/src/DataTypes/Serializations/tests/gtest_low_cardinality_serialization.cpp b/src/DataTypes/Serializations/tests/gtest_low_cardinality_serialization.cpp
index 9aa26ad5cd9..32d058da52e 100644

+function (clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers target)
+    cmake_parse_arguments (PCH "SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES" "REUSE_FROM" "HEADERS" ${ARGN})
+    if (PCH_REUSE_FROM)

+    set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES PCH_INSTANTIATE_TEMPLATES OFF)

+    get_target_property (binary_dir ${target} BINARY_DIR)

+        else ()
+            set (path "${binary_dir}/${source}")

+        if (PCH_SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES)

+                break ()
+            endif ()
+        endforeach ()
+    endforeach ()
+
+    get_target_property (launcher ${target} CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER)
+    list (FILTER launcher INCLUDE REGEX "(^|/)ccache$")
+    if (launcher)
+        execute_process (COMMAND ${launcher} --get-config sloppiness
+            OUTPUT_VARIABLE sloppiness OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE ERROR_QUIET RESULT_VARIABLE rc)
+        if (NOT rc EQUAL 0)
+            set (sloppiness "")
+        endif ()
+        string (REPLACE " " "" sloppiness "${sloppiness},pch_defines,time_macros")
+        string (REGEX REPLACE "^," "" sloppiness "${sloppiness}")
+        get_target_property (launcher ${target} CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER)
+        set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER "env;CCACHE_SLOPPINESS=${sloppiness};${launcher}")
+    endif ()
+endfunction ()
+
+function (clickhouse_add_precompiled_headers)
+    if (NOT ENABLE_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS)
+        return ()
+    endif ()
+
+    foreach (target IN LISTS CLICKHOUSE_PCH_TARGETS)
+        if (TARGET ${target})
+            clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_PCH_HEADERS})
+        endif ()
+    endforeach ()
+
+    if (NOT ENABLE_CONTRIB_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS)
+        return ()
+    endif ()
+
+    if (TARGET _aws)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_aws SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__aws})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET grpc)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (grpc SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_grpc})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _rocksdb)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_rocksdb SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__rocksdb})
+    endif ()
+    # The LLVM libraries share their compile flags, so they share one PCH, built by LLVMCore. The libraries below the IR
+    # (and two YAML/DWARF readers) declare their own Argument, Value, Type, CallingConv or isDigit, which clash with the
+    # IR headers of that PCH, so they are compiled as before.
+    set (llvm_pch_exclude LLVMDemangle LLVMSupport LLVMBinaryFormat LLVMRemarks LLVMBitstreamReader LLVMTextAPI
+        LLVMTargetParser LLVMObjectYAML LLVMDebugInfoDWARF LLVMDebugInfoDWARFLowLevel)
+    if (TARGET LLVMCore)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (LLVMCore SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_LLVM})
+        get_property (llvm_targets DIRECTORY "${ClickHouse_SOURCE_DIR}/contrib/llvm-project-cmake" PROPERTY BUILDSYSTEM_TARGETS)
+        foreach (target IN LISTS llvm_targets)
+            get_target_property (type ${target} TYPE)
+            if (target MATCHES "^LLVM" AND type STREQUAL "STATIC_LIBRARY" AND NOT target STREQUAL "LLVMCore"
+                AND NOT target IN_LIST llvm_pch_exclude)
+                clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES REUSE_FROM LLVMCore)
+            endif ()
+        endforeach ()
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _mongocxx)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_mongocxx SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__mongocxx})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _xgboost)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_xgboost SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__xgboost})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _arrow)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_arrow SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__arrow})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _libprotoc)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_libprotoc SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__libprotoc})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _vectorscan)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_vectorscan SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__vectorscan})
+    endif ()
+    foreach (target IN LISTS CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_TARGETS)
+        if (TARGET ${target})
+            clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_${target}})
+        endif ()
+    endforeach ()
+endfunction ()
```

+# Keep most debug info out of every link: each object file writes its DWARF to a .dwo file next to it
+# (-gsplit-dwarf), and only skeleton units, line tables and address ranges reach the binary. Links of
+# builds with debug info get much faster and the binary much smaller, but debuggers read the .dwo files
+# from the build directory (resolved against DW_AT_comp_dir), the in-process symbolizer cannot show
+# inlined frames, and the DWARF input format sees only the skeleton units. For local development builds only.
+option (SPLIT_DWARF "Write DWARF debug info to .dwo files in the build directory instead of the binary (-gsplit-dwarf), for faster development links" OFF)

comment.body:
@qoega, one decision for the Parser and Storage memory checks. They are the only CI users of `clickhouse-examples`, which only the `Build (arm_release)` job links.

**Why.** ThinLTO builds run 2 link jobs at a time. In the PR `Build (arm_release)` job the keeper and `clickhouse-examples` links start first, and the `clickhouse` link, the longest, waits for the keeper link. In 12 PR jobs on 2026-11-09 the links ended at a median of 535 s (keeper), 858 s (examples) and 1,433 s (`clickhouse`) after the last library. `Performance Comparison (arm_release, ...)` and the other PR jobs that test the ARM release binary start after this build.

**Change** (one small CMake PR): link `clickhouse-examples` after the keeper, so `clickhouse` gets the second link job at once, and with `-Wl,--lto-O0` (no optimization in its ThinLTO backends). Link phase measured locally with the CI link commands (x86, `-g0`, 32 cores, 2 link jobs):

| Links | Link phase (runs) |
|---|---:|
| as today | 1,312 s, 1,218 s |
| examples after the keeper | 1,297 s, 1,204 s (-1%) |
| examples after the keeper, `--lto-O0` | 817 s (-35%) |
| `--lto-O0` only | 1,074 s (-15%) |

On the CI timings above this is about 510 s (8.5 min) less for the PR `arm_release` build, an estimate (not measured on Graviton). The order alone is worth about 1%, so I do not propose it without `--lto-O0`.

**What it changes for the checks:** on PR and master they would profile a `clickhouse-examples` built without link-time optimization; PRs built before the first master build with the change compare a PR `--lto-O0` binary with an optimized master one. I ran both checks' own code and thresholds on both kinds of binary from current master:
- Parser: per-query allocations of the `--lto-O0` binary are byte-identical on all 100 queries.
- Storage: per-scenario differences of -184..+64 B, inside the spread of two runs of the same binary (-240..+72 B); the threshold is 1,024 B.
- 0 regressions, improvements or errors in every pair, including master optimized vs PR `--lto-O0`.
- Both checks finish sooner: profiling takes 11-16% longer, symbolization is 4-5 times faster.

Measured on x86 with `-g0`, not on aarch64 and not against master's `-g` build. The allocation difference given for this change in the [2026-11-09 summary](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130064#issuecomment-6753360734) (+1.06% median) did not reproduce on current master.

Should the checks use a `--lto-O0` `clickhouse-examples`? (a) yes, I open the PR; (b) no, I leave the build as it is.

issue.title: Refreshable materialized view in a Replicated database fails to load if Keeper is unreachable at startup; the failed load job is never retried, and the database's DDL and the DDL worker stay broken until a restart

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Confirmed user-visible misbehaviour in official release

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Refreshable materialized views: scheduled/periodic refresh, refresh state machine, refresh orches...

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
### Company or project name

Halter https://github.com/halter-corp

### Describe what's wrong

If the server starts while Keeper is not reachable yet, attaching a refreshable materialized view in a `Replicated` database fails (`Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes`). The failed load job is never retried after Keeper becomes reachable. The jobs that depend on it stay `CANCELED`: `startup table` of the view, `startup ddl worker`, and on 25.8 also the view's target table.

As a result, until the server is restarted:

- DDL in that database waits 300 s and fails with `Cannot enqueue query on this replica, most likely because replica is busy with previous queue entries. (UNFINISHED)`;
- `SELECT` from the view's target table fails with `Waited job failed` (25.8.33; works on 26.10.3.7);
- in a cluster, `ON CLUSTER` queries time out on the other replicas with `is not finished on 1 of 2 hosts (0 of them are currently executing the task, 0 are inactive)`.

The server itself stays up and answers other queries, so health checks keep passing. A restart (with Keeper reachable) fixes it.

We hit this in production on Kubernetes when an upgrade restarted ClickHouse and Keeper pods at the same time: one replica started in the same second as the first Keeper pod, before Keeper had a quorum, and stayed in this state for about 2.5 hours until we restarted it.

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes. Same result on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.10.3.7` with `clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper:26.10.3.7` (the `latest` images), with one difference: `SELECT` from the view's target table works there, because the target table is no longer cancelled with the view. The view, `startup ddl worker` and DDL in the database stay broken until a restart. On 26.10 the load error reads `Cannot resolve any of provided ZooKeeper hosts due to DNS error` (the stopped Keeper container's name does not resolve), on 25.8 `Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes`.

### How to reproduce

Versions: `altinity/clickhouse-server:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable` with `altinity/clickhouse-keeper:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable` and `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.10.3.7` with `clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper:26.10.3.7`. One server, one Keeper, default settings.

`keeper_config.xml` (copied to `/etc/clickhouse-keeper/keeper_config.xml`):

```xml
<clickhouse>
  <listen_host>0.0.0.0</listen_host>
  <keeper_server>
    <tcp_port>9181</tcp_port><server_id>1</server_id>
    <log_storage_path>/var/lib/clickhouse-keeper/log</log_storage_path>
    <snapshot_storage_path>/var/lib/clickhouse-keeper/snapshots</snapshot_storage_path>
    <raft_configuration><server><id>1</id><hostname>keeper</hostname><port>9234</port></server></raft_configuration>
  </keeper_server>
</clickhouse>
```

`server.xml` (copied to `/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/server.xml`):

```xml
<clickhouse>
  <zookeeper><node><host>keeper</host><port>9181</port></node></zookeeper>
  <macros><shard>01</shard><replica>r1</replica></macros>
</clickhouse>
```

Steps:

```sh
docker network create repro
docker create --name keeper --network repro --network-alias keeper altinity/clickhouse-keeper:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable
docker cp keeper_config.xml keeper:/etc/clickhouse-keeper/keeper_config.xml
docker create --name server --network repro altinity/clickhouse-server:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable
docker cp server.xml server:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/server.xml
docker start keeper server
```

```sql
CREATE DATABASE db ENGINE = Replicated('/clickhouse/databases/db', '{shard}', '{replica}');
CREATE TABLE db.target (id UInt64, v UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree(v) ORDER BY id;
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW db.mv REFRESH EVERY 1 HOUR APPEND TO db.target AS
    SELECT number AS id, 1 AS v FROM numbers(10);
```

Restart the server while Keeper is down, then bring Keeper back:

```sh
docker stop server keeper
docker start server     # Keeper is still down
sleep 20
docker start keeper     # Keeper reachable again
sleep 30
```

```sql
SELECT job, status, exception FROM system.asynchronous_loader WHERE status != 'OK';
SELECT count() FROM db.target;
CREATE TABLE db.after_keeper (id UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree ORDER BY id;
```

### Expected behavior

Once Keeper is reachable, the view is attached (the load job is retried), or at least the database and the DDL worker recover without a server restart.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

`system.asynchronous_loader`, 30 s after Keeper is back (unchanged later):

```
load table db.mv        FAILED    Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table db.mv' failed: Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes: Cannot attach table `db`.`mv` from metadata file store/…
startup ddl worker      CANCELED  Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup ddl worker' -> Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table db.mv' failed: …
startup table db.mv     CANCELED  Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.mv' -> Code: 695. …
startup table db.target CANCELED  Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.target' -> Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.mv' -> …
```

DDL in the database (after 300 s):

```
Code: 341. DB::Exception: Timeout: Cannot enqueue query on this replica, most likely because replica is busy with previous queue entries. (UNFINISHED)
```

`SELECT count() FROM db.target` (25.8.33 only; works on 26.10.3.7):

```
Code: 722. DB::Exception: Waited job failed: Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.target' -> Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.mv' -> Code: 695. …
```

In the two-replica production cluster, the affected replica logged every few seconds:

```
<Error> DDLWorker(<db>): Error on initialization of <db>: Code: 722. DB::Exception: Waited job failed: Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table <db>.<target>' -> Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table <db>.<mv>' -> Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table <db>.<mv>' failed: Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes: Cannot attach table …
```

and `ON CLUSTER` DDL from the other replica failed with `Code: 159 … is not finished on 1 of 2 hosts (0 of them are currently executing the task, 0 are inactive)`.

After a server restart (Keeper reachable): no failed load jobs, `SELECT` returns 10, DDL succeeds.

### Additional context

Possibly related, but with different causes: #89693 (`There is no a local address in host list` on a fresh pod), #124717, #126745.

comment.body:
The fix is small: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130611

The `RefreshTask` constructor of a coordinated view (`APPEND`, or any view in a `Replicated` database) connected to Keeper on `ATTACH` with no fallback, so a connection error failed the `load table` job, which the async loader does not retry. With the PR, on `ATTACH` a Keeper connection error defers the view's znode setup to the refresh scheduler, which already retries Keeper errors every 5 s, so the view attaches while Keeper is down and sets up its coordination once Keeper is reachable. `CREATE` and `RESTORE` are unchanged. I reproduced it on 26.8.34.13 and 26.10.2.103, and the PR adds an integration test that stops Keeper, restarts the server and checks that the views attach, refresh once Keeper is back, and that DDL in the database works.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The `Vortex` format page now documents that `String` columns are written as `Utf8` and the `output_format_vortex_string_as_string` setting. The `Vortex` and `SQLite` format pages are now regenerated from the source by the nightly docs job.


### Description

The `Vortex` format page still says that `String` columns are written as `Binary` and has no `output_format_vortex_string_as_string` row, although master writes `Utf8` since #130234 and throws on a value that is not valid UTF-8. The AI review on #130423 flagged it (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130423#discussion_r4522296444).

Root cause: `format_generators` in `ci/jobs/scripts/docs/autogenerate/autogenerate_docs.py` finds format pages only through the matched rows of `docs/_migration/slug-map.csv`. `reference/formats/Vortex.mdx` and `reference/formats/SQLite.mdx` had no row, so the nightly job skipped both pages without any error (`--only format:Vortex` reported "matched no generator"). The source registrations were already correct.

Change: two rows in the shape of the Puffin rows (#115375), and both pages regenerated with `autogenerate_docs.py --write --only format:Vortex` / `--only format:SQLite`. The `SQLite` page change is the generator rewriting one link to the current database engine path.

Validation: `--check --only format:` over all format pages reports drift for exactly these two pages after adding the rows, and none after `--write`. Internal links and anchors check clean.

This PR changes generated regions, so the Docs check needs the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label.

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128014
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed a hang of queries over `Executable` and `ExecutablePool` tables and the `executable` table function with `check_exit_code = 1` that stop reading the command's output early, for example with `LIMIT`. Such a query never returned and was not stopped by `max_execution_time`. The exit code is now checked only when the output is read to the end.

### Description
On 26.3 and 26.10, `SELECT x FROM t LIMIT 1` over an `Executable` table with `check_exit_code = 1` whose command writes more than the query reads (e.g. `exec yes 1`) never returns, and `max_execution_time` does not stop it; with `check_exit_code = 0` it returns at once. The same happens with `ExecutablePool` when a reply arrives in several chunks, and with the `executable` table function.

`ShellCommandSource::prepare` waited for the command on every `Status::Finished`, but `ISource::prepare` also returns `Finished` when the downstream finished the port (`LIMIT`) or the query was cancelled. The command then cannot exit: a plain command is blocked writing to a pipe nobody reads, a pool worker waits for its next request on a stdin that stays open, and `ShellCommand::wait` blocks in `waitpid` before it closes the pipes. Until #53631 the wait was in the end-of-output branch of `generate`.

The exit code is now checked only when the source read the output to the end. Otherwise the command is discarded and `~ShellCommand` terminates it within `command_termination_timeout`, as with `check_exit_code = 0`. So a query that stops early no longer reports a non-zero exit of the command even if it had already exited; a full read still does. Executable UDFs and dictionaries always read the output to the end, so their check is unchanged.

Validation: the new test hangs on master (both cases killed by `timeout 60`) and passes in about 1 s with the fix. The existing `executable` stateless tests and the `test_executable_table_function`, `test_executable_dictionary` and `test_executable_user_defined_function` integration tests pass.

Found while reviewing #128014 (a different defect in the same file). No issue exists for this hang.

The fix is my open #130272. issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127688
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed wrong results when the query condition cache served the entry of a filter on one column to a filter on another column whose name and type spell the same text, e.g. `WHERE a` on `a UInt8` after `WHERE aU` on `aU Int8` of the same table returned no rows.

### Description

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127688 (the same `c UInt8` / `cU Int8` class in the TopK cache key).

On 26.8 (also 26.6 and 26.7), with the default `use_query_condition_cache = 1`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (k UInt64, a UInt8, aU Int8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 100;
INSERT INTO t SELECT number, intDiv(number, 100) = 9, intDiv(number, 100) = 0 FROM numbers(1000);
SELECT count(), min(k) FROM t WHERE aU;  -- 100 0
SELECT count(), min(k) FROM t WHERE a;   -- 0 0, expected 100 900
```

`ActionsDAG::Node::updateOwnHash` hashes `result_name` and then the type name with no length, and `SipHash::update(const std::string &)` does not mix in the length, so the inputs `__table1.aU Int8` and `__table1.a UInt8` both hash the bytes `__table1.aUInt8`. Every query condition cache key (MergeTree `WHERE` and `PREWHERE`, `file()` and object storage, `Memory`) is this hash plus the table uuid and the part or file name, so `WHERE a` reads the granule verdicts of `WHERE aU`. A function node embeds its argument names, so only a bare-column filter on a pair like `x UIntN` / `xU IntN` reaches it. 26.3 rejects an `Int8` filter and is not affected.

The fix hashes every string in `Node::updateOwnHash` with its length first, and the sizes of its captured-name and lambda-argument lists, as the query tree and AST hashes already do. The hash is never persisted; in a mixed-version cluster an aggregation hash table size hint carried in a serialized plan just misses once.

Validation: the new test fails on master in 20 of 20 randomized runs and passes 50 of 50 with the fix; the `file()` Parquet case was checked locally; 189 query condition cache and automatic parallel replicas tests show no new failure; the related gtests pass.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127558

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Add the `output_format_arrow_datetime_as_timestamp` setting (disabled by default). When enabled, the `Arrow` and `ArrowStream` output formats write `DateTime` as an Arrow `TIMESTAMP` in seconds with the column's time zone, as for `DateTime64(0)`, so Arrow clients and ClickHouse read it back as a date and time instead of `UInt32`. Closes #127558.


### Description

`Arrow` and `ArrowStream` write `DateTime` as `uint32` (the documented mapping), so Arrow clients get a bare integer and ClickHouse reads the column back as `UInt32` (#127558). As suggested in the issue (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127558#issuecomment-6419149099), this adds an opt-in setting, disabled by default, so existing output does not change.

With `output_format_arrow_datetime_as_timestamp = 1`, the native Arrow IPC writer declares `DateTime` as `timestamp(SECOND, <column time zone>)` and writes the values as 64-bit integers, exactly as it already does for `DateTime64(0)`. ClickHouse reads such a column back as `DateTime64(0, tz)`. The schema and the data both come from the `DateTime` leaf cases in `SchemaConverter.cpp` and `RecordBatchEncoder.cpp`, so every nesting (`Nullable`, `Array`, `Tuple`, `Map`, `LowCardinality` dictionaries, `Variant`) follows. The `DateTime64` and `Date` cases now share the new helpers; their output is unchanged.

Arrow Flight keeps `uint32`: it uses the canonical mapping and ignores the `output_format_arrow_*` type settings by design (`arrowflight.mdx`). Parquet and ORC already write `DateTime` as a timestamp.

Validation: the new test covers the default, and with the setting on both formats, `Nullable`, `Array`, `Tuple`, `Map` keys, `LowCardinality` dictionaries, a value after 2038, explicit and default time zones. It fails on master and on four mutations (schema only, sign extension, dropped time zone, setting not plumbed). With default settings the output is byte-identical to master for `DateTime`, `DateTime64`, `Date`, `Nullable` and `LowCardinality`, in both formats. pyarrow reads the new output as `timestamp[s, tz=...]`.

issue.title: Add `max_rows` setting for databases

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with new product feature

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Allows running workflows for external contributors

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Database engine implementations (e.g., Atomic/Replicated) and database-level behavior.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109355

Adds a `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases: a ceiling on active MergeTree rows counted toward the database limit. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition-import/move operations. A batch `INSERT` may overshoot, and the next `INSERT` throws `TOO_MANY_ROWS`.

Enforcement is a best-effort snapshot check, not a reservation spanning the commit: concurrent operations may each observe free headroom and transiently overshoot the limit together; the next checked operation then fails. On replicated attach paths the limit is charged only for parts that ZooKeeper actually accepts: an `ATTACH` deduplicated by its block id stays a no-op even when the database is over the limit, and a partially duplicated `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` pays only for the accepted remainder. A multi-part `ATTACH PARTITION` is all-or-nothing: the rows of the parts ZooKeeper will accept are validated together before the first part is committed, so the command never leaves a partially attached partition behind.

The counted total is exposed through the nullable `system.databases.rows` column. It intentionally excludes engines that do not participate in `max_rows` accounting. The setting can be changed at runtime with `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING max_rows = N`; its default value, `0`, is unlimited.

### Changelog category (leave one):

- New Feature

### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

Add the `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases, limiting active MergeTree rows counted across a database. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition imports as a best-effort snapshot check, is reconfigurable via `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING`, and is exposed through `system.databases.rows`.

comment.body:
This is the abort that #126768 fixes (my PR, open, waiting for review).

`DataFileStatistics::getNullCounts` indexes `field_ids` by the position of the written block's column. On master, when a written column has no field id in the latest Iceberg schema, `fieldIdsOfWrittenColumns` returns an empty list and `DataFileStatistics` falls back to the schema's own ids, so a block wider than the latest schema reads past the end of `field_ids`. This is the stale-structure INSERT from #125361. In this run, earlier INSERTs into the same table `d15.t463` had failed with `No such column c1` and `No such column c2` before the crashing `INSERT INTO d15.t463 (c1)`.

#126768 removes that fallback: every written column must have a field id in the latest schema (the check Parquet already did, now for every format), otherwise the INSERT fails with `INCORRECT_DATA`. So `field_ids` always has one entry per block column, and this read cannot go out of bounds. Its integration test aborts the server on master for ORC and Avro after `DROP COLUMN`, and passes with the fix.

<!--

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/126735
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126829


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The `GROUP BY` top-K optimization (`enable_group_by_top_k_optimization`) now also applies when a matched `GROUP BY` key is sorted with `COLLATE`, e.g. `GROUP BY s ORDER BY s COLLATE 'en' LIMIT 10`.

### Description

The optimization was disabled for a `COLLATE` on a matched key. Now `TopKParams` owns the collators, the heap compares collated keys with `compareAtWithCollation` and keeps keys tied with the boundary, and `Aggregating` step v2 serializes each key's locale (plan version 22; older peers get no collated top-K). A collated first key gets no dynamic filter, whose per-row locale comparison would continue after the heap freezes.

A locale comparison costs more than a hash lookup, so with a collated heap the aggregation loops look a row's key up first: a known key is aggregated without a comparison, and only a new key is compared with the boundary. The serialized method of a composite key still compares first, because its key holder is costly to build twice. Otherwise a collated heap starts and freezes like any other.

Release, 32 threads, 100M `hits` rows (18.3M distinct `URL`), `COLLATE 'en' LIMIT 10`, off -> on, medians of 7 runs (measured for da9874b257c5):

| Query | off | on |
|---|---|---|
| `URL` | 895 ms | 382 ms |
| `URL`, 1 thread | 7312 ms | 5729 ms |
| `URL, b` (serialized method) | 1229 ms | 366 ms |
| 20M unique `toString(number)` | 96 ms | 24 ms |
| 1M keys in descending cycles | 67 ms | 35 ms |
| 300K keys in cycles | 66 ms | 35 ms |

CI runs the `URL`, unique and descending-cycles cases in `topk_aggregation_collate.xml`; `05407_group_by_top_k_collation` checks every case against off, also with `sum`, `uniqExact` and no aggregate functions.

-->

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130250


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed a refreshable materialized view in a `Replicated` database failing to load when the server starts while Keeper is unreachable. The failed load was never retried, so the view stayed missing and DDL in the database failed until a restart. Now the view is attached and sets up its Keeper coordination once Keeper is reachable. Closes #130250.

### Description

On 26.8.34.13 and 26.10.2.103 (official images, the reporter's repro from #130250), a server that starts while Keeper is unreachable fails the `load table` job of a coordinated refreshable view (`APPEND` in a `Replicated` database) with `Code: 999 ... Cannot resolve any of provided ZooKeeper hosts`, `startup ddl worker` stays `CANCELED`, and every DDL in the database fails with `Code: 341 ... (UNFINISHED)` until a restart.

Cause: the `RefreshTask` constructor connects to Keeper on `ATTACH` (feature-flag check, then creating this replica's coordination znodes) with no fallback, so a connection error fails the table load, and the async loader does not retry failed jobs. `ReplicatedMergeTree` and `DatabaseReplicated` already attach without Keeper, and the scheduling thread already retries Keeper errors every 5 s.

Change: on `ATTACH` only (not `CREATE` or `RESTORE`), a Keeper hardware error in that block is logged and the znode setup is deferred. The existing create code moves into `createCoordinationZnodesIfNeeded`, which `doScheduling` runs before its first znode read, after its feature-flag re-check, under its existing Keeper-error retry. With Keeper reachable nothing changes.

Validation: a new case in `test_refreshable_mv` stops all Keeper nodes, restarts the server, and checks that both views attach with no failed load jobs, refresh once Keeper is back (one of them with its znodes deleted beforehand, so the deferred create is exercised), and that DDL in the database works. It fails on master at the attach check and passes 5/5 with the fix. Removing the `doScheduling` part makes the deleted-znodes view fail with `No node`. `test_refreshable_mv`, `test_refreshable_mv_no_multi_read`, `test_refreshable_mat_view_replicated` and `test_refreshable_mv_keeper_loss` pass.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed a crash, or wrong results from a text index, after merging parts of a `MergeTree` table that has a text index and a column named `_part_index`.

### Description
On 26.3.60.2, 26.8.34.13 and 26.10.2.103, `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` on a `MergeTree` table with a text index and an ordinary column named `_part_index` crashes with SIGSEGV, and a vertical merge of such a table makes text index queries return rows of the other part (`hasToken(text, 'beta')` returns 1000 `'alpha'` rows). The schema is uncommon, but `CREATE TABLE` accepts it. No issue exists; I found it while testing text index merges.

Root cause: a merge that combines the source parts' text indexes maps each merged row to its source part by reading the virtual `_part_index` column, and a table column with that name shadows it. In a horizontal merge the name is read twice and the second copy is null. In a vertical merge the mapping is built from the user's values, which gives wrong rows, `CORRUPTED_DATA`, or an out-of-bounds write in `MergedPartOffsets::insert`.

Change: for such tables, merges rebuild the text indexes of the resulting part instead of merging them, which is the path row-reducing merges (Replacing, TTL, lightweight delete) already take. A new `rebuild_text_indexes` flag drives only the text index decisions; statistics, minmax and projections still follow `merge_may_reduce_rows`. Projections that need the same mapping already guard against such a column (#78429).

Validation: the new test `05617_text_index_merge_part_index_column` covers a horizontal and a vertical merge (`part_log` checks the algorithm). It crashes the server on the base build and passes 50/50 with randomized settings; removing the new condition makes it fail again. 150 related text index and projection tests (1 plain + 10 randomized runs) show no new failures; the only two failures fail identically on the base build.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
An `INSERT` into Google Cloud Storage with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` no longer fails when the file is larger than `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`.

### Description

On master, an `INSERT` into GCS with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` fails with `Code: 499 ... GCS conditional create of <key> must be a single PUT` as soon as the object exceeds `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`, even for the first write to a new key. #114995 made the new-file write conditional (`If-None-Match: *`), and #128866 makes `WriteBufferFromS3` refuse a conditional multipart upload to GCS, because GCS evaluates no precondition on an XML API multipart upload. Neither change is in a release.

The sink now marks its `If-None-Match` as best-effort (`object_storage_write_if_none_match_best_effort` in `WriteSettings`). For such a write, a GCS multipart upload goes ahead unconditionally, as before #114995, and the GCS `CompleteMultipartUpload` request carries no `If-None-Match` (GCS ignores it, and rejects its `x-goog-if-generation-match` translation). Single-part GCS writes stay conditional, other S3 providers keep the condition on `CompleteMultipartUpload`, and the strict callers (Iceberg metadata, backups, the Iceberg REST catalog) are still refused. So two concurrent same-name inserts can race again on GCS objects above the single-part limit, as agreed in #130282.

Reverting #114995 would also remove the error, but it would bring back the silent overwrites and the data race that PR fixed. A conditional GCS path exists (upload into a temporary key, then `compose` with `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`), but it leaves a visible temporary object in the user's prefix and cannot be tested in CI.

Validation: a new `test_storage_s3` case reaches MinIO as `storage.googleapis.com` (plain and partitioned `INSERT`, 1 MiB single-part limit); it fails on master with `Code: 499` and passes with the fix. Two gtests pin the strict refusal and the unconditional best-effort request.

issue.title: Terminate on exceptions in the workload scheduler thread

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with bugfix, not backported by default

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Workload scheduler and resource management: CPU/IO/memory scheduling, concurrency control, worklo...

issue.body:
### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed hangs of workload scheduling. A query using CPU scheduling with separate `MASTER THREAD` and `WORKER THREAD` resources could stop the scheduler thread of a resource when a workload was changed concurrently, after which queries and workload DDL waited forever; such a query now fails instead. A workload named like `p1_fair` could leave its sibling workloads detached, so their queries waited forever.


### Description
An exception escaping a workload scheduler thread was swallowed by the global thread pool: the thread exited silently, and queued requests and later workload DDL waited forever. Now the scheduler thread never dies silently:

- Both scheduler loops are `noexcept`, so an exception escaping them terminates the server. `MemoryTracker` does not throw in this thread (`LockMemoryExceptionInThread`, accounting is kept), nor in the drain of `stop`.
- A failure while modifying the scheduling hierarchy (create, update or delete a workload node) used to reach the DDL caller, which only logged it and left the hierarchy half-modified. It now terminates the server.

Two throws that could reach the scheduler thread are fixed:
- `PriorityPolicy` and `PrecedenceAllocation` keyed their children by name, so a workload named like the internal fair node next to it (`p<N>_fair`) failed the update and left workloads detached. They are keyed by node now.
- `CPULeaseAllocation::grant` and `CPUSlotsAllocation::grant` enqueue the next request, possibly into the other resource's queue (master vs. worker), which may have been purged; that throws `INVALID_SCHEDULER_NODE`. The allocation now fails instead, as if the queue had failed the request.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed a crash, or wrong results from a text index, after merging parts of a `MergeTree` table that has a text index and a column named `_part_index`.

### Description
On 26.3.60.2, 26.8.34.13 and 26.10.2.103, `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` on a `MergeTree` table with a text index and an ordinary column named `_part_index` crashes with SIGSEGV, and a vertical merge of such a table makes text index queries return rows of the other part (`hasToken(text, 'beta')` returns 1000 `'alpha'` rows). The schema is uncommon, but `CREATE TABLE` accepts it. No issue exists; I found it while testing text index merges.

Root cause: a merge that combines the source parts' text indexes maps each merged row to its source part by reading the virtual `_part_index` column, and a table column with that name shadows it. In a horizontal merge the name is read twice and the second copy is null. In a vertical merge the mapping is built from the user's values, which gives wrong rows, `CORRUPTED_DATA`, or an out-of-bounds write in `MergedPartOffsets::insert`.

Change: for such tables, merges rebuild the text indexes of the resulting part instead of merging them, which is the path row-reducing merges (Replacing, TTL, lightweight delete) already take. A new `rebuild_text_indexes` flag drives only the text index decisions; statistics, minmax and projections still follow `merge_may_reduce_rows`. Projections that need the same mapping already guard against such a column (#78429).

Validation: the new test `05617_text_index_merge_part_index_column` covers a horizontal and a vertical merge (`part_log` checks the algorithm). It crashes the server on the base build and passes 50/50 with randomized settings; removing the new condition makes it fail again. 150 related text index and projection tests (1 plain + 10 randomized runs) show no new failures; the only two failures fail identically on the base build.

### Changelog category (leave one):

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
...

### Description

With `ENABLE_BUILD_PROFILING`, lld writes the link time trace at its default granularity of 500 us. For the ThinLTO `clickhouse` link that is 6.7 million events in 1.7 GB of JSON, mostly per-pass LLVM events. Their only reader, Build profile diff, aggregates `OptFunction` events of at least 50 ms. Yet `build_profile_hook.py` parses every byte with `jq` and POSTs it before the artifact upload: 201 s in a PR `Build (arm_release)` ([job](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/42315009375/job/128354633601)), 230 s and 188 s in master `arm_release` and `amd_release`, and master inserts every row into the CI logs cluster.

The link trace is now recorded with `--time-trace-granularity=50000` (cache variable `LINK_TIME_TRACE_GRANULARITY`; `-DLINK_TIME_TRACE_GRANULARITY=500` restores lld's default). lld drops shorter events at record time, also on ThinLTO backend threads, and computes the `Total <name>` rows from all events. Master builds stop uploading link events under 50 ms; nothing in the repository reads them.

Build profile diff judged per-binary trace presence on unfiltered `OptFunction` rows, so a binary with no 50 ms function would be reported as a lost upload. It now uses the `Total OptFunction` row, which every link trace has, old or new, and the reduced PR upload keeps.

Measured on master `28cd3f355cea` (`amd_release` PR configuration, apt `ld.lld-22`, same objects, 16 pinned cores): the `clickhouse` trace is 16.9 MB instead of 1.69 GB; with the keeper trace, `prepare-time-trace.sh` takes 1 s instead of 85 s and the upload is 144k rows (38 MB) instead of 9.7M (3.1 GB). The link took 947 s instead of 1005 s (median of 4 pairs, -5.7%), before #130240 parallelized the regular LTO phase; not re-measured. Every linked binary is byte-identical. With the real insert and diff code against a local server, new traces compare cleanly against old ones, a trace without 50 ms functions is no longer flagged, and a missing one still is.

issue.body:
<!--
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117421
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed reading SQLite tables and columns whose names contain a double quote or a backslash. The `SQLite` table engine, the `sqlite()` table function and the `SQLite` database engine escaped identifiers with backslashes, which SQLite does not honour inside a quoted identifier, so such a table could not be read and the query failed with `SQLITE_ENGINE_ERROR`; a crafted column name could instead redirect the read to another table in the same database file.

### Description

Related: #117421. That PR fixes the SQLite INSERT sink; this is the read path it scoped out, promised in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117421#discussion_r4053575899.

The four SQLite read call sites passed `IdentifierQuotingStyle::DoubleQuotes`, which emits an embedded `"` as `\"` and doubles a real backslash. SQLite, like the SQL standard and PostgreSQL, escapes `"` by doubling it and treats `\` as a literal byte, so the identifier sent was not the one SQLite parsed: `c"1` went out as `"c\"1"`, and `a\b` as `"a\\b"`. Reading such a table failed with `Code: 591 ... SQL logic error (SQLITE_ENGINE_ERROR)`. `CREATE TABLE` succeeded, because structure inference passes the name as a literal, so after #117421 such a table is writable but never readable. Both characters are legal in SQLite identifiers.

This is an identifier-injection primitive, not only an unparseable name. A column named `a" FROM other_table --` went out as `SELECT "a\" FROM other_table --" FROM "target"`, a valid statement over `other_table`: on master that read silently returns `other_table`'s rows. It stays within one statement and one file: `SQLiteSource.cpp:53` passes `pzTail == nullptr`, so text after a `;` is discarded rather than executed, and the same DDL author can already pass arbitrary SQLite text via the `(SELECT ...)` and `query()` forms.

The fix passes `IdentifierQuotingStyle::DoubleQuotesPostgreSQL` at those four sites. That enumerator is the SQL-standard delimited-identifier rule, byte-for-byte what SQLite requires, so no enum member, helper, dispatcher or shared header changes. `DoubleQuotes` is left untouched for its other consumers: the `show_create_query_identifier_quoting_style` setting value, Cassandra and the XDBC bridge.

The four sites reach two dispatchers, `IAST::writeIdentifier` and `quoteExternalIdentifier`, and both needed the change, so the test isolates each with its own arm. It covers the engine table-name, `(SELECT ...)` and `query()` forms, the table function, a pushed-down `WHERE`, both halves of the escaping rule, and two controls green on master.

<details><summary>What each patch changes, per-patch measurements and checks</summary>

1. **Link fix.** In our default RelWithDebInfo builds with clang/lld 21.1.8, master's `clickhouse` failed to link: `localize_rust_c_symbols.sh` rewrites the Rust archives with `llvm-objcopy` (`llvm-objcopy-21`, the `CMAKE_OBJCOPY` of these builds), which leaves `.llvm_addrsig` sections with `sh_link=0` in the objects where it localizes a symbol; lld's `--icf=safe` warns about them and `--fatal-warnings` fails the link. #126478 alone does not fix these builds: it makes CMake pass the LLVM objcopy instead of GNU objcopy, and these builds already used it. With `-Wl,--no-fatal-warnings` in the linker flags the link succeeds; we did not try CI's toolchain. The patch removes `.llvm_addrsig` there, as `strip_rust_symbols.sh` does since #122904; this works with GNU objcopy too. Patch 1 is a link fix that both measured trees contain; it is not measured on its own.
2. **Build system and settings.** Today every build runs the cargo builds and rewrites the copied Rust archives in place (`localize_rust_c_symbols.sh`, `strip_rust_symbols.sh`), so the copy never matches cargo's output, is rewritten again and `clickhouse` relinks even when nothing changed; every library linking a crate also waits for all cargo builds before compiling anything. The patch (a) runs each post-processing step as a custom command that writes a new archive only when its input changed (the approach of #119121); (b) builds the workspace crates with one `cargo build`, so they no longer wait for each other on cargo's target-directory lock, and skips cargo when no input of the Rust libraries changed (`cmake/cargo_if_changed.sh`, which checks cargo's dep-info files and falls back to running cargo); (c) links the crates through imported targets without the cargo dependency, so C++ compiles run in parallel with cargo and only the sources including `delta_kernel_ffi.hpp` wait for the delta-kernel build; (d) on a CMake re-run, rewrites configure-time generated files only when their content changes, lists licenses without a fork per vendored crate and keeps `git status` out of submodule work trees; (e) for the settings files, replaces per-setting template code with table-driven accessors in `BaseSettings.h` and shared field operations, includes `FormatFactorySettings.h` only where it is used and moves the disk checks of `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` to `MergeTreeSettingsDisks.cpp` (no more `MergeTreeData.h`, `ZooKeeper.h`, `ASTFunction.h`). Measured separately on x86, part (a) alone took the no-op rebuild from 21.1 to 4.4 s and the rest of the build-system changes to 1.3 s; part (e) alone took a `Settings.cpp` edit from 42.8 to 28.2 s. One `cargo build` for all workspace crates unifies the features of the dependencies they share, as `cargo build --workspace` does, so the linked Rust code changes slightly: on an earlier master this change alone made the binary 0.3 MB smaller, while the 136 exported Rust FFI symbols and the outputs of PRQL, polyglot, PCO and Vortex smoke queries stayed identical; skim and wasmtime were linked but not run.
3. **ProtocolDefines.h and friends.** The parallel-replicas protocol versions move to `ParallelReplicasProtocolDefines.h`, so `RequestResponse.h` (and everything including it) no longer depends on `ProtocolDefines.h`; `FileCachePolicy` moves to `Core/FileCachePolicy.h`, so `FileCache_fwd.h` no longer includes `SettingsEnums.h`; `ActionsDAG.h` and `IQueryPlanStep.h` are replaced by forward declarations where one suffices. A `ProtocolDefines.h` edit recompiles 115 files instead of 278.
4. **Direct includes.** 87 files that used `FormatSettings` (and a few other headers) through transitive includes include them directly. Patch 4 only adds the direct includes that patch 5 needs; it is not measured on its own.
5. **FormatSettings.h out of common headers.** `ReadHelpers.h`, `WriteHelpers.h`, `FormatFactorySettings.h`, `SettingsEnums.h` and `Context.h` included the whole `FormatSettings.h`. The CSV/JSON enums they need move to `FormatSettingsEnums.h` and the JSON number writers to `writeJSONNumber.h`/`WriteHelpers.cpp`: a `FormatSettings.h` edit recompiles 1,203 files instead of 3,222.
6. **FormatSettings.h out of the remaining wide headers.** `NativeWriter.h`, `DateTimeTransforms.h`, `FunctionBinaryArithmetic.h`, `convertFieldToType.h`, `convertColumnToType.h`, `VirtualColumnUtils.h` and a few others stop including it: 708 files instead of 1,203.
7. **Operators.h and IDataType.h.** `IO/Operators.h` no longer includes `IO/ReadHelpers.h` (a `ReadHelpers.h` edit: 1,338 files instead of 2,002, 1,147 → 933 s (−19%) when measured alone), and `IDataType.h` no longer includes `ISerialization.h`; the substream types it needs move to `SerializationSubstream.h` (an `ISerialization.h` edit: 2,286 files instead of 3,218, 1,516 → 1,267 s (−16%) alone).
8. **Unit-test include.** One unit test used `ISerialization.h` through `IDataType.h`. Patch 8 only adds an include to one unit test; it is not measured on its own.
9. **Precompiled headers.** `cmake/precompiled_headers.cmake` adds per-target PCHs of stable standard-library, fmt, magic_enum, `base/` and third-party headers to the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries, with `-fno-pch-timestamp` so ccache still hits in a new build directory. Earlier attempts found little gain: #9162 (2020) measured a clean build of 74 minutes with PCH against 76 without, and the `dbms`-only PCH listed in #96721 saved 5.9 s, about 3% of CPU time, at 192 cores. Patch 9 covers far more of the build, including the contrib sources that mostly parse their library headers: on these 16-core hosts it cut clean-build CPU time by 19% (x86) and 18% (ARM) and wall time by 18.8% and 17.5%, with the same `.text` size. Compiler caches stay correct: after a change of only the PCH content, sccache 0.19, chcache and ccache 4.9.1 all missed, because the headers inside the PCH are part of what each cache hashes; ccache gets the `pch_defines,time_macros` sloppiness it needs only for the targets with a PCH. We did not measure CI builds with sccache, where every fresh build directory builds the PCHs again.
10. **Opt-in SPLIT_DWARF.** A `SPLIT_DWARF` CMake option (`-gsplit-dwarf -gno-gnu-pubnames`) keeps most debug information out of the objects the linker reads. `Dwarf.cpp` accepts the skeleton units (`DW_TAG_skeleton_unit`) so stack traces keep file and line, and one test that reads the binary's DWARF is skipped in split builds, as it is for `-g0`.
