### How to reproduce

<details><summary>Hosts, configuration and measurement procedure</summary>

- Hosts: x86, AWS r6i.8xlarge (16 cores / 32 vCPU, 247 GiB); ARM, AWS r7g.4xlarge (16 vCPU Graviton3, 123 GiB); Ubuntu 24.04.
- Toolchain: clang/lld 21.1.8 from apt.llvm.org, CMake 3.28.3, Ninja 1.11.1, ccache 4.9.1, Rust nightly-2026-03-22 as pinned by `contrib/corrosion-cmake`.
- Configuration (both arms): `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-21 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-21`, then `ninja -C build clickhouse` (default parallelism, ccache through `COMPILER_CACHE=auto`). Patch 10 is measured with `-DSPLIT_DWARF=ON` against the same tree without it.
- Trees: one source checkout and one `CCACHE_DIR` per arm, never shared. Before each incremental run the tree is synced with two no-op `ninja` runs.
- Scenarios, each timed from the edit to the finished `clickhouse` binary:
  - no-op: `ninja` on the synced tree;
  - leaf, `Settings.cpp`, `ServerSettings.cpp`, `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` and header edits: append a unique comment line to the file, `ninja`, then restore the file (the next sync rebuilds it);
  - CMake re-run: `touch CMakeLists.txt`, `ninja`;
  - new build directory with warm ccache: delete the build directory, `cmake` + `ninja`;
  - clean build: delete the build directory and the arm's ccache directory, `cmake` + `ninja`.
- Order: arms interleaved per scenario (A,B,B,A or A,B,B,A,A,B), 2 pairs for scenarios over 5 minutes, 3 for the others; the table shows medians and the 95% interval of the paired geometric ratio. The arm for patch 9 alone (all patches except 9 vs all patches) was interleaved with the same runs on x86.
- Patch application: 1 → 9 in order on master 64576f956c6b; patch 10 applies on top.

</details>

### Expected performance

<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A rebuild should cost about as much as the change: no cargo run, archive rewrite or relink when no Rust input and no object changed; after a header edit, recompiling only the files that use the header; after a CMake re-run with no real change, no regenerated file that forces recompiles. Clean builds should not parse the same large third-party headers in every translation unit.

</details>

**Patch 1: link fix for the localized Rust archives**

```diff
diff --git a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
index 61cf95aa9c8..4ef48524c02 100755
--- a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
+++ b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
@@ -125,12 +125,15 @@ if [ -s "$LOCALIZE_FILE" ]; then
     # Some Rust archives contain non-ELF members (e.g. debug metadata objects)
     # that cause llvm-objcopy to fail.  In that case, fall back to extracting
     # individual members, processing only valid ELF objects, and repacking.
-    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
+    # Also drop .llvm_addrsig: objcopy leaves its sh_link at 0, and lld --icf=safe then warns that it ignores it
+    # (an error with --fatal-warnings). Without the table lld treats these objects conservatively, as it does
+    # when it ignores the table. See strip_rust_symbols.sh.
+    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
         WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
 
         (cd "$WORK_DIR" && "$AR" x "$LIB_PATH")
         for obj in "$WORK_DIR"/*.o; do
-            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
+            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
         done
         "$AR" rcs "$LIB_PATH" "$WORK_DIR"/*.o
     fi
```

```diff
+# Precompiled headers of stable third-party headers.
+#
+# Most of the compile time of a typical ClickHouse source file is spent in the frontend, re-parsing the same
+# standard library headers for every translation unit. The headers below are used by most sources and change
+# only with toolchain or contrib updates, apart from a few base/ headers that almost every source includes anyway.
+# Each target builds its own PCH with its own flags. Sources with their own compile flags (-march, -O3,
+# -U_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE, ...) cannot use that PCH and are compiled as before.
+#
+# The largest contrib libraries get a PCH of their own public headers as well: their sources are small and
+# spend most of their compile time parsing the library headers, which change only with the submodule.
+#
+# Compiler caches: sccache and chcache hash the preprocessed source, which includes the PCH headers.
+# ccache refuses PCH compiles unless its sloppiness includes pch_defines,time_macros, so it is added
+# to the launcher of the targets that use the PCH (ClickHouse sources do not use __DATE__ or __TIME__).
+
+option (ENABLE_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS "Precompile common standard library, fmt and magic_enum headers for the largest targets" ON)
+option (ENABLE_CONTRIB_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS "Precompile the common headers of the largest contrib libraries" ${ENABLE_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS})
+
+set (CLICKHOUSE_PCH_HEADERS
+    algorithm array atomic bit cassert cctype cerrno cfloat climits clocale cmath compare cstddef cstdint cstdio
+    cstdlib cstring ctime cwchar cwctype deque exception functional initializer_list iosfwd iterator limits map
+    memory mutex new numeric optional ratio set source_location span stdexcept string string_view system_error
+    tuple type_traits typeinfo unordered_map unordered_set utility variant vector version
+    fmt/format.h magic_enum.hpp
+    # Third-party headers included by most sources: vendored Poco, boost, cityhash, double-conversion.
+    Poco/Exception.h boost/core/noncopyable.hpp boost/noncopyable.hpp boost/smart_ptr/intrusive_ptr.hpp city.h
+    boost/smart_ptr/intrusive_ref_counter.hpp boost/container/vector.hpp Poco/Timestamp.h
+    double-conversion/double-conversion.h Poco/Net/Throttler.h Poco/Timespan.h Poco/Message.h Poco/Logger.h
+    # base/ headers included by at least 90% of the sources: an edit of one rebuilds all users of the PCH,
+    # almost all of which include it anyway.
+    base/types.h base/defines.h base/sanitizer_defs.h base/EnumReflection.h base/strong_typedef.h base/extended_types.h
+    base/wide_integer.h base/wide_integer_impl.h base/throwError.h base/BFloat16.h base/Decimal_fwd.h base/unaligned.h

+# clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (target [SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES] {HEADERS header... | REUSE_FROM other_target})
+# SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES: sources in the target's own CMake directory (for contrib: stubs, generated parsers and
+# version files kept next to contrib/<library>-cmake/CMakeLists.txt) are compiled as before.
+function (clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers target)
+    cmake_parse_arguments (PCH "SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES" "REUSE_FROM" "HEADERS" ${ARGN})
+    if (PCH_REUSE_FROM)
+        target_precompile_headers (${target} REUSE_FROM ${PCH_REUSE_FROM})
+    else ()
+        set (headers)
+        foreach (header IN LISTS PCH_HEADERS)
+            list (APPEND headers "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:<${header}$<ANGLE-R>>")
+        endforeach ()
+        target_precompile_headers (${target} PRIVATE ${headers})
+    endif ()
+    # Keep template instantiation in the translation units, so the generated code does not change.
+    set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES PCH_INSTANTIATE_TEMPLATES OFF)
+
+    get_target_property (source_dir ${target} SOURCE_DIR)
+    get_target_property (binary_dir ${target} BINARY_DIR)
+    get_target_property (sources ${target} SOURCES)
+    foreach (source IN LISTS sources)
+        if (source MATCHES "^\\$<" OR NOT source MATCHES "\\.(cpp|cc|cxx)$")
+            continue ()
+        endif ()
+        # Resolve like CMake does: relative to the target's source directory, else its binary directory (generated files).
+        if (IS_ABSOLUTE "${source}")
+            set (path "${source}")
+        elseif (EXISTS "${source_dir}/${source}")
+            set (path "${source_dir}/${source}")
+        else ()
+            set (path "${binary_dir}/${source}")
+        endif ()
+        if (PCH_SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES)
+            string (FIND "${path}" "${source_dir}/" pos)
+            if (pos EQUAL 0)
+                set_source_files_properties ("${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} PROPERTIES SKIP_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS ON)
+                continue ()
+            endif ()
+        endif ()
+        foreach (property COMPILE_FLAGS COMPILE_OPTIONS COMPILE_DEFINITIONS)
+            get_source_file_property (value "${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} ${property})
+            if (value)
+                set_source_files_properties ("${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} PROPERTIES SKIP_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS ON)
+                break ()
+            endif ()
+        endforeach ()
+    endforeach ()
+
+    get_target_property (launcher ${target} CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER)
+    list (FILTER launcher INCLUDE REGEX "(^|/)ccache$")
+    if (launcher)
+        execute_process (COMMAND ${launcher} --get-config sloppiness
+            OUTPUT_VARIABLE sloppiness OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE ERROR_QUIET RESULT_VARIABLE rc)
+        if (NOT rc EQUAL 0)
+            set (sloppiness "")
+        endif ()
+        string (REPLACE " " "" sloppiness "${sloppiness},pch_defines,time_macros")
+        string (REGEX REPLACE "^," "" sloppiness "${sloppiness}")
+        get_target_property (launcher ${target} CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER)
+        set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER "env;CCACHE_SLOPPINESS=${sloppiness};${launcher}")
+    endif ()
+endfunction ()

+function (clickhouse_add_precompiled_headers)
+    if (NOT ENABLE_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS)
+        return ()
+    endif ()
+
+    foreach (target IN LISTS CLICKHOUSE_PCH_TARGETS)
+        if (TARGET ${target})
+            clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_PCH_HEADERS})
+        endif ()
+    endforeach ()
+
+    if (NOT ENABLE_CONTRIB_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS)
+        return ()
+    endif ()
+
+    if (TARGET _aws)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_aws SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__aws})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET grpc)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (grpc SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_grpc})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _rocksdb)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_rocksdb SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__rocksdb})
+    endif ()
+    # The LLVM libraries share their compile flags, so they share one PCH, built by LLVMCore. The libraries below the IR
+    # (and two YAML/DWARF readers) declare their own Argument, Value, Type, CallingConv or isDigit, which clash with the
+    # IR headers of that PCH, so they are compiled as before.
+    set (llvm_pch_exclude LLVMDemangle LLVMSupport LLVMBinaryFormat LLVMRemarks LLVMBitstreamReader LLVMTextAPI
+        LLVMTargetParser LLVMObjectYAML LLVMDebugInfoDWARF LLVMDebugInfoDWARFLowLevel)
+    if (TARGET LLVMCore)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (LLVMCore SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_LLVM})
+        get_property (llvm_targets DIRECTORY "${ClickHouse_SOURCE_DIR}/contrib/llvm-project-cmake" PROPERTY BUILDSYSTEM_TARGETS)
+        foreach (target IN LISTS llvm_targets)
+            get_target_property (type ${target} TYPE)
+            if (target MATCHES "^LLVM" AND type STREQUAL "STATIC_LIBRARY" AND NOT target STREQUAL "LLVMCore"
+                AND NOT target IN_LIST llvm_pch_exclude)
+                clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES REUSE_FROM LLVMCore)
+            endif ()
+        endforeach ()
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _mongocxx)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_mongocxx SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__mongocxx})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _xgboost)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_xgboost SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__xgboost})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _arrow)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_arrow SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__arrow})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _libprotoc)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_libprotoc SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__libprotoc})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _vectorscan)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_vectorscan SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__vectorscan})
```

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
...

### Description

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114819
Found on `Stress test (arm_msan)` for #101273: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101273&sha=87554fdfaf4167d4d5449321eca60e3e24c8eaa5&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20(arm_msan)

`DETACH DATABASE` on a `Replicated` database detaches tables one by one. There,
`shouldReplicateQuery` sees a database-level AST with a null `drop->table`, so each detach reaches
`DatabaseAtomic::detachTable`, which `DatabaseReplicated` does not override and which leaves
`tables_metadata_digest` untouched. An already-executing replicated DDL entry still holds its
`ZooKeeperMetadataTransaction`, so `checkDigestValid`'s "database is probably being dropped" exemption
does not cover it, and its digest assertion compares the full counter against the half-emptied map:
`LOGICAL_ERROR` `Digest does not match`, which aborts the server in debug and sanitizer builds.
`checkQueryValid` already refuses `DETACH TABLE` here, but only on the enqueue path this fan-out never
takes. `DROP DATABASE` fans out drops, which do reach the overriding `DatabaseReplicated::dropTable`, so
it is affected only on a read-only disk, which forces the per-table kind to `DETACH`.

Fix: after `stopReplication()` and before the fan-out, take and release the database-wide exclusive DDL
guard as a drain, covering both kinds. Both edges of that placement are load-bearing. It is no new
unbounded wait: this function already acquires that mutex exclusively 300 lines below.

All 19 CIDB occurrences in 60 days are on `Stress test (*)`, from 7 assertion sites, 0 on master in
120 days: `ci/jobs/scripts/stress/stress.py:865` detaches every database in parallel at teardown,
without waiting for in-flight DDL.

Validation: a new integration test, red without the fix, 50/50 green with it;
`test_replicated_database` 46/46; `test_postgresql_replica_database_engine` 86/86 (the only other engine
with a replication thread). `DETACH DATABASE` is unchanged when idle, +0.11s with 6 concurrent DDL
streams. It needs one new `PAUSEABLE_ONCE` failpoint; no existing pause point parks an entry between
its transaction and the digest commit.

Also noticed, not fixed here: `assertCanBeDetached` runs after the fan-out, so a concurrent reader can
make `DETACH DATABASE` throw `DATABASE_NOT_EMPTY` with its table map already empty.

<details>
<summary>The interleaving, from the failing run's own server log</summary>

```
08:03:02.765701  [27764] {94b7b544}  DETACH DATABASE test_2                  <- stress.py teardown
08:03:02.992034  [36842] {c4328688}  test_2.t_dv: Loading data parts
                                     ^ replicated entry #890, in flight, holds its transaction
08:03:03.125867  [ 3252] DDLWorker(test_2): Unexpected error ... Code: 341 Replication was stopped.
08:03:03.180690  [33523] {94b7b544}  test_2.`03164_multi_key__fuzz_4`: Start preparing for shutdown
   ... dozens more {94b7b544} per-table detaches ...
08:03:03.396327  [36842] {c4328688}  Current in-memory metadata digest: 175636054655643525
08:03:03.507749  [36842] {c4328688}  Digest of local metadata (10323468412571698593)
                                     is not equal to in-memory digest (175636054655643525)
08:03:03.508884  [36842] {c4328688}  Logical error: 'Digest does not match'.
```

Two threads, two query ids, 0.63 s. The aborting query, from `fatal.log`, is
`/* ddl_entry=query-0000000890 */ CREATE TABLE test_2.t_dv UUID '842f90c7-...' (...)`, and the reported
frame is `DatabaseReplicated.cpp:1303 assertDigestWithProbability <- :2648 commitCreateTable`.

The counter is high by the sum of the hashes of the tables the fan-out had already removed, which is why
the delta is not any single table's hash.

</details>

`LEFT ARRAY JOIN` is faster when no joined array is empty: `emptyArrayToSingle` now returns its argument as is instead of copying it row by row, which makes the `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` query of the `array_join` performance test about 1.6x faster.

### Description

`Performance Comparison (amd_release, master_head, 6/6)` on #128472, which only changes Iceberg manifest writing, flagged `array_join #1` (`LEFT ARRAY JOIN` of two one-element arrays over 10M rows) at +15%, confirmed after restart: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=128472&sha=7d3c4efb51731de1f1f13b27344be6f8e4645e81&name_0=PR&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28amd_release%2C%20master_head%2C%206%2F6%29).

An aligned `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` runs `emptyArrayToSingle` over every joined array. The function always rebuilt the column one row at a time, a `PODArray::resize` and an out-of-line `memcpy` call per row, even when no array is empty and the result equals the input. That copy is the whole gap between `#1` (0.112 s on master) and the inner `ARRAY JOIN` `#0` over the same data (0.058 s). In the job's CPU profile all extra time of the PR binary is in this loop (self +30%, its `memcpy` calls +76%), while `executeImpl` is byte-identical in both binaries, only at another address: a per-row call loop that is sensitive to code placement.

Now `emptyArrayToSingle` checks the offsets once (`std::adjacent_find`, stopping at the first empty array) and returns its argument when no array is empty. Columns are copy-on-write, and `executeConst` already returns its argument for the same case.

Validation: local RelWithDebInfo A/B, 10 interleaved rounds of 11 runs, 8 threads: `#1` 0.1015 -> 0.0620 s (1.65x); `#0` and a column with one empty array per block stay within noise (0.98x, 1.00x). `00206_empty_array_to_single` gains queries for every element type path, `Nullable`, `LowCardinality`, nested arrays, an empty array only in the last row, a `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` mixing both cases, and a `Map`; its new reference comes from the unchanged binary, and fast paths with either condition removed fail it.

issue.title: Merge Iceberg manifests on append

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with some performance improvements

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Data lake table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) integration.

issue.body:
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/98178

Every `INSERT` into an Iceberg table adds new manifests and carries all the manifests of the parent snapshot forward, so the number of manifests grows with the number of inserts. Reading manifests is a large part of the work of every query, and for many small manifests it is pure startup delay and cost, while it is easy to avoid: manifests are small, so merging them is cheap. `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... MANIFEST` (#98178) does this only on request and as a separate snapshot.

Like other Iceberg writers (`MergeAppend` in the reference implementation), `INSERT` now merges the small data manifests of the parent snapshot into fewer ones as part of the same commit, without any experimental setting. The new `append` snapshot lists the same data files as EXISTING entries keeping their snapshot ids, sequence numbers, statistics and partition tuples, so no data is read and no separate snapshot is created; older snapshots keep their own manifests.

- The merge happens when the new snapshot would have more small data manifests than the table property `commit.manifest.min-count-to-merge`, or, when it is not set, the `iceberg_manifest_min_count_to_compact` setting (default `100`).
- Merged manifests span partitions (otherwise a table with one insert per partition would never shrink), ordered by partition so the manifest-list partition bounds stay narrow, and hold up to the entries that fit in `commit.manifest.target-size-bytes` (default 8 MiB). Manifests that already hold at least half of that are carried forward as they are, so the cost of a merge stays bounded.
- `commit.manifest-merge.enabled` = `false` disables it. It is done only for format version 2, and skipped (not failed) for encrypted data files and for partition values that cannot be written (including `binary` and nested partition source columns); delete manifests are always carried forward unchanged.
- `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION` rewrites a data manifest that also lists files of other partitions (such as a merged one) without the dropped files, instead of failing. The full `OPTIMIZE TABLE` compaction rejects, before writing anything, a history where a data file is listed in several manifests (a merged one and the originals kept by older snapshots).

The collection and rewriting of data manifests moves from `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... MANIFEST` into a shared `DataManifestsRewriter`; `OPTIMIZE` keeps writing one manifest per partition, or one per partition spec and schema with `iceberg_insert_single_manifest_for_all_partitions` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128880). The manifest-list partition summary as a range and per-file partition tuples in `generateManifestFile` come from that PR. A manifest written with that setting can now also be handled by `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128880

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`INSERT` into an Iceberg table merges the small manifest files of the current snapshot within the same commit when there are more than `commit.manifest.min-count-to-merge` (or the `iceberg_manifest_min_count_to_compact` setting, 100 by default) of them, so the number of manifests a query has to read no longer grows with the number of inserts. The merge can be disabled with the table property `commit.manifest-merge.enabled` = `false`.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130322

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t ... AS SELECT ... FROM t` and `REPLACE TABLE` never returning when `database_atomic_wait_for_drop_and_detach_synchronously` is enabled: the statement waited for its own cached snapshot of the table it replaces. When the replaced table was a materialized view, the query could not be killed.

### Description

On 26.3, 26.8 and 26.10, `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x AS SELECT * FROM t` (and `REPLACE TABLE`, as in the documentation's example) never returns with `database_atomic_wait_for_drop_and_detach_synchronously = 1`. When the replaced object is a materialized view, `KILL QUERY` and `max_execution_time` cannot stop it, because its inner table is dropped without a process-list element (#114259).

Root cause: with `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query` (default 1) a query caches every MergeTree snapshot it takes, and a snapshot holds its storage. The statement reads the old table (structure inference and populate), swaps it out and drops it synchronously, so the drop waits for the last reference, which is in the same query's cache.

Change: clear the query's snapshot cache once the populate is done, before the rename takes its DDL guards, and in a `Replicated` database before the guard for the entry is taken, because the initiator executes the entry in the user's thread. Releasing before the guards also avoids a deadlock with a concurrent synchronous `DROP` of the replaced materialized view, which holds that guard while waiting for the inner table. The whole map is cleared because a replaced materialized view is cached under its inner table; nothing reads a table after either point.

Covered: plain table, `REPLACE`, `EMPTY AS SELECT`, a self-read in an `IN` subquery, a materialized view replaced while being read (a refreshable one checked by hand), a `Replicated` database including the initiator.

Validation: the new test fails on master after 60 s (`TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` at the first statement) and passes with the fix (50/50 with randomized settings, 20/20 with a `Replicated` database).

Found while answering https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130322#discussion_r4513071544

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t ... AS SELECT ... FROM t` and `REPLACE TABLE` never returning when `database_atomic_wait_for_drop_and_detach_synchronously` is enabled: the statement waited for its own cached snapshot of the table it replaces. When the replaced table was a materialized view, the query could not be killed.

### Description

On 26.3, 26.8 and 26.10, `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x AS SELECT * FROM t` (and `REPLACE TABLE`, as in the documentation's example) never returns with `database_atomic_wait_for_drop_and_detach_synchronously = 1`. When the replaced object is a materialized view, `KILL QUERY` and `max_execution_time` cannot stop it, because its inner table is dropped without a process-list element (#114259).

Root cause: with `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query` (default 1) a query caches every MergeTree snapshot it takes, and a snapshot holds its storage. The statement reads the old table (structure inference and populate), swaps it out and drops it synchronously, so the drop waits for the last reference, which is in the same query's cache.

Change: clear the query's snapshot cache once the populate is done, before the rename takes its DDL guards, and in a `Replicated` database before the guard for the entry is taken, because the initiator executes the entry in the user's thread. Releasing before the guards also avoids a deadlock with a concurrent synchronous `DROP` of the replaced materialized view, which holds that guard while waiting for the inner table. The whole map is cleared because a replaced materialized view is cached under its inner table; nothing reads a table after either point.

Covered: plain table, `REPLACE`, `EMPTY AS SELECT`, a self-read in an `IN` subquery, a materialized view replaced while being read (a refreshable one checked by hand), a `Replicated` database including the initiator.

Validation: the new test fails on master after 60 s (`TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` at the first statement) and passes with the fix (50/50 with randomized settings, 20/20 with a `Replicated` database).

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
When a gRPC client cancels a query with the `cancel` field of `QueryInfo`, the query is now also marked as cancelled in the process list, as `KILL QUERY` does, so work that checks only that (window function recalculation, `sleep`) stops promptly instead of running until it finishes or hits `max_execution_time`.

### Description

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130328#discussion_r4514995447

A gRPC `cancel` only cancelled the pipeline executor. Work already inside a processor that checks only the process list entry (`QueryStatus`) kept running: the window aggregate cancellation budget from #130328, `sleep`/`sleepEachRow`. The native protocol marks the entry since #129311 (the re-land of #127149), and HTTP does so on client close when `cancel_http_readonly_queries_on_client_close` is enabled.

The change, in `src/Server/GRPCServer.cpp` only: at the two places in `Call::generateOutput` where a client cancel stops a running executor, call `killCurrentQuery()` first. The resulting `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` is not reported as an error when the client asked to cancel, so the client still gets `cancelled = true` and `query_log` still shows `QueryFinish`. Other exceptions, and a `KILL QUERY` the client did not ask for, propagate as before.

Validation (debug build, signal to call end): a suffix-frame `sum() OVER` over 2M rows took 59.1 s and ended in `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` before, 0.05 s and `cancelled` after; `INSERT ... SELECT sleepEachRow(3)` took 59.0 s before, 0.98 s after. The new test `05617_grpc_cancel_marks_query_cancelled` fails before and passes after (50/50 runs). `test_grpc_protocol` passes (45/45).

Not covered, same as before: a cancel that arrives while the call is inside `executeQuery` (e.g. `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT`) or while a streamed `INSERT` block is being pushed is still noticed only afterwards, and a client that drops the call without sending `cancel` is still noticed only when a write to it fails.

The same URL reaches the server log and, after a successful read, `system.schema_inference_cache.source`. With a named collection, a user who cannot read `system.named_collections` gets its password this way.

issue.title: GCS INSERTs with s3_create_new_file_on_insert fail for files over 32 MiB

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Object storage connectivity (S3/GCS/Azure) including credentials, retries, multipart, etc.

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- Every INSERT to GCS with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` fails once the object exceeds `s3_max_single_part_upload_size` (32 MiB default).
- Triggered by any INSERT producing a multipart upload, even the first write to a fresh key, no concurrent writer needed.
- Expected both INSERTs to succeed and write two separate numbered files.
- On an `S3` table the later `SELECT` then 404s on the key that was never written.

Root cause: `StorageObjectStorageSink` sets `object_storage_write_if_none_match = "*"` for every backend except HDFS, so `WriteBufferFromS3::preFinalize` throws for a GCS client whenever the upload must go multipart, a guard added separately for small Iceberg metadata objects.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `StorageObjectStorage::write` -> `StorageObjectStorage::createSink` passes `fail_if_exists = create_new_file_on_insert && !truncate_on_insert` (StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1109; partitioned path: StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:198). The sink then sets `object_storage_write_if_none_match = "*"` for every backend except HDFS (StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:76-77). On finish, `StorageObjectStorageSink::finalizeBuffers` -> `WriteBufferFromS3::finalizeImpl` -> `preFinalize`, which throws for a GCS-provider client whenever a conditional create is not a single PUT (WriteBufferFromS3.cpp:188-192).

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:76`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp#L76) — conditional write requested for every backend but HDFS
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1109`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp#L1109) — createSink passes fail_if_exists for create_new_file_on_insert without truncate
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:198`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp#L198) — partitioned sink passes the same fail_if_exists
- [`src/IO/WriteBufferFromS3.cpp:188`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/IO/WriteBufferFromS3.cpp#L188) — GCS client throws on a conditional create that is not a single PUT

Impact: On master, every GCS export or append with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` that produces a file larger than 32 MiB fails, even with no concurrent writer. This worked on 26.10. The error does not point to the workaround (`s3_max_single_part_upload_size` above the file size, which buffers the whole object in memory). Unreleased: neither change is on 26.3/26.8, and 26.10.3.7 writes the files.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Reach MinIO under the hostname storage.googleapis.com so the S3 client detects the GCS provider, then INSERT roughly 40 MB of data to exceed the single-part upload size.

```bash
import pytest

from helpers.cluster import ClickHouseCluster

cluster = ClickHouseCluster(__file__)
node = cluster.add_instance("node", with_minio=True)

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def started_cluster():
    try:
        cluster.start()
        # The S3 client deduces the GCS provider from the endpoint, so reach MinIO under the GCS host name.
        node.exec_in_container(
            ["bash", "-c", f"echo '{cluster.minio_ip} storage.googleapis.com' >> /etc/hosts"],
            privileged=True,
            user="root",
        )
        yield cluster
    finally:
        cluster.shutdown()

def test_create_new_file_on_insert_multipart_gcs(started_cluster):
    url = f"http://storage.googleapis.com:{cluster.minio_port}/{cluster.minio_bucket}/gcs_new_file"
    creds = f"'{cluster.minio_access_key}', '{cluster.minio_secret_key}'"
    # About 40 MB, more than `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`: the object is uploaded in parts.
    insert = f"INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('{url}.csv', {creds}, 'CSV', 's String') SELECT repeat('a', 1000) FROM numbers(40000)"

    node.query(insert)
    node.query(insert, settings={"s3_create_new_file_on_insert": 1})

    assert node.query(f"SELECT _file, count() FROM s3('{url}*.csv', {creds}, 'CSV', 's String') GROUP BY _file ORDER BY _file") == "gcs_new_file.1.csv\t40000\ngcs_new_file.csv\t40000\n"
```

### Expected behavior

Both INSERTs succeed and the SELECT lists `gcs_new_file.csv` and `gcs_new_file.1.csv` with 40000 rows each.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
Both INSERTs succeed and the final SELECT returns:
gcs_new_file.1.csv	40000
gcs_new_file.csv	40000
(26.10.3.7 writes `export.csv` and `export.1.csv` with 40000 rows each for the same INSERTs.)
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The second INSERT throws S3_ERROR: GCS conditional create must be a single PUT, CompleteMultipartUpload ignores preconditions.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
helpers.client.QueryRuntimeException: Client failed! Return code: 243, stderr: Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 499. DB::Exception: Received from 172.18.0.6:9000. DB::Exception: GCS conditional create of gcs_new_file.1.csv must be a single PUT. CompleteMultipartUpload ignores preconditions.. Stack trace:
[frames 0-3 trimmed]
5. src/IO/WriteBufferFromS3.cpp:189:15: DB::WriteB
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Two options:
- Treat a GCS client like HDFS when the upload goes multipart: fall back to an unconditional `CompleteMultipartUpload` for the `*_create_new_file_on_insert` sink instead of throwing. Trade-off: large GCS files lose the overwrite protection #114995 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) adds, which is the 26.10 behaviour.
- Exclude GCS in the sink altogether. Trade-off: small GCS files also lose the `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0` single-PUT protection.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- If both #114995 and #128866 are backported, the regression goes with them.
- Other S3-compatible stores that reject `If-None-Match` on PUT or CompleteMultipartUpload would now fail these INSERTs too. Could not verify: only MinIO and the GCS client path were exercised.

Found during automated review of [PR #114995](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114995); this finding was not executed, so nobody is tagged. Per git blame, that PR introduced the cited lines (src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1109, src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:198). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114995_001`

comment.body: I opened https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130525 for this. The sink now treats its `If-None-Match: *` as best-effort: a GCS new-file write above `s3_max_single_part_upload_size` falls back to the unconditional multipart upload from before #114995, so two concurrent same-name inserts can race again on such objects. Single-part GCS writes and other S3 providers stay conditional, and Iceberg, backups and the REST catalog still refuse. Reverting #114995 would also remove the error, but it would bring back the silent overwrites it fixed.

issue.title: Do not execute addDate/addSeconds-family functions on NULL rows of Nullable(String)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Regular scalar functions: string processing, data conversion, arithmetic, math, comparison, condi...

issue.body:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130381
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117359

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `addDate`, `subDate`, `addSeconds`, `addDays`, `subtractX`, `date_add` and the `+` / `-` operators with an `INTERVAL` throwing `CANNOT_PARSE_DATETIME` when the String argument is a `Nullable(String)` that contains NULL rows. Since 26.10 this also broke valid queries such as `addDate(formatDateTime(c1, ...), INTERVAL ...)` over a `Nullable(DateTime64)` (regression from #117359).

### Details

**Problem**

```sql
SELECT min(addDate(formatDateTime(c1, '%Y-%m-%d 00:00:00'), toIntervalSecond(0))) AS lo,
       max(addDate(formatDateTime(c1, '%Y-%m-%d 00:00:00'), toIntervalSecond(0))) AS hi
FROM (SELECT parseDateTime64BestEffortOrNull(arrayJoin(['2026-01-01 10:00:00', '']), 3, 'UTC') AS c1);
-- Code: 41. DB::Exception: CANNOT_PARSE_DATETIME
```

The `+` / `-` spelling fails the same way, for example `formatDateTime(c1, ...) + INTERVAL 0 SECOND` and `date_add(DAY, 1, formatDateTime(c1, ...))`.

**Cause**

Since #117359, `formatDateTime` declines `canBeExecutedOnDefaultArguments`, so it is no longer executed on the rows behind a NULL. Those rows are now filled with the default of the result type, the empty string. Before, they held `formatDateTime(default)`, which was `'1970-01-01 00:00:00'`.

The next function in the chain still accepts the contract, so it runs over the whole nested column, placeholder included, and tries to parse `''`. #117359 does what it promises. What broke is an accidental guarantee: the placeholder under a NULL used to be a parseable string by luck.

The plain `Nullable(String)` case is older: `addDate(x, ...)` and `addSeconds(x, 0)` over a `Nullable(String)` with a NULL already fail on 26.7 and 26.9, as measured by @groeneai. What #117359 changed is the `formatDateTime(...)` input and the `+ INTERVAL` shape.

The String is not parsed in `addDate` or in `plus` themselves. Both end up calling the `addSeconds`/`addDays`/... family, and the parsing happens in `FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval`. The whole family is affected.

**Solution**

Three classes now decline `canBeExecutedOnDefaultArguments`, the same way `parseDateTime` does in #117359:

- `FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval`: covers all `addX` / `subtractX`.
- `FunctionOpDate`: covers `addDate` / `subDate`. It needs its own override because `defaultImplementationForNulls` decides on the outermost function.
- `FunctionBinaryArithmetic` (`plus` / `minus`, also used by `date_add`): it strips the Nullable itself, so the two overrides above are not reached on this path. It declines only for `String +/- Interval`, using the argument types already known in the constructor (`prepared_interval_function`). The rest of the arithmetic is unchanged.

NULL rows are then filtered out before execution, and their result is masked as NULL anyway. `IFunction` is not changed: there is no cheap way to rebuild `f(default)` for the filtered rows, and the contract already says the value behind a NULL is not meaningful.

**Trade-off**

For `FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval` and `FunctionOpDate` the hook has no access to the argument types, so a `Nullable(DateTime)` or `Nullable(Date)` input that contains NULLs also takes the filter, execute, expand path. Inputs without NULLs keep the fast path, because the filtering is keyed on the presence of a NULL (`anyArgumentHasNullRows`). The cost of the filtered path for date inputs with NULLs is not measured.

**Tests**

New test `05616_adddate_subdate_nullable_string_null_rows` covers:

- plain `Nullable(String)` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(String))` with a NULL, for `addDate`, `subDate`, `addSeconds` and `subtractDays`;
- `x + INTERVAL`, `x - INTERVAL` and `INTERVAL + x` on `Nullable(String)`, and `x + INTERVAL` on `LowCardinality(Nullable(String))`;
- the query from the issue, with and without `compatibility = '24.12'`, and `addSeconds`, `+ INTERVAL`, `- INTERVAL` and `date_add` variants over `formatDateTime(...)`;
- `Nullable(Date)` with a NULL, to check the filtered path on date arguments;
- inputs without NULLs.

issue.title: Performance regression: primary-key analysis of a bare UInt8 filter (`WHERE flag`) grows with the number of marks on 26.8 (index_granularity = 8192)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: MergeTree* family: parts, merges, primary index, column statistics, background data transformation.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Regression found by chReplay production query replay

issue.body:
Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/89603

### Description

Since 26.8, a filter on a bare UInt8 column that is part of the primary key (`WHERE flag`) is used in primary-key analysis; 26.6 ignored it. When that column is not the first key column and the first key column changes every few hundred granules, the generic exclusion search splits the part into many ranges, and its cost grows with the number of marks. A `LIMIT 0` query that took a few ms on 26.6 now takes hundreds of ms on a 244k-mark part, and seconds on a production table with about 79M marks at the default `index_granularity = 8192`.

Reproduces on master `26.11.1.1374` (`d29c1d95f608`), 26.8.35.29 and 26.8.1.515. Not reproduced on 26.6.9.19 or 26.6.1.2370.

`WHERE flag != 0` already took this path on 26.6. The regression is that a bare `WHERE flag` now does too.

### How to reproduce

The table uses the default `index_granularity = 8192`. Each `c1` value covers about 1.73M rows (about 211 granules), and `c2` is split 50/50 inside each `c1` value. One part, 2B rows, 244141 marks, about 1 GB on disk.

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (c1 DateTime, c2 UInt8, c3 LowCardinality(String), c4 UInt32)
ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY toDate(c1) PRIMARY KEY (c1, c2, c3) ORDER BY (c1, c2, c3, c4)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192;

INSERT INTO t SELECT toDateTime('2026-08-01 00:00:00') + 30 * intDiv(number, 1730000), (number % 1730000) >= 865000, concat('ex', toString(cityHash64(number) % 20)), toUInt32(cityHash64(number, 1) % 50) FROM numbers(2000000000);

OPTIMIZE TABLE t FINAL;

SELECT c1, c4 FROM t WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2 LIMIT 0 SETTINGS compatibility = '25.12';
```

### Performance

`clickhouse local`, 6 runs of each query in one process (first run, then the warm range):

| Query | 26.6.9.19 | 26.8.35.29 | master d29c1d95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2`, `compatibility = '25.12'` | 32 ms, then 8 ms | 316 ms, then 114-196 ms | 295 ms, then 54-74 ms |
| `WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2` | 17 ms, then 6-25 ms | 276 ms, then 59-184 ms | 295 ms, then 50-106 ms |
| `WHERE c2`, `compatibility = '25.12'` | 20 ms, then 6-17 ms | 218 ms, then 35-84 ms | 305 ms, then 90-175 ms |
| `WHERE c2 != 0`, `compatibility = '25.12'` | 91 ms, then 26-43 ms | 307 ms, then 35-103 ms | 308 ms, then 58-177 ms |

Primary-key selection for `WHERE c2`: 26.6 reads `244141/244141 marks from 1 ranges`; 26.8 and master read `123212/244141 marks from 1156 ranges`.

The cost grows with the number of marks: the same layout with 500M rows (61036 marks, 289 ranges) takes about 6 ms on 26.6 and 20-50 ms on master.

The production table this was found on has about 79.3M marks in 519 parts at `index_granularity = 8192` (about 8177 rows per mark) and the same key layout. A `LIMIT 0` query on it took 41 ms on 26.6.1.2370 and 6278 ms on 26.8.1.515.

### Expected behavior

Primary-key analysis on a bare boolean column should not add seconds of planning time when it prunes little, and a `LIMIT 0` query should stay near-instant as it is on 26.6.

### Note on the previous repro

The earlier repro in this issue used `index_granularity = 1` with 2M rows to get 2M marks cheaply. The affected table uses the default `index_granularity = 8192`, so a fix that only bounds the search for small `index_granularity` (for example https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126096) would not help it.

comment.body:
I opened https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130578 (option B). When the `LIMIT` above a MergeTree read takes no row (`limit + offset = 0`, and it does not read till end for `exact_rows_before_limit` or totals), `ReadFromMergeTree` now stops after partition pruning, statistics pruning and sampling, without the primary key and skip index analysis. `force_primary_key`, `force_index_by_date` and `force_data_skipping_indices` are still checked; parallel replicas and forced or preferred projections keep the analysis.

On the issue's table (2B rows, `index_granularity = 8192`, 244141 marks), `SELECT c1, c4 FROM t WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2 LIMIT 0`: before, a 41053-step exclusion search selecting 123212/244141 marks from 1156 ranges; after, no analysis and 0 marks. Warm medians, base vs fix (RelWithDebInfo): 24.5 -> 2.0 ms with `compatibility = '25.12'`, 14.5 -> 2.0 ms without it. `LIMIT 10` and `count()` are unchanged.

One behaviour change: such a query reads nothing, so `max_rows_to_read` and `max_partitions_to_read` no longer reject it.

issue.title: Reject `input` in `INSERT ... RETURNING`

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Runtime execution pipeline, processors, vectorized operators, resource management during execution.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
Reject the `input` table function inside the `RETURNING` query before building the insert pipeline. Reuse the existing recursive scanner so the check also covers scalar subqueries and CTEs. The supported `INSERT ... RETURNING ... SELECT ... FROM input` path is unchanged.

An `input` behind a view or a SQL UDF is not in the query text, so `Context::initializeInput` also rejects a second read of the input with `INVALID_USAGE_OF_INPUT` instead of a `LOGICAL_ERROR`. The server sets the input initializer and the blocks reader together and resets only the initializer once `input` is read, so a blocks reader without an initializer means the insert has already read the input. Without the blocks reader, a missing initializer is still a `LOGICAL_ERROR`.

`executeQueryImpl` retains input callbacks for `RETURNING`, because the insert may receive its data separately. However, the existing input-function check only scans the insert's source `SELECT`. An `input` inside `RETURNING` can therefore reach `Context::initializeInput` without an initializer, or initiate another input exchange while the client expects a result.

Validated the narrow patch on the reusable `Debug` build based on `ce534743bf1a9469c520f6fa4e1d5ef959936efb` (`26.11.1.1`). Without the fix, the local reproducer aborts on a logical exception in `Context::initializeInput`, and so does the server on the view case. With the fix, the direct, scalar-subquery, CTE, view and parameterized-view cases return `INVALID_USAGE_OF_INPUT` and leave the table empty. A valid local insert using `input` with rows supplied through stdin returns `2, 5` for the count and sum both before and after the fix.

The new functional test and seven existing tests pass: `05453_insert_returning_reject_input`, `05401_insert_returning`, `05402_insert_returning_client`, `05407_insert_returning_explain_subcolumns`, `05441_insert_returning_access`, `05442_insert_returning_local_infile`, `02249_insert_select_from_input_schema_inference`, and `03380_input_async_insert`. The existing tests cover the supported TCP/HTTP, stdin, local, file-input, access-check and schema-inference paths. The C++ style check is clean.

The test sets `send_table_structure_on_insert_with_inline_data = 1` for the view cases, so the insert reads the data the client sends separately. With `0` the server parses the `VALUES` itself, the view is the first reader of the input, and the client gets `Unknown packet 11`, as for `INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM v` on master. `05453` passed 12 of 12 runs with randomized settings, and `03005_input_function_in_join` and `00952_input_function` also pass.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127722
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126476

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required)

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixes unsupported use of `input` in the unreleased `INSERT ... RETURNING` feature.

comment.body:
I read the updated description against `324be04`, and it matches the code: `TCPHandler`, `LocalConnection` and `GRPCServer` set both callbacks together, `Context::initializeInput` resets only the initializer, and `executeQueryImpl` keeps the callbacks for `RETURNING`. `Not for changelog` also fits, because `INSERT ... RETURNING` was merged after the 26.11 cut and is not in a release yet. I have nothing further on the code.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The connection string of the `odbc` and `jdbc` table functions and of the `ODBC` and `JDBC` table engines, password included, is no longer shown in cleartext in the bridge request URL quoted by errors, `system.query_log`, the server log and `system.schema_inference_cache`. On 26.8.28.14-lts, and on master after #120407, a failed bridge request quotes its URL with the password while the logged query shows `odbc('[HIDDEN]', 'db', 't')`:

```
SELECT * FROM odbc('DSN=nonexistent_dsn;PWD=SEKRIT_ODBC_p0', 'db', 't')
Code: 86. DB::HTTPException: Received error from remote server http://127.0.0.1:60245/columns_info?use_connection_pooling=1&version=1&connection_string=DSN%3Dnonexistent_dsn%3BPWD%3DSEKRIT_ODBC_p0&schema=db&table=t&...
```

The same URL reaches `system.query_log.exception`, the server log, `system.schema_inference_cache.source` after a successful read, and the `remote_url_allow_hosts` rejection. With a named collection, a user who cannot read `system.named_collections` gets its password this way.

The server sends the connection string to the bridge as the `connection_string` query parameter, and `maskURICredentials`, which all these renders call since #120407, masks only the userinfo and the presigned-URL parameters.

`maskPresignedURLParameters`, which `maskURICredentials` and `RemoteHostFilter::checkURL` call, now also hides the whole value of `connection_string`: its grammar belongs to the driver, so the password cannot be located inside it. Its other callers hide it too (for example, `url('http://h/?connection_string=...')` in the logged query text). The bridge protocol does not change, so older external bridges keep working.

`05404_xdbc_connection_string_masked` checks the client error, `system.query_log` and an `ODBC` engine insert, and a new `test_allowed_url_from_config` case checks the URL rejection; both fail without the change. The test uses a DSN that does not exist, because a read that really connects crashes the external bridge when the flaky check runs the test in parallel; the success path (`system.schema_inference_cache`) was checked locally against the CI bridge.

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/126230
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129160


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Backward Incompatible Change


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `vector_similarity` index can no longer be created (`CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE ... ADD INDEX`, `CREATE INDEX`) on a `MergeTree`-family engine other than `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`, e.g. `ReplacingMergeTree` or `CollapsingMergeTree`, because `SELECT ... FINAL` that uses such an index may return row versions that were already replaced or deleted. Existing tables keep working. To create such an index anyway, set the MergeTree setting `allow_vector_similarity_index_in_specialized_merge_tree = 1` (or `compatibility` to `26.10` or lower in the default profile).

### Description

The vector index selects candidates in each part before `FINAL` merges the row versions across parts, so on engines whose merges combine rows a newer version that is not a candidate of its own part is dropped and an older one is returned (#126230; reproduced on 26.8-26.10 with default settings). As agreed on the issue, such tables now refuse the index instead of the read path being changed.

The check runs at `CREATE TABLE` and at `ALTER TABLE ... ADD INDEX` (which `CREATE INDEX` becomes), only for an index the statement introduces. It never runs for `ATTACH`, server startup, `RESTORE`, `Replicated` database replay or replica recovery, so existing tables, and replicas applying DDL already committed by an older initiator, are not affected. Two paths that re-create an existing table do run it and need the setting: the `CREATE OR REPLACE` with which a refreshable materialized view without `APPEND` replaces its target on each refresh, and a `CREATE TABLE` that adds a replica to an existing `ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree` (or similar) table. The new MergeTree setting `allow_vector_similarity_index_in_specialized_merge_tree` (default `false`; `true` when the default profile has `compatibility <= 26.10`) restores the old behaviour. Five existing tests now set it.

Validation: the new test fails on master and passes with the change; removing either check makes it fail at the matching statement; 50 of 50 randomized runs pass. A table created by master still loads and accepts other `ALTER`s, and in a `Replicated` database a master replica's `CREATE` and `ADD INDEX` replay on an upgraded one.

issue.title: Support hierarchical (dotted) database and table names

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with new product feature

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Database engine implementations (e.g., Atomic/Replicated) and database-level behavior.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Skip for auto-updating.

issue.body:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/71171

Database and table names can contain dots, and such names can now be written without quotes. A qualified name `a.b.c` has no fixed split into a database and a table anymore: it is resolved against the catalog, trying the name as written, then the longest database prefix first (`a.b` with the table `c`, then `a` with the table `b.c`), then the table `a.b.c` of the current database. Quoting does not matter: `a."b.c"`, `"a.b".c` and `a.b.c` are the same name. This is how the tables of a data lake catalog, named `namespace.table`, are addressed: `SELECT * FROM catalog.namespace.table`.

The current database is hierarchical as well: `USE a.b` is allowed when the database `a.b` exists, when the database `a` has tables named `b.*` (then `SELECT * FROM c` reads `a`.`b.c`), or when there are databases named `a.b.*` (then `SELECT * FROM c.d` reads the table `d` of the database `a.b.c`). Unqualified names inside such a session resolve relatively, including the `SELECT` and `TO` target of a materialized view. `SHOW TABLES` lists the tables under the selected name with names relative to it. `currentDatabase()` returns the name as selected. The `database` setting and the HTTP `database` parameter accept the same names.

Column qualifiers follow: `SELECT a.b.c.x FROM a.b.c` and `SELECT b.c.x FROM a.b.c` work with the table `a`.`b.c`, and inside `USE a.b` also `SELECT c.x FROM c`. `SHOW COLUMNS`, `SHOW INDEXES`, `joinGet` and `dictGet` (in the identifier and the string forms) and qualified asterisks (`ns.t.*`) accept hierarchical names the same way.

The unquoted parts of a name never create a new namespace: `CREATE TABLE a.b.c` creates the table `a`.`b.c` only when the database `a` already has tables named `b.*`, otherwise it fails with `UNKNOWN_DATABASE` as before. This protects against typos in database names (`CREATE TABLE defualt.t` does not silently create `default`.`defualt.t`). The first table of a namespace is created by quoting its name: `CREATE TABLE a."b.c"`. `RENAME TABLE` targets follow the same rule. A dotted database name is accepted unquoted by every statement that takes a database name: `CREATE DATABASE a.b`, `DROP DATABASE a.b`, `USE a.b`, `RENAME DATABASE a.b TO c.d`, `EXISTS DATABASE a.b`, `SHOW CREATE DATABASE a.b`, `SHOW TABLES FROM a.b`, `ALTER DATABASE a.b`, `CHECK DATABASE a.b` and `SYSTEM SYNC/RESTORE DATABASE REPLICA a.b`.

Implementation: the resolution is centralized in `DatabaseCatalog` (`resolveHierarchicalName`, `resolveHierarchicalNameForCreation`, `resolveHierarchicalDatabase`) and used by `Context::resolveStorageID`, `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` and the `CREATE`/`DROP`/`RENAME`/`EXISTS`/`SHOW TABLES` interpreters. `ASTTableIdentifier` keeps any number of parts; all the parsers that hand-rolled `[db.]table` now share `parseDatabaseAndTableAsAST`. Names without dots take the same code paths as before, with no extra catalog lookups. The catalog lookup itself (`DatabaseCatalog::getTable`) stays exact: a name is resolved before the access is checked, and the lookup gets exactly the resolved table.

The access of `CREATE`, `RENAME`, `DROP`, `ALTER`, `DELETE`, `UPDATE`, `OPTIMIZE`, `SYSTEM` and the row-policy statements is checked for the tables the names resolve to: the interpreters resolve the names first, rewriting both parts of the name in the query (`InterpreterCreateQuery::resolveHierarchicalNames`, `InterpreterRenameQuery::resolveHierarchicalNames`, including the `TO` targets of a view), and `getRequiredAccess` sees the resolved names, also on the `ON CLUSTER` path, so a grant on the nonexistent database `a.b` does not authorize anything in the database `a`. The resolution probes which candidate databases and namespaces exist before the access check, so the error a user without grants gets tells `a.b`.`c` from `a`.`b.c`; this is the same information that `UNKNOWN_DATABASE` from `Context::resolveStorageID` reveals for plain names, and it is deliberate: the name is a lookup key, and the check is done on what it resolves to. A query executed `ON CLUSTER` resolves the name on the initiator when it can; when no database of the name exists there, the name is shipped as written. The hosts replaying the query use a qualified name exactly as shipped (`DatabaseCatalog::isBoundHierarchicalName`) and never pick another split of it, so they act on the object the access was checked for on the initiator. A name with an empty part (`.inner_id.x`, `t.`, `a..b`) is not hierarchical and is never split.

The access statements take hierarchical names too: `GRANT SELECT ON catalog.namespace.table`, `CREATE ROW POLICY p ON catalog.namespace.table`, and the corresponding `REVOKE`, `CHECK GRANT`, `DROP`, `MOVE` and `SHOW` statements. The exact name of an access statement is resolved against the catalog the same way as in a query (`resolveHierarchicalNamesForAccess`), so that a privilege or a policy names the object the same name reads in a `SELECT` - a longest-prefix split alone would store the grant on the phantom database `catalog.namespace` and silently grant nothing. Whole-database elements (`GRANT SELECT ON a.b.*`) and the wildcards are prefixes rather than object names, and are taken as written.

Not included, to keep the change reviewable: a relative `USE b` inside `a` (the client mirrors `USE` into the database it reconnects with, so it would need protocol-level support), and translating `GRANT`/`REVOKE` on a name prefix into wildcard grants. Both can be done on top of the `DatabaseCatalog` helpers.

The tests 01936, 02041 and 02963 asserted that three-part identifiers are rejected with `INVALID_IDENTIFIER`; three-part names are valid now and those queries fail with `UNKNOWN_DATABASE` / `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` / `BAD_ARGUMENTS` (a dictionary that is not found) instead, so their expectations were updated. The new tests are `05077_hierarchical_names`, `05079_hierarchical_names_access` (the access checks of `CREATE`, `RENAME` and `DROP` with grants on the phantom database only, and the exact hierarchical names of `GRANT`, `REVOKE`, `CHECK GRANT` and the row policies), `05080_hierarchical_names_metadata_and_functions`, `05182_hierarchical_names_on_cluster`, `05183_hierarchical_database_names_admin` and `05227_hierarchical_names_access_ddl` (`OPTIMIZE`, `SYSTEM`, `ALTER`, `DELETE` and the row policies with grants on the phantom database only, locally and `ON CLUSTER`). `05333_hierarchical_names_bind_function_arguments` checks that the qualified names of `joinGet` and `dictGet` are bound to the objects they denote (in a stored view and in the query sent to the shards), and that `SHOW TABLES` of a name prefix lists the tables of a remote database under it. A bound name in the string form keeps its split into the database and the table by quoting the parts with dots (`'db.`ns.j`'`), so that it is not retargeted when a database `db.ns` appears later. `merge` accepts a namespace of tables as its database (`merge('db.ns', ...)`, or `merge('regexp')` inside `USE db.ns`). `05441_hierarchical_names_review_followups` covers the unqualified `joinGet` / `dictGet` names inside a namespace, mutations, `DROP ... ON CLUSTER` and `EXCHANGE TABLES` access binding, the `GRANTS` of authentication methods, `USE` access checks, and `merge` over a namespace. `05447_hierarchical_names_alias_and_quoted_qualifiers` checks that an explicit alias qualifies a column before a longer hierarchical table name and that a quoted qualifier may cross the boundary between the database and the table; the integration test `test_access_control_on_cluster::test_hierarchical_name_bound_on_cluster` checks on two hosts that a host replaying an `ON CLUSTER` query does not pick another split of a bound name. `05446_hierarchical_names_exact_lookup` covers the exact lookup with the name resolved before the access check (`hasColumnInTable`), computed constant names of `joinGet` / `dictGet` bound in a view, and a short `ATTACH` of the last detached table of a namespace. The statement documentation for `USE` and `SHOW TABLES` is updated in the parsers' doc strings (the pages are autogenerated from them).

`05452_hierarchical_names_review_followups_2` covers an exact database/table qualifier being preferred over a quoted one crossing the boundary, the source of `CLONE AS` resolved before the new table exists, `MODIFY QUERY` bound before it is replayed `ON CLUSTER` or by a `Replicated` database, hierarchical names of parameterized views, the isolation of `_temporary_and_external_tables`, the old analyzer keeping the split of bound `joinGet` / `dictGet` names, dependency checks and renamed restore of stored bound names, and context-dependent name expressions (`getSetting`) not being frozen in a view. `05453_hierarchical_names_xgboost_access` checks that `predictXGBoost` checks the access on the dictionary it loads. `05454_hierarchical_names_review_followups_3` covers a later element of a multi-table `RENAME` seeing the tables moved by the earlier ones, `RENAME TABLE IF EXISTS` of an absent table staying a no-op, the exact-boundary preference in qualified asterisks, and the argument of the `Dictionary` engine bound to the dictionary it denotes (dependencies and renamed restore). `dictGet` and `predictXGBoost` check the access again when a name loads another dictionary (after a rename between blocks), and `ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM` checks `SELECT` on the source actually read if it differs from the bound one.

`05498_hierarchical_names_review_followups_6` covers: a name relative to the current database giving way to the alias of another source (both analyzer compatibility modes); a compound `IN` operand that may be a subcolumn staying an expression in heavy `ALTER UPDATE` and lightweight `UPDATE`; a source database not making an unrelated qualified name an expression (`CREATE TABLE ... ON CLUSTER AS SELECT ... WHERE x IN db.ns.keys`); a column default of `ALTER ... ON CLUSTER` bound before it is shipped; an unqualified `GRANT` or row policy target getting the current database only once; a compound `joinGet` argument that may be an expression; and the MySQL `COM_INIT_DB` access check for the database a hierarchical name denotes.

`05617_hierarchical_names_review_followups_8` covers: a materialized CTE qualifying its columns before a longer hierarchical table name; the columns of a subquery source (from its select list) deciding whether a compound `IN` operand or `joinGet` name is an expression or a table; `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` in a `Replicated` database bound before it is enqueued; and `ALTER ... ON CLUSTER UPDATE ... IN m.n` with a subcolumn `m.n` validated with the mutated table in scope.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- New Feature

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Support hierarchical (dotted) database and table names written without quotes: `SELECT * FROM catalog.namespace.table` resolves against the existing databases and tables (`catalog.namespace`.`table`, `catalog`.`namespace.table`, or the table `catalog.namespace.table` of the current database), `USE catalog.namespace` selects a namespace of tables inside a database or a group of databases with a common prefix, and `SHOW TABLES` lists the tables under it. Closes [#71171](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/71171).

issue.title: Keep database replication running after refused drops and detaches

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Database engine implementations (e.g., Atomic/Replicated) and database-level behavior.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127875
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123694

`InterpreterDropQuery::executeToDatabaseImpl` stops database replication before checking whether its tables can be dropped or detached. A refusal then leaves the database attached with its replication worker shut down. For a `Replicated` database, subsequent DDL fails with `DATABASE_REPLICATION_FAILED`. For a `MaterializedPostgreSQL` database, new rows in PostgreSQL silently stop arriving.

Run the existing table refusal checks before `stopReplication` for databases with replication threads. Remember only the storage whose size check consumed `force_drop_table`, so its drop does not need the flag a second time; the other tables are checked again after `flushAndPrepareForShutdown`, as on master. Release the checked tables before `stopReplication`, because the replication worker may be executing a `DROP TABLE ... SYNC` that waits until nothing else holds the table. Check database detachability before shutdown, and reject detaching a nonempty `MaterializedPostgreSQL` database before its replication handler is stopped.

Reproduced and validated with a master-based Debug build, version `26.11.1.1`, at `ce534743bf1`, before and after applying the fix:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Replicated`: refuse `DROP DATABASE` with `max_table_size_to_drop = 1`, then create another table | `CREATE TABLE` fails with `DATABASE_REPLICATION_FAILED` | DDL succeeds; existing table accepts an insert and contains 1,001 rows |
| `MaterializedPostgreSQL`: refuse `DETACH DATABASE`, then insert 1,000 more rows into PostgreSQL | ClickHouse remains at 1,000 rows while PostgreSQL has 2,000 | ClickHouse reaches 2,000 rows without a restart |
| `MaterializedPostgreSQL`: refuse a size-limited `DROP DATABASE`, then insert 1,000 more rows into PostgreSQL | ClickHouse remains at 1,000 rows while PostgreSQL has 2,000 | ClickHouse reaches 2,000 rows without a restart |

Added `05452_refused_drop_database_keeps_replication`, which also checks a subsequent successful detach/attach and drop and a `Buffer` table that fills its destination during the drop, `test_drop_database_while_worker_drops_table_sync` in `test_replicated_database`, which drops the database while its worker executes a `DROP TABLE ... SYNC` from another replica, and two parameterizations of `test_refused_database_drop_keeps_replication` in the existing PostgreSQL integration cluster. All three regression cases fail without the fix and pass with it.

The patched Debug build, both existing PostgreSQL table attachment/detachment tests, `03362_create_table_after_truncate_replicated_database`, and `05325_replicated_database_drop_view_with_time_series_inner_table` pass. A separate check verifies that a size-limited database drop authorized by `force_drop_table` succeeds and consumes the flag once. C++ style, Python lint and Black checks pass.

This does not make database drops transactional: cancellation or an execution-time failure after shutdown has begun can still leave a partially processed database. The related PR addresses the broader table-shutdown ordering.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `DROP DATABASE` refused by table size or dependency checks no longer stops replication of a `Replicated` or `MaterializedPostgreSQL` database. An unsupported `DETACH DATABASE` of a nonempty `MaterializedPostgreSQL` database is also refused before stopping replication.

issue.title: FINAL without rescoring returns stale row versions in vector search

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Vector similarity index in MergeTree: ANN/HNSW index build/query, usearch integration, vector ind...

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- Under FINAL, vector search without rescoring can return a row version a newer insert already replaced.
- Trigger: querying with `FINAL` and `ORDER BY` a distance function with `vector_search_with_rescoring = 0` and `use_skip_indexes_if_final = 1`.
- Expected the latest version of each key, but the old version (or a deleted row with `is_deleted`) comes back instead.
- Impact: silent wrong top-k results for `ReplacingMergeTree` tables with a `vector_similarity` index until parts merge.

Root cause: `optimizeVectorSearchWithVectorIndexSecondPass` in `useVectorSearch.cpp:433` enables the no-rescoring `_distance` rewrite even under `FINAL`, only disabling the rescoring row filter for `FINAL` at line 437. `MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp:1742` now always applies the candidate filter per block before the `FINAL` merge, so a newer version not in its part's candidate set never reaches the merge and the older candidate wins.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: - `optimizeVectorSearchWithVectorIndexSecondPass` keeps the no-rescoring `_distance` rewrite under `FINAL` (`useVectorSearch.cpp:433`); only the rescoring row filter is switched off for `FINAL` (`useVectorSearch.cpp:437`).
- The reader then cuts each part's block down to that part's index candidates (`MergeTreeRangeReader::executePrewhereActionsAndFilterColumns` -> `ReadResult::optimize`, `MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp:1742`) before the `FINAL` merge. The newer version of a key that is not a candidate in its own part never reaches the merge, so the older candidate version wins.
- #126135 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) made that filter mandatory. Before it, blocks where >= 60% of rows were candidates parked the filter in `final_filter` and never applied it, so `FINAL` saw every version. 26.3.34.136 and 26.6.8.7 return the correct `2 1, 3 1, 4 1` for the repro below.
- Blocks with < 60% candidates were filtered before #126135 too: the `index_granularity = 1` variant already returns the stale row on 26.6.8.7.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/useVectorSearch.cpp:433`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8aa46590c607e/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/useVectorSearch.cpp#L433) — no-rescoring rewrite enabled under FINAL; only the rescoring row filter at :437 checks isQueryWithFinal
- [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp:1742`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8aa46590c607e/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp#L1742) — this PR: candidate filter now always applied in the reader, before the FINAL merge

Impact: Silent wrong top-k under `FINAL`. A replaced row version (or an `is_deleted` row) comes back, with its old payload, for `ReplacingMergeTree` tables that have a `vector_similarity` index. Trigger: an update moves a key's vector out of its part's candidate set while an older version is still a candidate in an unmerged part (for example, re-embedding a document). It lasts until the parts merge. Before #126135 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) only blocks with < 60% candidates were affected; now every block is.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master` (`c4a9337df880`); not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Requires `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` so the old and new versions stay in separate unmerged parts.

[▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/35c14ea0-1070-4fa8-bd71-863cf9de82aa)

```sql
-- Test: vector search without rescoring under FINAL must not return a row version replaced by a newer one.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tab;
SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0;
SET vector_search_with_rescoring = 0;
SET use_skip_indexes_if_final = 1;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tab;

CREATE TABLE tab (id UInt64, ver UInt64, vec Array(Float32), INDEX idx vec TYPE vector_similarity('hnsw', 'L2Distance', 2) GRANULARITY 100000000)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(ver) ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 4;

SYSTEM STOP MERGES tab;

INSERT INTO tab VALUES (1, 1, [0, 0]), (10, 1, [50, 0]), (11, 1, [60, 0]), (12, 1, [70, 0]);
-- Moves id 1 away from the reference vector.
INSERT INTO tab VALUES (1, 2, [100, 0]), (2, 1, [1, 0]), (3, 1, [2, 0]), (4, 1, [3, 0]);

SELECT id, ver FROM tab FINAL ORDER BY L2Distance(vec, [0., 0.]) LIMIT 3;
SELECT id, ver FROM tab FINAL ORDER BY L2Distance(vec, [0., 0.]) LIMIT 3 SETTINGS use_skip_indexes = 0;

DROP TABLE tab;
```

Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`c4a9337df880`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

FINAL queries with vector search should return the latest non-deleted version of each row regardless of whether rescoring is enabled.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
2	1
3	1
4	1
2	1
3	1
4	1
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The no-rescoring candidate filter is applied under FINAL too, so a superseded or deleted row version can be returned instead of the current one.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`c4a9337df880`):

```
1	1
2	1
3	1
2	1
3	1
4	1
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Turn off the no-rescoring rewrite under `FINAL`: `bool optimize_plan = !settings.vector_search_with_rescoring && !read_from_mergetree_step->isQueryWithFinal();`. `FINAL` vector queries then take the path `vector_search_with_rescoring = 1` already takes under `FINAL` (exact distance over the selected granules, no row filter), which returns the correct rows in the repro. Trade-off: `FINAL` loses the `_distance` shortcut and reads the vector column. The control `FINAL, no PREWHERE, no rescoring: the vector column is replaced` in `02354_vector_search_final_prewhere.sql` asserts the current rewrite and has to flip. The repro fits next to the rescoring `FINAL` case in `02354_vector_search_rescoring.sql`.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- Backporting #126135 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) to 26.7/26.8/26.9 without the `FINAL` guard carries the dense-block variant to those branches as well (26.3 does not apply the `_distance` rewrite under `FINAL`).

Found during automated review of [PR #126135](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126135); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr126135_001`

comment.body:
I opened https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130572. It refuses `vector_similarity` indexes at `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE ... ADD INDEX` on every MergeTree engine except `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`. The new MergeTree setting `allow_vector_similarity_index_in_specialized_merge_tree = 1` restores the old behaviour, and existing tables keep loading and replicating.
