issue.title: A Delta Lake SHALLOW CLONE is unreadable: the absolute `file:` data-file path is treated as relative and concatenated onto the clone directory (`Code: 107 FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Confirmed user-visible misbehaviour in official release

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Data lake table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) integration.

issue.body:
🕵️ A Delta **shallow clone** references the source data files by absolute URI (`file:/…`), as the format
requires. When ClickHouse actually opens those files it resolves the path **as relative**, concatenating
the absolute URI onto the clone's own table directory, so every data file is missing:

```
Code: 107. DB::Exception: Cannot get metadata of file
  /…/wh/plain_cl/file:/…/wh/plain/part-00001-….snappy.parquet
  : , errno: 2, strerror: No such file or directory: While executing ReadFromObjectStorage. (FILE_DOESNT_EXIST)
```

Note the mangled path `<clone_dir>/file:/<source_dir>/part-….parquet` — the absolute `file:` URI was
appended to the clone directory instead of being used as the absolute location.

**Any query that opens data files fails.** `SELECT count()` on a clone *without* deletion vectors is the
only thing that appears to work, and only because it is answered from the Delta metadata statistics
(`numRecords`) without opening files; `SELECT *` / `SELECT sum(id)` on the same clone fail. A clone of a
table *with* deletion vectors fails even on `count()`, because deletion vectors force a file read.

### Reproduction

Spark 4.0.2 + delta-spark 4.0.1 writing to a local directory; ClickHouse reads via `deltaLakeLocal`.

```python
# spark-submit --jars delta-spark_2.13-4.0.1.jar,delta-storage-4.0.1.jar repro.py
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
spark = (SparkSession.builder.master("local[2]")
    .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
    .getOrCreate())

src = "/tmp/d_src"; clone = "/tmp/d_clone"
spark.sql(f"CREATE TABLE src (id BIGINT, n1 INT) USING delta LOCATION '{src}'")
spark.sql("INSERT INTO src SELECT id, CAST(id AS INT) FROM range(100)")
spark.sql(f"CREATE TABLE clone SHALLOW CLONE src LOCATION '{clone}'")
```

```sql
-- ClickHouse
SELECT count()   FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/d_clone');   -- 100  (metadata only; misleading)
SELECT sum(id)   FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/d_clone');   -- Code: 107  (opens files → mangled path)
SELECT *         FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/d_clone') FORMAT Null;  -- Code: 107
```

**Expected:** the clone reads the source's data files (here `sum(id)` = 4950, 100 rows).
**Actual:** `Code: 107 FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` for any file-opening query, with the concatenated
`<clone>/file:/<source>/part-….parquet` path. (With deletion vectors enabled on the source, even
`count()` fails the same way.)

### Root cause (single site)

The kernel-returned data-file path is resolved in one place,
`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/DeltaLake/TableSnapshot.cpp:635`:

```cpp
std::string full_path = DB::resolvePathInsideTable(
    context->getDataPath(), DB::unescapeForFileName(KernelUtils::fromDeltaString(path)));
```

and `resolvePathInsideTable` (`DataLakes/Common/Common.cpp:148`) does a plain
`std::filesystem::path(table_path) / relative_path`. A `file:`-scheme string has no leading `/`, so it
is joined as a *relative* path → `<clone_dir>/file:/<source_dir>/…`. For a normal (non-clone) table the
kernel hands back an in-table path so this works; for a shallow clone the path is an absolute `file:`
URI pointing outside the table, which is mishandled.

A fix would detect a kernel-returned absolute URI (`file://`, `s3://`, …) or absolute path and use it
directly rather than joining it under `getDataPath()` (the scheme-parsing helpers already exist in
`DeltaLake/KernelHelper.cpp`). Note `resolvePathInsideTable` also intentionally throws
`PATH_ACCESS_DENIED` for anything outside the table directory — shallow clones legitimately reference
files outside the clone dir, so that guard needs to permit scheme-qualified absolute paths. This is the
Delta analogue of the external-path support proposed for Iceberg in #90740.

This resolution is shared by all Delta backends (the reader is kernel-only, so the setting
`allow_experimental_delta_kernel_rs` is irrelevant), so S3/Azure/HDFS shallow clones — whose add-paths
are absolute `s3://` / `abfss://` / `hdfs://` URIs — should fail identically; verified here on
`deltaLakeLocal` with `file:` URIs.

comment.body:
Acknowledged. I'm investigating the absolute data-file path handling for Delta Lake shallow clones; I'll follow up here with a PR (or my findings) shortly.

issue.title: Look the columns cache up once per mark range, not once per PREWHERE gap

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with some performance improvements

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Allows running workflows for external contributors

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: MergeTree* family: parts, merges, primary index, column statistics, background data transformation.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
With `use_columns_cache = 1`, an in-order or `FINAL` read of a part with many marks and a `PREWHERE` that leaves gaps was 2-5x slower than without the cache, even with every lookup a hit. After every gap the reader re-enters its mark range, and `startColumnsCacheRange` of `MergeTreeReaderWide` and `MergeTreeReaderCompact` looked up the cache entries of every column for the whole rest of the range again, which is quadratic in the length of the range. In-order and `FINAL` reads give a reader whole parts, so with thousands of marks per part this dominated the query. A re-entry now keeps the entries looked up when the range began. Two smaller costs of the same reads are gone too: a copy for the cache reserved a whole stripe per run of granules (often a single granule after `PREWHERE` gaps), and the wide reader looked columns up in name-keyed sets for every granule.

On one wide part of 3M rows and 5,861 marks with 20 `UInt32` columns, 1 thread and a warm cache, a `PREWHERE` passing 3% of the rows goes from 537 ms to 17 ms CPU for `FINAL`, against 116 ms without the cache. All 70 query shapes tried, on wide and compact parts, are faster with the cache now, at 0.04-0.46x of the CPU without it. The new performance test `columns_cache_prewhere_gaps` goes from about 0.4 s to 0.017 s per query. The perf comparison environment now gets a 1 GiB columns cache instead of none, so that the test measures it. Queries use the cache only with `use_columns_cache = 1`, which is off by default, so other performance tests are not affected.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127287

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Reads from the columns cache (`use_columns_cache = 1`) with a `PREWHERE` that skips granules no longer look the cache up again after every skipped part of the range. This made long in-order and `FINAL` reads of cached parts several times slower than reads without the cache.

issue.title: Delayed Distributed INSERT ignores kill at shutdown, Buffer rows lost

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Distributed table engine & query routing across shards (sharding/load balancing).

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- A client INSERT delayed by `bytes_to_delay_insert` at SIGTERM is not cancelled and stalls the graceful stop.
- Trigger: synchronous HTTP INSERT into a `Distributed` table with `max_delay_to_insert` above `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, pending bytes past threshold.
- Expected the stop to finish in seconds and keep all rows; instead it stalls then force-exits.
- Forced exit skips `ContextSharedPart::shutdown`, so every acknowledged `Buffer` row and async-insert queue entry on the node is dropped.

Root cause: The delay loop in `StorageDistributed.cpp` only checks `isShutdownCalled`, pending bytes, and elapsed time, never query cancellation; `killAllQueries` in `Server.cpp` runs before `shutdown_called` is set in `Context.cpp`, so the kill has no effect and `safeExit` later skips the real shutdown path.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `Server::main` closes the listeners, calls `killAllQueries` (`Server.cpp:3947`), waits for connections (`Server.cpp:3954`) and `safeExit`s if any remain (`Server.cpp:3988`). All of that runs before `global_context->shutdown()` (`Server.cpp:1653`) sets `shutdown_called` (`Context.cpp:1172`). The delay loop (`StorageDistributed.cpp:2427-2430`, entered from `DistributedSink::consume`, `DistributedSink.cpp:225`) checks only `isShutdownCalled`, pending bytes and elapsed time. So the kill is ignored and the new check is never reached.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/StorageDistributed.cpp:2430`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1dc326280a7/src/Storages/StorageDistributed.cpp#L2430) — delay loop polls `isShutdownCalled`, pending bytes and elapsed time; never the query's cancellation
- [`programs/server/Server.cpp:3947`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1dc326280a7/programs/server/Server.cpp#L3947) — `killAllQueries` before the connection wait; the delayed INSERT ignores it
- [`programs/server/Server.cpp:3988`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1dc326280a7/programs/server/Server.cpp#L3988) — `safeExit` when connections remain after `shutdown_wait_unfinished`; skips `global_context->shutdown()`
- [`src/Interpreters/Context.cpp:1172`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1dc326280a7/src/Interpreters/Context.cpp#L1172) — `shutdown_called` is set only inside `ContextSharedPart::shutdown`, reached from `Server.cpp:1653` after the forced-exit decision

Impact: Data loss on a graceful restart. Every acknowledged `Buffer` row and async-insert queue entry on the node is dropped, for all tables and not only the `Distributed` one, because `_exit` skips `ContextSharedPart::shutdown`. Trigger: a `Distributed` table with `bytes_to_delay_insert` and `max_delay_to_insert` above `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, pending bytes over the threshold (shard outage), and a synchronous client INSERT in the delay at SIGTERM. With the default `max_delay_to_insert = 60` the stop is held for up to 60 s instead (not measured). Pre-existing: also reproduced on official 26.10.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Reproduce with `bytes_to_delay_insert` and `max_delay_to_insert` set above `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, a shard outage to keep pending bytes over threshold, and a synchronous client INSERT in flight at SIGTERM.

```bash
import threading
import time

import pytest

from helpers.cluster import ClickHouseCluster

cluster = ClickHouseCluster(__file__)
node = cluster.add_instance(
    "node", main_configs=["configs/remote_servers.xml"], stay_alive=True
)
shard = cluster.add_instance("shard", stay_alive=True)

BUFFER_THRESHOLDS = "1, 100000, 100000, 1000000, 1000000000, 10000000, 1000000000"

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def started_cluster():
    try:
        cluster.start()
        yield cluster
    finally:
        cluster.shutdown()

def test_client_insert_delayed_during_shutdown(started_cluster):
    shard.query("CREATE DATABASE cli")
    shard.query("CREATE TABLE cli.data (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x")
    node.query("CREATE DATABASE cli")
    node.query(
        "CREATE TABLE cli.dist (x UInt64) ENGINE = Distributed(shard_cluster, cli, data) "
        "SETTINGS bytes_to_delay_insert = 1, max_delay_to_insert = 3600"
    )
    node.query("SYSTEM STOP DISTRIBUTED SENDS cli.dist")
    node.query("INSERT INTO cli.dist SELECT number FROM numbers(10)")
    node.query("CREATE TABLE cli.mt (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x")
    node.query(f"CREATE TABLE cli.buf (x UInt64) ENGINE = Buffer(cli, mt, {BUFFER_THRESHOLDS})")
    node.query("INSERT INTO cli.buf SELECT number FROM numbers(100)")

    # A client INSERT into `dist` is being delayed by `bytes_to_delay_insert` when the stop begins.
    def delayed_insert():
        try:
            node.http_query(
                "INSERT INTO cli.dist SETTINGS async_insert = 0 VALUES (1)",
                method="POST",
                params={"query_id": "delayed_client_insert"},
                timeout=900,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"delayed insert ended with: {str(e)[:200]}")

    threading.Thread(target=delayed_insert, daemon=True).start()
    for _ in range(100):
        if node.query("SELECT count() FROM system.processes WHERE query_id = 'delayed_client_insert'") == "1\n":
            break
        time.sleep(0.1)
    else:
        assert False, "the client INSERT did not start"
    time.sleep(2)

    start = time.time()
    node.stop_clickhouse(stop_wait_sec=600)
    print(f"stop took {time.time() - start:.1f}s, harness SIGKILL: {node.clickhouse_forced_stop}")
    node.start_clickhouse()

    count = node.query("SELECT count() FROM cli.mt")
    print(f"bug case: mt count after restart = {count!r}")
    assert count == "100\n"
```

### Expected behavior

The stop should finish quickly and all acknowledged `Buffer` rows should survive the restart.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
mt count after restart = '100\n', with the stop finishing within seconds (the same-binary controls took 1.2 s and 2.2 s and kept 100 rows)
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The stop stalls for the full delay window and then force-exits, losing all acknowledged `Buffer` rows and async-insert queue entries on the node.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
run 1: stop took 120.2s, harness SIGKILL: False
bug case: mt count after restart = '0\n'
E       AssertionError: assert '0\n' == '100\n'
run 2: stop took 120.5s, harness SIGKILL: False
bug case: mt count after restart = '0\n'
E       AssertionError: assert '0\n' == '100\n'
standalone script on clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.10: graceful stop took 124 s; rows in db.mt after restart (expected 100)	
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Also leave the delay loop when the INSERT is cancelled: pass `[this] { return isCancelled(); }` from `DistributedSink::consume`, or check the query's `QueryStatus::isKilled`. Then `killAllQueries` ends the INSERT before the connection wait, and `KILL QUERY` takes effect at once. Trade-off: the delayed INSERT fails with `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` instead of queueing its block. It was never acknowledged, so no acknowledged row is lost.

</details>

### Additional context

Same pattern as #129890.

Open risks:
- `INSERT ... SELECT` into the `Distributed` table is always synchronous and takes the same loop; not exercised at shutdown.
- Default async path (`async_insert = 1`, `wait_for_async_insert = 1`): the client waits in `WaitForAsyncInsertSource`, which does not poll cancellation either (`KILL QUERY SYNC` took 21.3 s for `max_delay_to_insert = 20`). Its 120 s `wait_for_async_insert_timeout` usually ends before the forced exit; not exercised at shutdown.
- Refreshable MV refreshes and background queries joined before `ContextSharedPart::shutdown` (`Server.cpp:3962-3963`) can sit in the same loop; not exercised.

Found during automated review of [PR #129890](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129890); this finding was not executed, so nobody is tagged. The cited lines predate that PR: per git blame they were introduced by #115377 (Bound the shutdown wait for cancelled backups and restores). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr129890_001`

comment.body:
Acknowledged. I'm investigating why a client INSERT sleeping in the `bytes_to_delay_insert` delay of a `Distributed` table is not cancelled by `killAllQueries` at shutdown; I'll follow up here with a PR (or my findings) shortly.

comment.body:
I re-reviewed `f1fcf088` and measured it on the CI `amd_debug` binary of this head (merge commit `68c46197`), on a single node with an embedded Keeper and a one-replica cluster `c`.

My earlier points:
1. Fixed. `GRANT SYSTEM DROP VECTOR SIMILARITY INDEX CACHE ON tenant.t` is accepted, and with only that grant `FOR TABLE tenant.t` works, while `FOR TABLE default.t` and the form without a table return `ACCESS_DENIED`.
2. Fixed. No other rotation set in `QueryFuzzer.cpp` contains the type, so `FOR TABLE ... INDEX ...` is fuzzed as written.
3. Fixed in the changelog entry. The first line of the description still says `[FOR TABLE db.t] [INDEX idx]`.

`removeAndCancelPendingInsertions` and the guarded erase in `cleanup` look right to me. I also ran the `05509` sequence by hand and read `system.stack_trace` while the failpoint was paused: the paused thread is the `TCPHandler` during planning (`ReadFromMergeTree::selectRangesToRead` -> `filterMarksUsingIndex` -> `MergeTreeIndexReader::read`), not a pipeline thread inside `IProcessor::work`, so the `PAUSE` does not hold an executor thread.

On the open review threads:
- Database existence (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130325#discussion_r4518736581): this is not new. `InterpreterSystemQuery::execute` resolves the name for every statement that takes a table, before any handler runs. For a user with no grants, `FOR TABLE nonexistent_db.t` gives `UNKNOWN_DATABASE` and `FOR TABLE private_db.t` gives `ACCESS_DENIED`, the same as `SYSTEM DROP TIME SERIES CACHES`, `SYSTEM PREWARM MARK CACHE` and a plain `SELECT * FROM nonexistent_db.t`. I would not special-case this command.
- ON CLUSTER (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130325#discussion_r4527579544): reproduced. From database `tenant`, a user granted the privilege only on `tenant.t` (plus `CLUSTER`) ran `... ON CLUSTER c FOR TABLE t`. The queued query keeps the bare `FOR TABLE t`, and afterwards the search on `default.t` missed the cache while the one on `tenant.t` hit it. The dictionary commands had the same problem, fixed for #114322 in `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor::visitDDL(ASTSystemQuery &)`: it qualifies a bare name with the initiator's database unless the cluster sets its own default database. Adding `CLEAR_VECTOR_SIMILARITY_INDEX_CACHE` there should make the queued query use the database the access check used.
- Moved parts (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130325#discussion_r4527579558): the gap exists but is bounded. The moved-away copy evicts its own entries when its last reader releases it (`removeIfNeeded` -> `clearCaches`, `IMergeTreeDataPart.cpp:1172`), so I would not block on it.

No other findings.

issue.title: Add SQL-managed CREATE/ALTER/DROP CLUSTER

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with new product feature

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Distributed table engine & query routing across shards (sharding/load balancing).

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Allows running workflows for external contributors

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: PR that regenerates docs artifacts from source; exempt from the autogenerated-region edit guard

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/102405
-->

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/93137.

This is a **new implementation** of SQL-managed cluster definitions.

The earlier approach on branch `feature-sql-cluster-interface` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/102405) grew too complex: separate `CREATE ENDPOINT` / `CREATE SHARD` / `CREATE CLUSTER` catalog layers, distributed DDL via `ON CLUSTER`, and a dedicated `ClusterMetadataDDLWorker`. This PR replaces that design with a simpler model:

- Single nested `CREATE CLUSTER` / `ALTER CLUSTER` / `DROP CLUSTER` syntax with `SHARD` and `REPLICA`
- Metadata storage behind `<cluster_metadata>`, modeled after `NamedCollections`
- Incremental in-memory updates on local DDL; background sync when metadata is stored in Keeper
- New `source` and `create_query` columns in `system.clusters` for SQL-managed clusters
- Dedicated privileges: `CREATE SQL CLUSTER`, `ALTER SQL CLUSTER`, `DROP SQL CLUSTER`

## Metadata storage

Configured via `<cluster_metadata>` in the server config. Supported backends:

| `type` | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `local` (default) | Metadata stored as `.sql` files under `{data_path}/sql_clusters_metadata` on each node |
| `local_encrypted` | Same as `local`, with encryption (`key_hex`, `algorithm`) |
| `keeper` / `zookeeper` | Metadata stored in ClickHouse Keeper; other nodes reload via a background watch |
| `keeper_encrypted` / `zookeeper_encrypted` | Same as `keeper`, with encryption |

Example config for local storage:

```xml
<cluster_metadata>
    <type>local</type>
    <path>/var/lib/clickhouse/sql_clusters_metadata</path>
</cluster_metadata>
```

Example config for Keeper storage:

```xml
<cluster_metadata>
    <type>keeper</type>
    <path>/clickhouse/sql_cluster_metadata</path>
    <update_timeout_ms>5000</update_timeout_ms>
</cluster_metadata>
```

Each SQL-managed cluster is stored as a single `CREATE CLUSTER ...` statement. On startup, `SQLClusterFactory` loads metadata into `Context`; local DDL updates both storage and in-memory cluster definitions immediately.

### Local vs Keeper behavior

- **Local storage** keeps metadata on disk independently on each node. Use `ON CLUSTER` to run DDL on all nodes so every replica gets its own metadata file. Covered by integration tests (`test_local_storage_on_cluster`, `test_local_storage_encrypted_on_cluster`).
- **Keeper storage** stores metadata centrally. DDL can be executed on a single node; other nodes pick up changes via background sync (`SQLClusterFactory::updateFunc`). Covered by integration tests (`test_keeper_storage`, `test_keeper_storage_encrypted`).

All three statements also accept an optional `ON CLUSTER` clause and are executed through the existing distributed DDL infrastructure when it is present.

## Example

```sql
CREATE CLUSTER my_cluster (
    user = 'Me',
    SHARD (
        user = 'Me', password = 'p@s$w0rd',
        REPLICA (host = 'abc.clickhouse.cloud', port = 9000),
        REPLICA (host = 'def.clickhouse.cloud', port = 9000, user = 'Alexey', password = 'qwerty')
    ),
    SHARD (
        user = 'Me', password = 'p@s$w0rd',
        host = 'xyz.clickhouse.cloud', port = 9000
    )
);

-- local storage: distribute DDL to all nodes
CREATE CLUSTER my_cluster ON CLUSTER 'my_clickhouse_cluster' (...);

ALTER CLUSTER my_cluster (
    user = 'Me',
    SHARD (
        REPLICA (host = 'abc.clickhouse.cloud', port = 9000),
        REPLICA (host = 'def.clickhouse.cloud', port = 9000)
    )
);

DROP CLUSTER my_cluster;
```

SQL-managed clusters appear in `system.clusters` with `source = 'SQL'` and the stored `create_query`. Secrets in `create_query` are hidden according to the same rules as `system.named_collections`.


### Changelog category (leave one):
- New Feature


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Add SQL-managed `CREATE CLUSTER`, `ALTER CLUSTER`, and `DROP CLUSTER` statements with local or Keeper-backed metadata storage.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Merges that only delete rows (`ReplacingMergeTree`, `CollapsingMergeTree`, `VersionedCollapsingMergeTree`, lightweight deletes, `TTL ... DELETE`, `OPTIMIZE ... DEDUPLICATE`) now merge existing text indexes and projections with `_part_offset` instead of rebuilding them. `OPTIMIZE FINAL` of a `ReplacingMergeTree` with a text index that drops 16% of the rows takes 40% less time and 6 times less memory. Controlled by the MergeTree setting `merge_text_indexes_and_projections_on_delete_only_merges` (enabled by default); with it enabled, a merge of `CollapsingMergeTree` data with invalid values of the sign column fails with `INCORRECT_DATA` if the table has a text index or such a projection, and disabling it merges such data as before.

### Description

Continues Anton Popov's branch, as asked in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/120804#issuecomment-6741931889, from its port to master in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/120804#issuecomment-6741488996 (source) and https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/120804#issuecomment-6741492049 (tests). The first commit is that port, with his authorship of `2244d92d65`.

`OPTIMIZE FINAL` runs of a `ReplacingMergeTree` with a text index (RelWithDebInfo, setting on vs off, 10 pairs, 2.5M source rows):

| rows dropped | time, on / off | peak memory, on / off |
|---|---|---|
| 16% | 0.60 | 26 / 162 MiB |
| 90% | 0.99 | 39 / 117 MiB |
| none (`MergeTree`) | 1.00 | 22 / 22 MiB |

The new perf test `text_index_merge_delete_only.xml` covers 21% and 83% dropped; at 83% the merge is 20% slower.

Merged parts were byte-identical to rebuilt ones in 11 cases, but a projection orders rows with equal sort keys by source part, so replicas that differ in the setting or version fetch such parts; `compatibility = '26.10'` keeps rebuilding.

Behaviour change: an invalid sign in `CollapsingMergeTree` data (from an `INSERT` with `optimize_on_insert = 0` or an attached part) now makes a horizontal merge of a table with a text index or a `_part_offset` projection fail with `INCORRECT_DATA`. `isMappingEnabled` is now also true for the new mode; its other reader `UniqueKeyTxnCommit` has no caller yet (#123013). Merges keep rebuilding when the table or a source part has a column `_part_offset` or `_part_index`, since it shadows the virtual column the mapping reads.

issue.title: Writing Iceberg `.metadata.json` with `zstd` at a high `output_format_compression_level` allocates ~836 MiB for a tiny file

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Data lake table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) integration.

issue.body:
### Describe the situation

Writing Iceberg metadata with `zstd` at a high `output_format_compression_level` allocates a full-size zstd compression context for every `.metadata.json` file. At level 22 that is about 836 MiB, even though the file is a few hundred bytes. This happens on every `CREATE TABLE` (`v1.metadata.json`) and on every `INSERT` commit (`vN.metadata.json`).

This is the same root cause that https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130231 fixes for Parquet pages, but in a code path that PR does not touch.

### How to reproduce

On current `master` (tested with `26.11.1.1724`, commit `5e817c7b710b490bc14de98ab6d504498409800c`):

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (a Int64, s String) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('<user_files>/t')
SETTINGS iceberg_metadata_compression_method = 'zstd';

INSERT INTO t
SETTINGS allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1,
         iceberg_metadata_compression_method = 'zstd',
         output_format_compression_level = 22,
         output_format_parquet_compression_method = 'none'
SELECT number, toString(number) FROM numbers(10);
```

`output_format_parquet_compression_method = 'none'` only reduces how much the data files contribute; the effect comes from the metadata write.

Peak memory of the `INSERT` (`clickhouse client --memory-usage`):

| metadata compression | `output_format_compression_level` | peak memory |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | 22 | 0.4 MiB |
| `zstd` | 3 | 5.9 MiB |
| `zstd` | 19 | 91.9 MiB |
| `zstd` | 22 | **835.9 MiB** |

The resulting `v2.zstd.metadata.json` is 715 bytes. A breakpoint on `ZstdDeflatingWriteBuffer::initialize` shows exactly one level-22 context per `INSERT`, created from `IcebergStorageSink::onFinish` → `writeMetadataFileAndVersionHint` → `writeMetadataFile` → `writeMessageToFile`. `ZSTD_resetCCtx_internal` is called with `pledgedSrcSize = ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN`.

These allocations are not checked against `max_memory_usage`: they show up under `MemoryAllocatedWithoutCheck`, and they add up when several Iceberg tables commit concurrently.

### Root cause

`writeMessageToFile` already has the whole JSON in memory, but compresses it through the streaming wrapper:

https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5e817c7b710b490bc14de98ab6d504498409800c/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp#L357-L364

`WriteBuffer::finalize` first calls `next()` (`WriteBuffer::finalizeImpl() { next(); }`). That makes `ZstdDeflatingWriteBuffer::nextImpl` call `ZSTD_compressStream2` with `ZSTD_e_flush`:

https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5e817c7b710b490bc14de98ab6d504498409800c/src/IO/ZstdDeflatingWriteBuffer.cpp#L96-L108

zstd infers the source size only when the first call of a frame uses `ZSTD_e_end` (`ZSTD_CCtx_init_compressStream2`: `if (endOp == ZSTD_e_end) cctx->pledgedSrcSizePlusOne = inSize + 1;`). With `ZSTD_e_flush`, the size stays unknown, so zstd uses the full level-22 parameters (`windowLog = 27`, `chainLog = 27`, `hashLog = 25`) instead of shrinking them to the input size. By zstd's own estimate (`ZSTD_estimateCStreamSize_usingCParams`), that is about 834 MiB with unknown size, compared with about 18.5 MiB for a known 1 MiB input.

`IcebergRESTCatalogStorage` writes metadata the same way:

https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5e817c7b710b490bc14de98ab6d504498409800c/src/Server/IcebergRESTCatalog/IcebergRESTCatalogStorage.cpp#L68-L70

### Suggested fix

Compress the in-memory metadata in one shot so zstd sees the source size, as https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130231 does in `Parquet::compress`. For example, use `ZSTD_compress2` or `ZSTD_compress` when the method is `zstd`, in both `writeMessageToFile` and `IcebergRESTCatalogStorage`.

A broader option is to make `ZstdDeflatingWriteBuffer::finalizeImpl` call `flush(ZSTD_e_end)` directly when no `ZSTD_compressStream2` call has happened yet, tracked with an explicit flag rather than `total_out`. That helps any caller that writes a blob and immediately calls `finalize`. It does not help callers that call `next()` first, which includes the `IOutputFormat`-based sinks.

A regression test can follow `05569_parquet_zstd_memory_limit` from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130231: write an `IcebergLocal` table with `iceberg_metadata_compression_method = 'zstd'` and `output_format_compression_level = 22`, then check `memory_usage < 500000000` in `system.query_log`. Before the fix this is about 876 MB.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130231
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/126418

comment.body:
Acknowledged. I'm investigating the full-size zstd context allocated for Iceberg metadata writes (`writeMessageToFile` and `IcebergRESTCatalogStorage`); I'll follow up here with a PR (or my findings) shortly.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130316

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view queried by its own definer is no longer read as an opaque step, so the optimizations of the query apply to it again, as before 26.10 (for example, `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` reads in order through it). Other users, and sessions of the definer that are limited by the `GRANTS` of their authentication method or use other roles, still read such a view sealed, and such sessions of the definer no longer bypass the check that hides its plan in `EXPLAIN`.

### Description

On 26.10, `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` over a `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view that filters rows reads the whole table: 3,001,000 rows instead of 43,688 in #130316. Since #122330, every `DEFINER` / `NONE` view that can hide rows is read through the opaque `ReadFromSealedView` step, so read-in-order, top-N and the outer predicate for index analysis cannot see through it. The seal keeps hidden rows away from the invoker, but in the report the invoker is the definer.

`StorageView::isReadByDefiner` holds when the query runs with exactly the identity of the view's own query: an initial query of the definer (compared by UUID), with the definer's default roles (current and external), no `GRANTS` limit from the authentication method, and no row policy on the view itself. Such a query can read everything the view hides, so `readImpl` and the `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` pushdown into views no longer seal the view for it. The same check replaces the name-only definer shortcut that decides whether `EXPLAIN` shows the hidden plan. Secondary queries, other users, other role sets and `NONE` views stay sealed. The parallel-replicas carrier, the `Distributed` pushdown and `analyzer_inline_views` keep the structural check.

Reverting #122330 is not proposed: it would reopen the row leak it fixed.

Validation on a debug build: the issue's query reads 43,688 rows as the definer (3,001,000 on master) and still 3,001,000 as another user. The new test fails on master, and each of the six conditions was removed in a separate build, each caught by the test. All 58 tests with `DEFINER` / `NONE` views pass; 05257, 05407 and 05331 now test the sealed path through a non-definer or a `NONE` view. A performance test is added.

delta-kernel-rs and chdig are built as members of the Rust workspace in `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace`, with one `Cargo.lock`, one cargo target directory and features resolved once for all members, so the crates they share with the other Rust libraries are compiled once, in one parallel cargo run.

### Description

Step 3 of the layout in #86562, after #130348 (step 2).

- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs-cmake` and `contrib/chdig-cmake` get one-line wrapper crates (`pub use delta_kernel_ffi;`, `pub use chdig;`), imported through the workspace manifest like the other six.
- One environment for every member (`clickhouse_config_crate_env`: OpenSSL variables, `CFLAGS` with `-I contrib/openssl/include`, `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): build scripts track their environment, so any difference rebuilds shared crates every build.
- `resolver.feature-unification = "workspace"`: corrosion runs one `cargo rustc` per package, and cargo otherwise resolves features per package.
- The workspace manifest is also a root package, `_ch_rust_workspace`, with one feature per member. `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace/CMakeLists.txt` builds it with the enabled members' features before their runs, which then compile only their wrapper. Not with LTO, where each member's run does its own code generation. The wrappers are plain libraries imported with `OVERRIDE_CRATE_TYPE <crate>=staticlib`, so the root run writes no unused archives.
- `Cargo.lock` is resolved offline from `contrib/rust_vendor` (no `rust_vendor` change); delta-kernel-rs and chdig take the workspace's semver-compatible versions.
- The `aws-lc-sys` `LDFLAGS` workaround goes: the crate left the graph.
- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` moves to the merge commit of ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#22: the pin of #130062 plus `crate-type = ["lib"]`.

Rust-only cold build, `-j48`: Debug 200 s / 1027 s CPU on master, 108 s / 779 s here. With ThinLTO 13.2 min on master, 18.4 min here: the members' LTO runs queue on the one target directory.

Validation, x86_64 Debug:
- 1240 compile units in 3 target directories before, 799 in one after, no crate built with two feature sets.
- Build and link pass; a no-op build compiles nothing, also alternating between members; the member archives are the same cargo units as without the root package.
- Delta Lake stateless tests 77/77; prql, pco, polyglot, vortex and wasm tests 98/99 (the other fails on master too); `chdig --help` works.

issue.title: 26.10: `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` over a `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view reads the whole table (regression from #122330)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Query plan optimization: physical plan steps, plan-level rewrites and optimizations (QueryPlan pa...

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Regression found by chReplay production query replay

issue.body:
Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122330

### Description

SELECT * ... ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 15 over a SQL SECURITY DEFINER view (UNION ALL of MergeTree branches that filter on the first sorting-key column) is about 4.7x slower in 26.10 and reads every row. The view is now planned as ReadFromSealedView, so read-in-order/top-N on the base table's sorting key no longer applies. A SQL SECURITY INVOKER view runs at the same speed on both versions.

Regression between `26.8.1.667` (OLD) and `26.10.2.142` (NEW).

### How to reproduce

Run the setup once, then measure only the SELECT on each version.

```sql
CREATE TABLE default.t1 (c1 String, c2 String, c3 String, c4 String, c5 DateTime, c6 String DEFAULT '', c7 Map(String, String), c8 Array(Float32) DEFAULT [], INDEX i1 c1 TYPE bloom_filter(0.0001) GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (c2, c5);
INSERT INTO default.t1 (c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c7, c8) SELECT concat('m', toString(number)), 'a', 'u1', repeat('c', 200), toDateTime('2026-01-01 00:00:00') + number, map('k1', toString(number % 1000), 'k2', repeat('x', 200)), [toFloat32(number), 1.0, 2.0, 3.0] FROM numbers(3000000);
INSERT INTO default.t1 (c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c7) SELECT concat('n', toString(number)), 'b', 'u2', 'x', toDateTime('2026-01-01 00:00:00') + number, map('k3', 'z') FROM numbers(1000);
CREATE VIEW default.v1 (c1 String, c2 String, c3 String, c4 String, c5 DateTime, c6 String, c7 Map(String, String), c8 Array(Float32), c9 DateTime) DEFINER = default SQL SECURITY DEFINER AS SELECT *, c5 AS c9 FROM default.t1 WHERE c2 = 'a' UNION ALL SELECT *, c5 AS c9 FROM default.t1 WHERE (c2 = 'b') AND (c7['k3'] = 'z');
WITH w1 AS (SELECT * FROM default.v1) SELECT * FROM w1 ORDER BY c9 DESC LIMIT 15
SETTINGS compatibility = '25.8', max_threads = '8';
```

### Performance

Original query (milliseconds; SQL omitted):

| OLD 26.8.1.667 | NEW 26.10.2.142 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 903 | 1813 | 2.01× |

Synthetic repro above (milliseconds):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 | 61 | 4.69× |

Synthetic repro above, read rows of the SELECT (`system.query_log`):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 43,688 | 3,001,000 | 68.69× |

Synthetic repro above, peak memory in bytes of the SELECT (`system.query_log`):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 54,307,113 | 86,463,120 | 1.59× |

### Expected behavior

As in 26.8: the LIMIT with ORDER BY on the sorting-key time column should use read-in-order inside the view branches and read only a few granules (about 44k rows instead of 3M).

### Additional reproducers

Other findings with the same cause show it in different query shapes (87 findings with their own bisect, on 8 workloads). Each repro is self-contained: run the setup once, then measure only the last `SELECT`.

#### The outer `WHERE` is not pushed into a `FINAL` read under a `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view

Selecting from a `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view (here over `ReplacingMergeTree ... FINAL`) no longer pushes the outer WHERE into the view. EXPLAIN shows `ReadFromSealedView` with no partition, primary-key or skip-index pruning, so the whole table is scanned with FINAL. On the original data the query went from 26 ms to more than 200 s (timeout). The same view with SQL SECURITY INVOKER is unaffected.

```sql
CREATE TABLE default.t1 (c1 String, c2 String, c3 String, c4 LowCardinality(String), c5 DateTime64(3), c6 String, c7 Nullable(String), c8 DateTime64(3), c9 UInt8, INDEX i1 c2 TYPE bloom_filter() GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(c8, c9) PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(c5) PRIMARY KEY (c3, c4, toDate(c5)) ORDER BY (c3, c4, toDate(c5), c1);
INSERT INTO default.t1 SELECT toString(number), hex(intHash64(intDiv(number, 10))), concat('p', toString(number % 5)), 'A', toDateTime64('2026-05-01 00:00:00', 3) + toIntervalSecond(intDiv(number * 3, 1)), concat('n', toString(number % 100)), repeat('x', 200), toDateTime64('2026-05-01 00:00:00', 3), 0 FROM numbers(6000000);
CREATE VIEW default.v1 DEFINER = default SQL SECURITY DEFINER AS SELECT o.* FROM default.t1 AS o FINAL;
SELECT c1, c6, substring(ifNull(c7, ''), 1, 1200) FROM default.v1 WHERE c3 = 'p1' AND c5 >= '2026-05-20 00:00:00' AND c5 <= '2026-05-20 00:15:00' AND c2 = hex(intHash64(toUInt64(533000)))
SETTINGS compatibility = '25.12';
```

| | OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Query time, ms | 4 | 116 | 29.00× |
| Read rows | 0 | 8,497,092 | — |
| Selected marks | 0 | 737 | — |

#### A `WHERE` on a `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view no longer prunes partitions or primary-key ranges

A WHERE filter on a view declared with SQL SECURITY DEFINER no longer prunes partitions or primary-key ranges of the underlying MergeTree table. NEW reads every part where OLD reads 1 part / 64 marks. On the original data it is about 17-80x slower, with peak memory 254 MiB → 912 MiB. The same view without SQL SECURITY DEFINER prunes normally on both versions.

```sql
CREATE TABLE default.t1 (`c0` DateTime64(3), `ts` DateTime64(3), `k` LowCardinality(String), `v1` Nullable(Float32)) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(c0) PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(ts) ORDER BY (k, ts);
INSERT INTO default.t1 SELECT toDateTime64('2025-01-01 00:00:00', 3) + number, toDateTime64('2025-01-01 00:00:00', 3) + intDiv(number, 50) * 150, concat('k', toString(number % 50)), number % 1000 FROM numbers(24000000);
CREATE VIEW default.v1 DEFINER = default SQL SECURITY DEFINER AS SELECT t.ts AS ts, t.v1 AS v1, t.k AS k FROM default.t1 AS t FINAL;
SELECT count() FROM default.v1 WHERE ts >= toDateTime64('2025-03-01 00:00:00', 3) AND ts <= toDateTime64('2025-03-08 00:00:00', 3)
SETTINGS compatibility = '25.4';
```

| | OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Selected marks | 64 | 2,941 | 45.95× |
| Read rows | 524,288 | 24,000,000 | 45.78× |
| Query time, ms | 5 | 36 | 7.20× |

comment.body:
I opened #130552. A `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view is no longer read through the opaque `ReadFromSealedView` step when the query runs with exactly the identity of the view's own query: the definer, with its default roles, as an initial query, without a `GRANTS` limit from the authentication method, and with no row policy on the view. With it, the query from the description reads 43,688 rows as `default` (3,001,000 on master), and in the second reproducer `v_final` read by its definer reads 2,230,554 rows, the same as `v_final_invoker`.

Other readers still read such a view sealed (in the second reproducer, 10,000,000 rows for a user with only `SELECT` on `v_final`): the seal is what keeps the rows the view hides away from them. The regression comes from #122330. I don't propose reverting it, because that would reopen the row leak through these views that it fixed.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Install `pigz` in the `clickhouse/binary-builder` image, so the release build jobs compress their `.tgz` packages in parallel.

### Description

`packages/build` already compresses the `.tgz` tarballs with `pigz` when `/usr/bin/pigz` exists, else with `tar -czf`. The `Build Packages` step of `Build (amd_release)` / `Build (arm_release)` runs inside `clickhouse/binary-builder`, which does not install `pigz` (checked in the current master image `16143eb26bdf0bdb2f00_amd`), so every tarball is compressed by single-threaded `gzip`. The four tarballs took 60 s of the 69 s step in [a PR `arm_release` job](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/42315009375/job/128354633601), and 248 s of 282 s in a [master `amd_release` job](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/42598309267).

This PR adds `pigz` to the image's package list. Nothing else changes. This PR's own `Build (amd_release)` / `Build (arm_release)` do not exercise it: they are reused from the CI cache, because the build-job digests do not include the `binary-builder` image digest (`ci/praktika/digest.py`).

Validation, locally on the master `26.11.1.1733` packages with the same `pigz` 2.8, `gzip` 1.12 and GNU tar 1.35 as the image, median of 3 runs on 16 cores:
- `clickhouse-common-static` (746 MB): `gzip` 25.0 s, `pigz` 2.1 s (1.4 s on 32 cores, the size of the `m8g.8xlarge` runner).
- `clickhouse-common-static-dbg` (4.1 GB): `gzip` 117.8 s, `pigz` 12.7 s (7.2 s on 32 cores).

The decompressed tar streams are byte-identical to `gzip`'s, `sha512sum -c` passes, and BusyBox `tar xzf` in Alpine (the path of the Alpine server and keeper images) extracts the same files. The tarballs are about 0.1% smaller. Their bytes and `.sha512` differ from `gzip`'s, but do not depend on the number of cores.

Reported in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130064#issuecomment-6740954794.

issue.title: Reject `input` in `INSERT ... RETURNING`

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Runtime execution pipeline, processors, vectorized operators, resource management during execution.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
Reject the `input` table function inside the `RETURNING` query before building the insert pipeline. Reuse the existing recursive scanner so the check also covers scalar subqueries and CTEs. The supported `INSERT ... RETURNING ... SELECT ... FROM input` path is unchanged.

An `input` behind a view or a SQL UDF is not in the query text, so `Context::initializeInput` also rejects a second read of the input with `INVALID_USAGE_OF_INPUT` instead of a `LOGICAL_ERROR`. The server sets the input initializer and the blocks reader together and resets only the initializer once `input` is read, so a blocks reader without an initializer means the insert has already read the input. Without the blocks reader, a missing initializer is still a `LOGICAL_ERROR`.

`executeQueryImpl` retains input callbacks for `RETURNING`, because the insert may receive its data separately. However, the existing input-function check only scans the insert's source `SELECT`. An `input` inside `RETURNING` can therefore reach `Context::initializeInput` without an initializer, or initiate another input exchange while the client expects a result.

Validated the narrow patch on the reusable `Debug` build based on `ce534743bf1a9469c520f6fa4e1d5ef959936efb` (`26.11.1.1`). Without the fix, the local reproducer aborts on a logical exception in `Context::initializeInput`, and so does the server on the view case. With the fix, the direct, scalar-subquery, CTE, view and parameterized-view cases return `INVALID_USAGE_OF_INPUT` and leave the table empty. A valid local insert using `input` with rows supplied through stdin returns `2, 5` for the count and sum both before and after the fix.

The new functional test and seven existing tests pass: `05453_insert_returning_reject_input`, `05401_insert_returning`, `05402_insert_returning_client`, `05407_insert_returning_explain_subcolumns`, `05441_insert_returning_access`, `05442_insert_returning_local_infile`, `02249_insert_select_from_input_schema_inference`, and `03380_input_async_insert`. The existing tests cover the supported TCP/HTTP, stdin, local, file-input, access-check and schema-inference paths. The C++ style check is clean.

The test sets `send_table_structure_on_insert_with_inline_data = 1` for the view cases, so the insert reads the data the client sends separately. With `0` the server parses the `VALUES` itself, the view is the first reader of the input, and the client gets `Unknown packet 11`, as for `INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM v` on master. `05453` passed 12 of 12 runs with randomized settings, and `03005_input_function_in_join` and `00952_input_function` also pass.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127722
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126476

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The hash tables of large hash `JOIN`s no longer switch to the Robin Hood mode by default (it was enabled in 26.10). This makes joins with random keys up to 1.8 times faster, but the hash table takes up to 1.75 times more memory and joins on dense keys can be up to 1.3 times slower. The new setting `enable_robin_hood_hash_for_joins` turns the mode back on.


### Description

Since #125001 (in 26.10), a bucket of a large hash join table switches to the Robin Hood mode at 2^16 cells and then fills up to 0.9 instead of 0.5 before it doubles, so a right table above about 8.4M keys takes up to two times less memory. This PR turns that off by default for joins and adds `enable_robin_hood_hash_for_joins` to turn it on (`compatibility` 26.10 or older turns it on). Aggregation and `uniqExact` are unchanged.

The grower gets a per-table switch that allows the Robin Hood mode; `HashJoin` sets it from the setting when it creates its maps. Since the unified hash join, this covers every hash join that splits its hash table into parts (`hash_join_layout`); one-part tables, grace hash buckets and `StorageJoin` never use the mode.

Measured with the CI release build of da4f7d3 (8M-128M right rows, 8 and 32 threads, sweep in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128012#issuecomment-6773961553), time with the mode on relative to off: `intHash64` keys with half of the left keys missing 1.06-1.80x whenever the Robin Hood table is filled above 0.5, 0.86-0.94x when it is not; dense keys and the `right_full_hash_join_nullmaps` shape mostly 0.79-0.92x; peak memory 0.57-0.59x when the table is smaller. With the mode off, a join near the `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join` limit spills to grace hash sooner.

Extends `05345_robin_hood_large_hash_tables` (both modes, checked by their memory usage) and `parallel_hash_join_various.xml` (`left_large_right`, `left_large_right_dense`), and adds `hash_join_robin_hood.xml`: both modes for `UInt64`, `String` and two-column keys at a fill of 0.83, where the Robin Hood mode is the slowest.

- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
When `http_forbid_headers` forbids `Authorization`, Basic credentials that would be sent in that header are now refused too: the userinfo of `url`, `urlCluster` and `URL` table URLs (including url wildcards and `web` disks), `credentials` of `HTTP` dictionaries created by DDL, the userinfo of `format_avro_schema_registry_url`, and `user`/`password` of the `Elasticsearch` engine. Before, only an explicit `Authorization` header was refused.

### Description

On 26.8.18.2, 26.9.19.9 and 26.10.2.103, with `<http_forbid_headers><header>Authorization</header></http_forbid_headers>`, `url(..., headers('Authorization' = ...))` is refused, but `url('http://user:password@host/...')` still sends `Authorization: Basic ...`: the credentials parsed from the userinfo are turned into that header in `ReadWriteBufferFromHTTP::prepareRequest`, after the explicit headers and never through `HTTPHeaderFilter`.

This adopts the request-time design of @ kolsha's draft #128998: `HTTPHeaderFilter::checkBasicCredentials` / `checkURIUserInfo` check a synthetic `Authorization` header with the existing filter, in `setCredentialsFromURL` (every URL-userinfo sender), each request of a DDL `HTTP` dictionary, and each schema registry request. A forbidden failover option fails the read instead of being skipped. Credentials with an empty username send nothing and are not refused, except by the schema registry, which sends any userinfo. Stored `URL` and `Elasticsearch` tables stay attached after the header is forbidden, and a loaded `HTTP` dictionary is refused on its next update; only requests are refused. Admin-only senders (interserver credentials, XML dictionaries) are unchanged.

Added on top of #128998: the `HTTP` dictionary is checked per request instead of when its source is created, the initiator of `urlCluster` checks every URL before a worker gets it (a worker checks it under its own configuration, which can differ), the same check for `Elasticsearch` `user`/`password`, and tests for the `web` disk read, `web_index` metadata and `AvroConfluent` output paths. This PR supersedes the draft #128998.

Validation: integration tests in `test_storage_url`, `test_disk_over_web_server` and `test_storage_elasticsearch`; the 16 forbidden-header cases fail on master and pass with the fix, the empty-username and redirect cases pass on both.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`LEFT ARRAY JOIN` is faster when no joined array is empty: `emptyArrayToSingle` now returns its argument as is instead of copying it row by row, which makes the `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` query of the `array_join` performance test about 1.6x faster.

### Description

`Performance Comparison (amd_release, master_head, 6/6)` on #128472, which only changes Iceberg manifest writing, flagged `array_join #1` (`LEFT ARRAY JOIN` of two one-element arrays over 10M rows) at +15%, confirmed after restart: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=128472&sha=7d3c4efb51731de1f1f13b27344be6f8e4645e81&name_0=PR&name_1=Performance%20Comparison%20%28amd_release%2C%20master_head%2C%206%2F6%29).

An aligned `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` runs `emptyArrayToSingle` over every joined array. The function always rebuilt the column one row at a time, a `PODArray::resize` and an out-of-line `memcpy` call per row, even when no array is empty and the result equals the input. That copy is the whole gap between `#1` (0.112 s on master) and the inner `ARRAY JOIN` `#0` over the same data (0.058 s). In the job's CPU profile all extra time of the PR binary is in this loop (self +30%, its `memcpy` calls +76%), while `executeImpl` is byte-identical in both binaries, only at another address: a per-row call loop that is sensitive to code placement.

Now `emptyArrayToSingle` checks the offsets once (`std::adjacent_find`, stopping at the first empty array) and returns its argument when no array is empty. Columns are copy-on-write, and `executeConst` already returns its argument for the same case.

Validation: local RelWithDebInfo A/B, 10 interleaved rounds of 11 runs, 8 threads: `#1` 0.1015 -> 0.0620 s (1.65x); `#0` and a column with one empty array per block stay within noise (0.98x, 1.00x). `00206_empty_array_to_single` gains queries for every element type path, `Nullable`, `LowCardinality`, nested arrays, an empty array only in the last row, a `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` mixing both cases, and a `Map`; its new reference comes from the unchanged binary, and fast paths with either condition removed fail it.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `SELECT ... LIMIT 0` from a MergeTree table no longer runs the primary key and skip index analysis, which took up to seconds on large tables with a filter on the key. Such a query reads nothing, so `max_rows_to_read` and `max_partitions_to_read` no longer reject it. Closes #125812.

### Description

On the table of #125812 (244141 marks, `WHERE c2` on a `UInt8` primary key column, which #89603 turned into a key condition), `SELECT c1, c4 FROM t WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2 LIMIT 0` runs a 41053-step primary key exclusion search, although `LIMIT 0` takes no row.

`optimizePrimaryKeyConditionAndLimit` already passes `limit + offset` of the first `LIMIT` above a read to the read, and `ReadFromMergeTree` ignored it. When that is 0 and the `LIMIT` does not read till end (`exact_rows_before_limit`, totals), the read is now marked, and `selectRangesToRead` returns after partition pruning, statistics pruning and sampling, with no ranges. The read then builds the empty pipe it builds for any read that selects nothing. `force_primary_key`, `force_index_by_date`, `force_data_skipping_indices` and SAMPLE validation still run. The return precedes the query condition cache, which records the granules missing from a selection as not matching. Parallel replicas, `make_distributed_plan` and forced or preferred projections keep the analysis.

Behaviour change: such a query reads nothing, so `max_rows_to_read` and `max_partitions_to_read` no longer reject it, the table's `max_concurrent_queries` no longer counts it (as for any read below `min_marks_to_honor_max_concurrent_queries`), and `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` shows no primary key or skip index entry for it.

Validation (RelWithDebInfo base vs fix, the issue's 2B-row table, warm medians): the issue's query with `compatibility = '25.12'` 24.5 -> 2.0 ms, without it 14.5 -> 2.0 ms; `LIMIT 10` (16 ms) and `count()` (79 vs 80 ms) unchanged. The new performance test through `perf.py`: 18.3 -> 3.0 ms and 29.5 -> 3.6 ms. The new stateless test covers the kept checks, the query condition cache, projections, `FINAL` and a cloned sealed-view plan; dropping the `exact_rows_before_limit` term, the forced skip index check, the projection terms or the `clone()` copy, or letting the empty selection reach the query condition cache, makes it fail.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

issue.body:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/54775
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/74430
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50692
Depends on: https://github.com/ClickHouse/AMQP-CPP/pull/9 and the submodule bump that follows it (see "Dependency" below)

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixes `RabbitMQ` tables that silently stop consuming, with `DROP TABLE` hanging until a restart, when inserts fall far behind the broker (about 1 million messages with default settings, 100000 with a small `rabbitmq_max_block_size`). ClickHouse now limits how many unacknowledged messages RabbitMQ sends at once.

### Description
The consumer sets no `basic.qos`, so RabbitMQ pushes every ready message into a bounded queue of `max(100000, block size)` entries (block size: `rabbitmq_max_block_size`, or `max_insert_block_size / rabbitmq_num_consumers` = 1048449 by default). Once inserts are that far behind, the libuv delivery callback blocks in `push()` while `streamToViews`, the only thread that drains the queue, waits for the loop task to return: consumption stops without any error in the log and `DROP TABLE` hangs in `shutdown()`. In production this hits as soon as inserts fall behind under load: consumption stops without any error, `DROP TABLE` hangs, and only a server restart recovers. Because of this we had to build our own ingestion system instead of using the RabbitMQ engine.

Fix:
1. Non-global `basic.qos` per subscription, `clamp(queue_size / num_queues, 1, 65535)` (65535 unless there are several queues). A channel then has at most `num_queues * prefetch_count <= queue_size` deliveries outstanding, so `received` never fills and the delivery callback never waits for space.
2. Ack messages that produce no rows, so they cannot hold prefetch slots forever.
3. End a block once the channel's prefetch window is used up and nothing is pending, instead of waiting for the flush interval. The window counts messages an earlier reader of the pooled consumer left unacked (a direct `SELECT`); if they hold all of it, the block acks them, as the next block does on master.

**Dependency.** With the AMQP-CPP currently pinned, one `basic.nack` (a failed insert into a view, `SYSTEM STOP/CANCEL` during a block) makes AMQP-CPP queue every later ack without sending it (#76163). On master that gives duplicates; with a prefetch window the broker stops after 65535 unacked messages and the table stalls until it reconnects. Measured: one failing message, then 70000 messages:

| binary | AMQP-CPP | consumed |
|---|---|---|
| master | 4fccd7f (pin) | 70000 of 70000 |
| this PR | 4fccd7f (pin) | stops at 65535 (broker: 65535 unacked, 0 acks) |
| this PR | c0049e0 (AMQP-CPP#9) | 70000 of 70000 |

So this PR should merge after AMQP-CPP#9 and its submodule bump.

Behaviour changes:
- A block ends after at most `prefetch_count` messages per consumer (65535, or `queue_size / num_queues` with several queues, documented), so a large `rabbitmq_max_block_size` can give more, smaller parts. Draining a 300000-message backlog with default settings takes the same time as on master (8.5–8.9 s vs 8.8–8.9 s, 7 parts each, 3 runs each).
- A direct `SELECT` without `rabbitmq_commit_on_select` still leaves what it read unacked, as on master, and a view's next block acks it. Without a view, `prefetch_count` (up to 65535) such reads use up the window until the connection is re-established.
- The window makes a pre-existing lost wake-up in `waitForMessages` likelier: with `rabbitmq_flush_interval_ms = 0` a block can sleep until the next delivery or the sanity timeout. Fixed in a follow-up PR.

Tests: five new integration tests pass with the fix at `3a227d8e483` (3 of 3 runs each after merging master with #125105, 10 of 10 before). Four fail on current master; the fifth, a window held entirely by direct `SELECT`s, fails on `ed652fa8d` and passes on master, which has no window. Before the merge, the rest of `test_storage_rabbitmq` passed on a minimal local build, except two tests that need Arrow or the JSON type and failed on master too.

Repro, one minute on the official 26.9 image: https://gist.github.com/comino/349122b3f425d277569c08187289852f

<details><summary>Stacks and design notes</summary>

Stacks while stuck (`system.stack_trace`, official 26.9.12.8, shortened):
```
loop thread:      pthread_cond_wait <- RabbitMQConsumer::subscribe()::$_1 <- … <- AMQP::DeferredReceiver::process <- uv_run <- RabbitMQHandler::startLoop
streaming thread: mutex::lock <- BackgroundSchedulePoolTaskInfo::deactivate <- StorageRabbitMQ::streamToViews
DROP TABLE:       mutex::lock <- StorageRabbitMQ::shutdown <- InterpreterDropQuery::executeToTableImpl
```

- QoS is non-global because global QoS is deprecated and rejected by quorum and stream queues.
- No new settings and no queue or exchange declaration changes, so existing tables and queues keep working.
- Side effect: without `basic.qos`, RabbitMQ caps quorum-queue consumers at 2000 unacked messages; with an explicit prefetch a 20000-message quorum backlog drained in 8 s instead of 56 s (RabbitMQ 4, `rabbitmq_flush_interval_ms = 5000`).
- Tests: `test_rabbitmq_backlog_larger_than_received_queue`, `test_rabbitmq_empty_messages_are_acked` (waits for the ack in the log), `test_rabbitmq_block_ends_when_prefetch_is_used_up`, `test_rabbitmq_view_acks_messages_a_select_left_unacked`, `test_rabbitmq_view_acks_a_window_selects_left_unacked`.
</details>

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `DeltaLake` queries hanging forever, without reacting to `KILL QUERY`, when delta-kernel could not create the thread that hands a result back (for example at a container PID limit).


### Description

On 26.3.12.3, a `DeltaLake` query hangs forever and ignores `KILL QUERY` when the server cannot create a new thread: in #128033 a `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = DeltaLake` run by `DDLWorker` blocked for 26 hours at a Kubernetes PID limit and stalled the distributed DDL queue. Master and 26.8 to 26.10 pin the same kernel code.

Cause: delta-kernel's `block_on` handed every result back through `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. When no thread can be created, tokio panics after queueing the closure that owns the result sender, so the sender is never dropped and the caller's `recv()` waits forever. Every synchronous kernel call goes through `block_on`.

Change: `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` moves from `88ff5a94` to `86762ee5`, the merge commit of ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#19 (a cherry-pick of delta-io/delta-kernel-rs#3202), which sends the result directly from the async task. It touches only `kernel/src/engine/default/executor.rs`, with no Cargo manifest or lock change. The fork branch tip carries unrelated changes, so the pin is the fix commit, not the tip.

Validation: a standalone kernel program that lowers `RLIMIT_NPROC` before calling `block_on` hangs on `88ff5a94` (panic `OS can't spawn worker thread`, caller blocked in `futex_wait`) and returns the result on `86762ee5`, in 6 of 6 runs each. The server builds with the new pin, and 59 local DeltaLake stateless tests pass. No ClickHouse test is added: running a server out of threads at exactly this point is not deterministic in a functional test.

#130062 moves the pointer to `c694ca3e`, which already contains this commit.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`INSERT INTO FUNCTION viewIfPermitted(... ELSE f(...))` now requires the write grant of `f` (for example `WRITE ON URL`), as an insert into `f` directly does. Before, only the read grant was checked, so a user with `READ ON URL` and no `WRITE ON URL` could make the server send an insert to a URL. Also fixed `Logical error: 'Unexpected table function name: viewIfPermitted'` when reading through the `ELSE` function with parallel replicas enabled; reading through an explicit cluster function after `ELSE` (`urlCluster`, `s3Cluster`, ...) now fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

### Description

Reported privately; there is no public issue.

On 26.3.60.2 and 26.10.2.103, a user with `READ ON URL` but no `WRITE ON URL` is refused `INSERT INTO FUNCTION url(...)`, yet the same insert through `viewIfPermitted(SELECT ... ELSE url(...))` succeeds when the user cannot run the `SELECT`, and the server sends the rows to the URL. This is the wrong privilege on a request the server originates; the destination's own authentication still applies.

`TableFunctionViewIfPermitted::executeImpl` passed `is_insert_query` to the structure lookup of the `ELSE` function but not to its `execute`, so `ITableFunction::execute` checked `READ` instead of `WRITE` on its source; every `ELSE` function with a source grant (`file`, `s3`, ...) goes through this call. It is now forwarded, as `loop` does for its inner function. The structure check from #116793 stays a read check.

Under parallel replicas, `parallel_replicas_for_cluster_engines` also turned the `ELSE` `url` into a `*Cluster` storage, which cannot rewrite a query that names `viewIfPermitted` and failed with a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (26.3.60.2, 26.10.2.103; an abort in debug builds), hit in [`Stateless tests (arm_binary, ParallelReplicas, s3 storage, parallel)`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=129756&sha=adff553c61e5df82002bb6e5ff710fe6117d0292&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20ParallelReplicas%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29). The `ELSE` function now runs with that setting disabled. An explicit `*Cluster` function after `ELSE` has the same problem (`urlCluster` and `fileCluster` fail the same way, `s3Cluster` edits the arguments of `viewIfPermitted`), so reading one now fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

Validation: the new test (insert denied with only `READ ON URL`, allowed with `WRITE ON URL`; `SELECT` through the fallback allowed, also with parallel replicas; `urlCluster` after `ELSE` rejected) fails 50/50 on master and passes 30/30 with randomized settings; its `urlCluster` case aborts master's debug build.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed partition pruning of `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` on `ReplicatedMergeTree` when the predicate computes a function named like a stored column, for example ``toYYYYMM(d) = 202401 AND `toYYYYMM(d)` = 7``: a partition was skipped, or the `ALTER` failed with `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` when the column and the function have different types.


### Description
On 26.10.2.103 and 26.9.25.15 this `ALTER` succeeds but leaves the row (#130256):
```sql
CREATE TABLE t (d Date, `toYYYYMM(d)` UInt32) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{database}/t', '1') PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(d) ORDER BY tuple();
INSERT INTO t VALUES ('2024-01-01', 7);
ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE toYYYYMM(d) = 202401 AND `toYYYYMM(d)` = 7 SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2;
SELECT count() FROM t; -- 1, expected 0
```
With a `String` column of that name and ``length(`toYYYYMM(d)`) = 1``, it fails with `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` on 26.10.2.103 (without pruning, the row is deleted).

The mutation pruning DAG uses plain names, and the planner reuses a node by name. With the function first, the column reference `` `toYYYYMM(d)` `` resolves to the function node: the #130196 check in `KeyCondition` sees no input of that name, so the two atoms contradict on the partition key; with different types, building the DAG throws.

The change: before the DAG is built, if a function of the resolved predicate has the action name of a storage column, pruning is skipped and all partitions are mutated, as with `optimize_mutations_with_partition_pruning = 0`. The cost: on such a table, `DELETE WHERE toYYYYMM(d) = 202401` is no longer pruned. #125723 (mine, open) fixes the naming in the planner itself, mutation filter included.

Not covered: the mutation execution side (a part where only some rows match, `ALTER UPDATE`, lightweight `DELETE` still keep the rows, with or without pruning) and statistics part pruning in `SELECT`. On 26.9 and 26.10 the example's row stays even without pruning; master deletes it.

The fix and the test come from #130301, handed over by its author; his commits keep him as author.

05616 fails on master (`0 1 1`, then `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`) and passes 50/50 randomized runs with the change.

Mutation partition pruning builds its predicate DAG with plain names, so a column named like a predicate function (`toYYYYMM(d)`) is merged into that function node and `ALTER DELETE` skips a matching partition; the change skips mutation pruning when a function node of that DAG is named like a storage column.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `system.licenses` in official builds: `pdqsort` was missing, and `libxml2`, `rapidjson` and `sz3` showed the license file of a test fixture or a bundled tool instead of the library's own license.

### Description

On 26.10.3.7 (also 26.8 and 26.3), `SELECT license_path FROM system.licenses WHERE library_name = 'libxml2'` returns `/contrib/libxml2/test/html-tokenizer/NOTICE`, the notice of an html5lib test fixture, instead of `/contrib/libxml2/Copyright`. `rapidjson` shows `contrib/natvis/LICENSE` (a debugger visualizer, the file behind the warning fixed in #99909), `sz3` shows `tools/pysz/LICENSE`, and `pdqsort` has no row although it is compiled in.

`list-licenses.sh` picks the license file with an awk program that relies on `IGNORECASE`, which only GNU awk supports. The builder image (Ubuntu 24.04) has mawk, where `/LICENSE/`, `/COPY/` and `/NOTICE/` are case-sensitive, so a lowercase top-level `license.txt` or `Copyright` is never chosen: a deeper upper-case file wins, or nothing matches. The program now upper-cases the file name with `toupper` and matches on the basename only, which is POSIX awk. Matching the basename also fixes GNU awk on a checkout path containing "license", where every candidate matched and configure failed with `sources with unknown license found in aws-c-s3`.

Validation: the script output is byte-identical under gawk, mawk, busybox awk and `gawk --posix`, for a plain path and a path containing "license", and equals today's gawk output, so gawk builds do not change; official builds gain the `pdqsort` row and 3 corrected rows (`rapidjson` becomes `BSD`, as in gawk builds). `01276_system_licenses` gains the `libxml2` and `pdqsort` rows (`rapidjson` and `sz3` are not checked out in Fast test): 50/50 OK on a mawk-configured build, FAIL on the CI master binary of the same commit.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):


### Description

Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126184#discussion_r4293581009: `maskedURL` in `MetadataStorageFromIndexPages.cpp` duplicated `maskedURI` in `ReadWriteBufferFromHTTP.cpp`.

`src/Common/maskURIPassword.h` gets `[[nodiscard]] std::string maskURICredentials(std::string_view)`, the existing in-place masking applied to a copy. It replaces both helpers and five more places that copied a URL and masked the copy by hand: `WriteBufferFromHTTP`, `HTTPException::makeExceptionMessage`, `StorageURL`'s `getLastFilePath`, `HTTPConnectionPool` and `AvroConfluentSchemaRegistry`. The last two called `maskURIUserinfo` and `maskPresignedURLParameters` directly, so they would have missed anything added to `maskURICredentials` later. A non-const `std::string` lvalue still resolves to the in-place `bool` overload, so the in-place callers are unchanged; const lvalues and rvalues get the copy. `[[nodiscard]]` makes a call that expects in-place masking of a const string a build error.

No behaviour change. `05212_http_uri_credentials_masked`, `05404_http_error_body_presigned_credentials_scrubbed` and `05315_avro_schema_registry_url_credentials_masked` (50 randomized runs each) and the two `test_storage_url` index page tests pass. ### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `FINAL` query on a table whose row policy compares `ORDER BY` columns with a value computed once per query, such as `currentUser()`, `now()` or an `IN (subquery)` set, applies the policy before the merge again, as in 26.8, instead of reading and merging every row first. Closes #130317.

### Description

Since 26.9 a row policy like `c2 = substring(currentUser(), 1, 3)` on an `ORDER BY` column is applied after `FINAL`, and PREWHERE with it, so the whole table is read and merged before the policy filters it. On the query in #130317 this costs 9.7x memory and 2.7x time with the same result. Policies using `now()`, `currentDatabase()` or `IN (subquery)` are deferred too.

#117248 added `node->isDeterministic()` to `isNodeDeterministic`, the gate of `isRowPolicyDeferredAfterFinal`. For a `COLUMN` node it returns `is_deterministic_constant`, which the analyzer sets to false for a constant folded from a non-deterministic function. Applying the policy before `FINAL` only needs every version of one key to get the same verdict, and a constant has one value for the whole query, so it cannot split a dedup group. Only a lambda folded into a constant is evaluated per row, and `allNodeFunctions` still checks its body, so the cases #117248 fixed stay deferred (05141, 05182). This PR removes that check; the flag itself stays, the query condition cache needs it. I do not propose reverting #117248: it fixes wrong results (#117016).

On a `GraphiteMergeTree` table such a policy is again applied before the rollup, as a literal policy already is (26.8 behaviour, see #112817).

Validation: new test `05616_row_policy_after_final_query_constant` fails on master (the policy is deferred) and passes 50/50 with random settings, in the parallel-replicas flavour and with `serialize_query_plan = 1`. New performance test `final_row_policy_query_constant`. On the master release build, the issue's data, the `currentUser()` policy (the plan master uses) against the same policy as a literal (the plan this PR restores): 0.093 s / 1.20 GiB against 0.029 s / 288 MiB, and 0.183 s / 3.47 GiB against 0.033 s / 453 MiB with `compatibility = '24.0'` (medians of 10).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issue.body:
### Company or project name

ClickHouse

### Describe what's wrong


When uploading a file to minio in multipart upload in chunks, if the server returns 404 error, ClickHouse keeps retrying. The default retry attempts are configured as 500.  During every retry, Clickhouse logs broken pipe or connection closed errors, and does not recognize 404 error.

404 errors could happen, if there are huge uploads running, which could take more than 24hrs(some config limit), in which case object storage can garbage collect and remove the temporary uploaded files.

 ClickHouse writes the whole body before it reads any response and does not send "Expect: 100-continue", so the   write fails with "Broken pipe" / "Connection reset by peer". It never reads the 404, records the failure as a retryable network error, and retries (s3_retry_attempts + 1)^2 times (the SDK retry loop is nested inside   ClickHouse's own retry loop). With the default s3_retry_attempts = 500 that is 251,001 attempts.


### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes

### How to reproduce

Attached a script, this script downloads clickhouse binary and minio image to setup. Need to docker  installed on the host.

[repro_404_not_seen.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33130297/repro_404_not_seen.sh)

`$export DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock`

2) Run the script "./repro_404_not_seen.sh"

The script will show ClickHouse retrying on 404.  Eventhough the retries=3, total retries are square(3 + 1) which is 16. This is because clickhouse and aws sdk both retry with retry attempts.
