comment.body:
Thanks. Agreed: I'll replace commit 2 of #124557 (reading the early response over plain HTTP after a failed write) with `Expect: 100-continue` support, in a new PR. Commit 1 (no outer retry of an error the SDK has already retried) stays.

One correction: master does not send `Expect: 100-continue` to S3. Since 25.10 (`2fa038920c216`) `ExtendedRequest::IsStreaming()` returns `false`, so the SDK never adds the header (the MinIO audit in the issue shows `Expect header present: False`), and since #116222 `HTTPClientSession::sendRequestHeaders` rejects a request that has it. So the client side has to be implemented, not fixed.

Plan:
1. `sendHTTPRequest`: after the headers, wait for an interim response up to a timeout. `100 Continue` -> send the body. A final status -> that is the response, the body is not sent and the connection is not reused. Timeout -> send the body anyway (RFC 9110, 10.1.1). Nothing is read after a failed write, so HTTPS works the same way.
2. A 404 answered this way goes through the normal S3 error path: `NoSuchUpload` at the first attempt, no retry.
3. Selector: send the header only for a body of at least N bytes (`PutObject`, `UploadPart`); 0 disables it.
4. Remove the plain-HTTP early read, the `broken_s3` early mode and its test.

Question: should the selector default to on for large bodies (for example from 1 MiB, where one extra RTT is small next to the transfer) or to off? With off, this issue keeps the commit 1 bound by default: `s3_retry_attempts + 1` attempts, each one sending the whole part.

The backports requested today (#130424 to 26.8, #130425 to 26.9, `v26.4-must-backport`) carry commit 2 too.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed filters on `toString` of an integer key, such as `toString(key) = '999999999999999999'`, skipping matching rows when one granule (or one `minmax` skip index granule) held integers of 15 or more digits with different numbers of digits. `toString(key) IN (subquery)` (also `CAST(key AS String)`) over an integer or `Date` key uses the primary key again when the subquery returns integers (or dates), as before 26.10. Closes #130315.

### Description

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130315
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/118957

On 26.3, 26.8 and 26.10, `toString(k) = '999999999999999999'` over a `UInt64` key returns 0 instead of 1 when one granule holds 999999999999999999 and 1000000000000000000. `ToStringMonotonicity` compared `floor(log10(x))` in `double`, which gives `n` for `x = 10^n - 1` from 15 digits on, so such a range counted as monotonic although its texts are in the opposite order. The digit count is now exact (`common::digits10`); 0 stays apart from 1..9 as before, because a `Bool` renders them as configurable strings.

Since #118957 (26.10), `toString(k) IN (SELECT <integers>)` over an integer sorting key reads every granule, where 26.8 pruned (#130315). #118957 declines a non-`String` set element over a string column, because `IN` parses the column (`'02'` and `'2'` are both `2`) while the index renders the element. When the string is the text that the key's own chain computes from a native integer (`toString`, `CAST`/`_CAST` to `String`), it holds only canonical numerals, so the set and the index agree; the same holds for `Date`. The decline now exempts exactly that case; types with a custom serialization (`Bool`, also inside `SimpleAggregateFunction`) stay declined. This path needs the exact digit count: 26.8 pruned it with the same wrong result. Reverting #118957 would bring back the wrong results it fixed (`s IN (SELECT toUInt8(2))` over a `String` key holding `'02'`).

Validation: on the issue's setup the first parent of #118957 and this PR select 1186/3668 granules, master 3668/3668, 39 rows on all. Both tests fail on master; every indexed count matches a full-scan `countIf`, and `max_rows_to_read` checks pin the pruning, also for 19-digit keys. 50 randomized runs pass.

issue.title: DeltaLake: delta-kernel block_on waits forever when its result-handoff thread cannot be spawned (fixed upstream in delta-kernel-rs#3202)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Confirmed user-visible misbehaviour in official release

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Data lake table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) integration.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

A `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = DeltaLake(...)` executed by `DDLWorker` blocked for 26 hours and stalled the whole distributed DDL queue (`distributed_ddl.pool_size = 1`; 2,650 entries piled up behind it and every `ON CLUSTER` statement failed with code 159). `KILL QUERY` set `is_cancelled = 1`, but the query kept running. Restarting the server cleared it.

The server log shows what started it, at the second the statement got stuck:

```
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at /ClickHouse/contrib/delta-kernel-rs/kernel/src/engine/default/executor.rs:122:17:
OS can't spawn worker thread: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)
```

The pod has a PID limit of 4096 (kubelet `podPidsLimit`). The server had 4,027 threads, 3,166 of them idle `TokioBackgroundExecutor` threads: each DeltaLake table whose snapshot has been loaded keeps one (`TableSnapshot::KernelSnapshotState` builds a default engine, and `get_default_engine_impl` gives every engine its own `TokioBackgroundExecutor` thread). There were 3,882 DeltaLake tables. After the restart the server had 768 threads, the queue drained in about a minute, and the same `CREATE TABLE` succeeded.

**Why it hangs instead of failing.** `executor.rs:122` is the result handoff in `TokioBackgroundExecutor::block_on` (ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs `c7dd9844`, pinned by 26.3.12.3; `609a93b3`, pinned by the 26.3 branch now, and `88ff5a94`, pinned by master, have the same code):

```rust
let (sender, receiver) = channel::<T::Output>();
let fut = Box::pin(async move {
    let task_output = task.await;
    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {   // line 122
        sender.send(task_output).ok();
    })
    .await
    .unwrap();
});
self.send_future(fut);
receiver.recv().expect("TokioBackgroundExecutor has crashed")
```

When `spawn_blocking` cannot start a thread, tokio panics with `OS can't spawn worker thread`. The closure that owns `sender` stays in the blocking pool's queue and is neither run nor dropped, so the caller's `receiver.recv()` (a `std::sync::mpsc` channel, no timeout) waits forever. Nothing on the ClickHouse side can interrupt that wait, which is why `KILL QUERY` has no effect. `TokioMultiThreadExecutor::block_on` has the same handoff.

**Fix.** delta-io/delta-kernel-rs#3202 ("fix: avoid tokio blocking pool handoff deadlock", merged 2026-08-29, released in v0.28.0) sends the result directly from the async task, since `std::sync::mpsc::Sender::send` never waits:

```rust
sender.send(task_output).ok();
```

It was written for a related case (a full blocking pool deadlocking the same handoff), and it removes the thread spawn from the handoff altogether, so it covers this case too. Every synchronous kernel call goes through `block_on`, so it also covers the scan, CDF and write paths, not only the snapshot load (#117434).

The fork is on v0.23 (master) and v0.19.2 (26.3), which predate it. #3202 is a one-file change that cherry-picks onto both lines, the same way the JSON-reading hang was backported in ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#17 and #106054:

- master (`ClickHouse/v0.23.0`): https://github.com/ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs/pull/19
- 26.3 (`ClickHouse/v0.19.2-with-panic-safe-ffi`): https://github.com/ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs/pull/20

Once they are merged, the `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` pointer needs to move on master and on 26.3.

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

The code is the same on master (fork pin `88ff5a94`), so it should (not reproduced on master). Hitting it needs the process to run out of threads; the regression test in #3202 reproduces the same handoff hang with a blocking pool of one thread.

### How to reproduce

1. Run the server with a process thread limit close to its thread count (here: Kubernetes `podPidsLimit: 4096`).
2. Load enough DeltaLake tables that the per-table `TokioBackgroundExecutor` threads bring the server to the limit (here: about 3,200).
3. Run `CREATE TABLE ... ON CLUSTER ... ENGINE = DeltaLake(...)`. When the result handoff cannot spawn its thread, the statement never returns and the DDL queue stops behind it.

### Expected behavior

The statement fails with an error when a thread cannot be spawned, instead of waiting forever.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

```
std::sync::mpmc::list::Channel<...>::recv
delta_kernel::engine::default::filesystem::ObjectStoreStorageHandler<TokioBackgroundExecutor>::read_files
delta_kernel::snapshot::builder::SnapshotBuilder::build
delta_kernel_ffi::snapshot_impl
DeltaLake::TableSnapshot::initOrUpdateSnapshot() const
DeltaLake::TableSnapshot::getVersion() const
DB::DeltaLakeMetadataDeltaKernel::getTableSnapshot(...) const
DB::DeltaLakeMetadataDeltaKernel::getTableSchema(...) const
DB::resolveSchemaAndFormat(...)
DB::StorageObjectStorage::StorageObjectStorage(...)
DB::InterpreterCreateQuery::doCreateTable(...)
DB::DDLWorker::tryExecuteQuery(...)
DB::DDLWorker::processTask(...)
```

### Related issues and pull requests

- #117280: same stack, 2026-08-31, same cluster. Its server log had already rotated, so I could not confirm the same trigger there.
- #117431: makes the snapshot-load wait interruptible and bounded. It is still useful as a safety net, but in this failure mode the kernel call never returns, so the worker it waits on stays stuck until restart. #3202 removes the hang itself.
- #117434: the remaining uninterruptible kernel waits (scan, CDF, writes), which go through the same `block_on`.
- delta-io/delta-kernel-rs#3202: the upstream fix.

### Additional context

26.3.12.3 (official build), `USE_DELTA_KERNEL_RS=1`, Kubernetes (OKD), single node. The thread count itself — one OS thread per DeltaLake table whose snapshot is loaded — is a separate capacity question and not part of this report.

issue.title: Fix Parquet arrays of tuples read as empty when the requested elements are not in the file

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with bugfix, not backported by default

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Allows running workflows for external contributors

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Issues related to the native Parquet reader.

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->


Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130101
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130173


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed reading Parquet arrays of tuples when none of the requested tuple elements is in the file, e.g. a field added to a struct inside an array by schema evolution: such arrays were read as empty, so `ARRAY JOIN` and filters on their size lost rows. Now they keep their sizes from the file, and the missing elements get default values.


### Description

On 26.10.3.7, with a file written as `l Array(Tuple(a Int32, c String))`, `SELECT l.d FROM file('f.parquet', Parquet, 'l Array(Tuple(a Int32, c String, d Nullable(Int32)))')` returns `[]` instead of `[NULL]`, `ARRAY JOIN l.d` drops every row, `WHERE length(l.d) > 0` matches nothing, inserting `l.a, l.d` into a `Nested` column fails with `SIZES_OF_ARRAYS_DONT_MATCH`, and the structure `l Array(Tuple(d Nullable(Int32)))` reads `[]`. Reading the whole `l` keeps the sizes. Iceberg reaches this through schema evolution of a struct inside a list; there the whole column is fixed, while its subcolumns read `[]` for another reason (#130023).

Parquet stores array sizes (repetition/definition levels) only in leaf columns, and the reader requested a leaf only for requested elements that exist in the file, so nothing under the array was read.

Now, when no requested element under an array has a leaf, the reader also reads one leaf of the array only for its levels (preferring a fixed-width leaf, even one read for another column), and fills the missing elements with defaults per element. This covers the whole column, `arr.elem` subcolumns and flattened subcolumns like `l.d`, at any array depth. A column like `l.d` that is not in the file is still reported as missing, so its `DEFAULT` applies. An array dropped from the Iceberg schema is never used, and an ambiguous case-insensitive match fails with `DUPLICATE_COLUMN`. A leaf that cannot be decoded raises the error it raises when requested. Its values are dropped right after decoding, and the columns cache key tells such a column apart.

`03548_parquet_missing_tuple_elements` pinned the empty arrays; two of its expectations change, and it is extended with ARRAY JOIN, WHERE, PREWHERE, a `DEFAULT`, nested arrays, a `GEOMETRY` leaf, Iceberg schema changes, the columns cache and case-insensitive matching. It fails on master and passes with the fix. ORC is not changed here.

<!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: -->

---
Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=130259&sha=latest&name_0=PR)]
Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/130259](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F130259+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]
<!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

comment.body:
Two things I measured on master (`41a73dec`) that bear on this:

- `Arrow` and `ArrowStream` are no longer read through `ArrowColumnToCHColumn` (the library reader was removed in 26.8, `input_format_arrow_use_native_reader` is obsolete). The native `ArrowIPCBlockInputFormat` has its own copy of the rule in [`prepareArrowColumnForCast`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/41a73dec3078305e46661880e00bbff50e86a994/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/ArrowIPC/ArrowIPCBlockInputFormat.cpp#L332-L387): it matches by name whenever both tuples are named, without the positional fallback, and then calls `castColumn` directly, not `castColumnToRequestedType`. The `ArrowColumnToCHColumn` block is now reached through Vortex, Arrow Flight and the Delta Lake change feed.
- The defaults already differ between the readers. A file with `t Tuple(a Int32)` read as `t Tuple(a Int32, e Enum8('x' = 5, 'y' = 7)), z Enum8('x' = 5, 'y' = 7)`: `t.e` is `'x'` in Arrow (`createColumnConstWithDefaultValue`) and 0 in Parquet and ORC, so `SELECT t` fails there with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_OF_ENUM`. The whole missing column `z` is 0 in all three, so `SELECT z` fails in all three. Choosing the default once would need to cover each reader's missing-column fill as well, not only `CAST`.

This PR keeps the existing Parquet fill for the elements it adds. If you want, I can do the unification as a follow-up PR once #130279 and this one are merged.

issue.body:
On s390x, use the lld linker and set the default arch level to z13 in cpu features.

`lld` has been supported on s390x since at least v19 so use it instead of the `mold` linker.

Allow setting the arch level on s390x.
z13 is the minimum arch level on versions of Red Hat, Ubuntu and SUSE that are in support so use that as the default. z10 can be set if older machine support is desired.

Remove the mold linker from the `binary-builder` image since it was added for s390x and is no longer used.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

issue.body:

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130064


### Changelog category (leave one):
- CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Install `pigz` in the `clickhouse/binary-builder` image, so the release build jobs compress their `.tgz` packages in parallel.

### Description

`packages/build` already compresses the `.tgz` tarballs with `pigz` when `/usr/bin/pigz` exists, else with `tar -czf`. The `Build Packages` step of `Build (amd_release)` / `Build (arm_release)` runs inside `clickhouse/binary-builder`, which does not install `pigz` (checked in the current master image `16143eb26bdf0bdb2f00_amd`), so every tarball is compressed by single-threaded `gzip`. The four tarballs took 60 s of the 69 s step in [a PR `arm_release` job](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/42315009375/job/128354633601), and 248 s of 282 s in a [master `amd_release` job](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/42598309267).

This PR adds `pigz` to the image's package list. Nothing else changes. This PR's own `Build (amd_release)` / `Build (arm_release)` do not exercise it: they are reused from the CI cache, because the build-job digests do not include the `binary-builder` image digest (`ci/praktika/digest.py`).

Validation, locally on the master `26.11.1.1733` packages with the same `pigz` 2.8, `gzip` 1.12 and GNU tar 1.35 as the image, median of 3 runs on 16 cores:
- `clickhouse-common-static` (746 MB): `gzip` 25.0 s, `pigz` 2.1 s (1.4 s on 32 cores, the size of the `m8g.8xlarge` runner).
- `clickhouse-common-static-dbg` (4.1 GB): `gzip` 117.8 s, `pigz` 12.7 s (7.2 s on 32 cores).

The decompressed tar streams are byte-identical to `gzip`'s, `sha512sum -c` passes, and BusyBox `tar xzf` in Alpine (the path of the Alpine server and keeper images) extracts the same files. The tarballs are about 0.1% smaller. Their bytes and `.sha512` differ from `gzip`'s, but do not depend on the number of cores.

Reported in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130064#issuecomment-6740954794.

comment.body:
Thanks. This PR's `Build (amd_release)` / `Build (arm_release)` did not run: they were reused from the CI cache. `Config Workflow` marks them affected by the `binary-builder` change, but the cache lookup still found a record for their digest (`eed958774b5f8fe01e84-46a2`, built by another PR on the old image).

The reason is in `ci/praktika/digest.py`: the image digest is added to a job digest only when `":" not in job_config.run_in_docker`, a check meant to skip tagged images like `ubuntu:22.04`. It runs over the whole `run_in_docker` string, and for the build jobs that string contains `--volume=.:/ClickHouse`. So a `binary-builder` change never changes the build-job digests. The rebuilt image does contain `pigz` (`Setting up pigz (2.8-1)` in `Dockers Build (amd)`), and the release builds pick it up as soon as their sources change.

The description said the PR's own release builds use the rebuilt image. That was wrong, and I have corrected it.

If you want, I can send a separate PR that runs that check on the image name only (`Job.get_docker_image_name()`), so that a build-image change rebuilds the builds that run in it. The `ci-force-all` label would also make this PR's release builds run (along with every other job), but I can't add labels.

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125001


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The hash tables of large hash `JOIN`s no longer switch to the Robin Hood mode by default (it was enabled in 26.10). This makes joins with random keys up to 1.8 times faster, but the hash table takes up to 1.75 times more memory and joins on dense keys can be up to 1.3 times slower. The new setting `enable_robin_hood_hash_for_joins` turns the mode back on.


### Description

Since #125001 (in 26.10), a bucket of a large hash join table switches to the Robin Hood mode at 2^16 cells and then fills up to 0.9 instead of 0.5 before it doubles, so a right table above about 8.4M keys takes up to two times less memory. This PR turns that off by default for joins and adds `enable_robin_hood_hash_for_joins` to turn it on (`compatibility` 26.10 or older turns it on). Aggregation and `uniqExact` are unchanged.

The grower gets a per-table switch that allows the Robin Hood mode; `HashJoin` sets it from the setting when it creates its maps. Since the unified hash join, this covers every hash join that splits its hash table into parts (`hash_join_layout`); one-part tables, grace hash buckets and `StorageJoin` never use the mode.

Measured with the CI release build of da4f7d3 (8M-128M right rows, 8 and 32 threads, sweep in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128012#issuecomment-6773961553), time with the mode on relative to off: `intHash64` keys with half of the left keys missing 1.06-1.80x whenever the Robin Hood table is filled above 0.5, 0.86-0.94x when it is not; dense keys and the `right_full_hash_join_nullmaps` shape mostly 0.79-0.92x; peak memory 0.57-0.59x when the table is smaller. With the mode off, a join near the `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join` limit spills to grace hash sooner.

Extends `05345_robin_hood_large_hash_tables` (both modes, checked by their memory usage) and `parallel_hash_join_various.xml` (`left_large_right`, `left_large_right_dense`), and adds `hash_join_robin_hood.xml`: both modes for `UInt64`, `String` and two-column keys at a fill of 0.83, where the Robin Hood mode is the slowest.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
delta-kernel-rs and chdig are built as members of the Rust workspace in `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace`, with one `Cargo.lock`, one cargo target directory and features resolved once for all members, so the crates they share with the other Rust libraries are compiled once, in one parallel cargo run.

### Description

Step 3 of the layout in #86562, after #130348 (step 2).

- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs-cmake` and `contrib/chdig-cmake` get one-line wrapper crates (`pub use delta_kernel_ffi;`, `pub use chdig;`), imported through the workspace manifest like the other six.
- One environment for every member (`clickhouse_config_crate_env`: OpenSSL variables, `CFLAGS` with `-I contrib/openssl/include`, `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): build scripts track their environment, so any difference rebuilds shared crates every build.
- `resolver.feature-unification = "workspace"`: corrosion runs one `cargo rustc` per package, and cargo otherwise resolves features per package.
- The workspace manifest is also a root package, `_ch_rust_workspace`, with one feature per member. `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace/CMakeLists.txt` builds it with the enabled members' features before their runs, which then compile only their wrapper. Not with LTO, where each member's run does its own code generation. The wrappers are plain libraries imported with `OVERRIDE_CRATE_TYPE <crate>=staticlib`, so the root run writes no unused archives.
- `Cargo.lock` is resolved offline from `contrib/rust_vendor` (no `rust_vendor` change); delta-kernel-rs and chdig take the workspace's semver-compatible versions.
- The `aws-lc-sys` `LDFLAGS` workaround goes: the crate left the graph.
- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` moves to the merge commit of ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#22: the pin of #130062 plus `crate-type = ["lib"]`.

Rust-only cold build, `-j48`: Debug 200 s / 1027 s CPU on master, 108 s / 779 s here. With ThinLTO 13.2 min on master, 18.4 min here: the members' LTO runs queue on the one target directory.

Validation, x86_64 Debug:
- 1240 compile units in 3 target directories before, 799 in one after, no crate built with two feature sets.
- Build and link pass; a no-op build compiles nothing, also alternating between members; the member archives are the same cargo units as without the root package.
- Delta Lake stateless tests 77/77; prql, pco, polyglot, vortex and wasm tests 98/99 (the other fails on master too); `chdig --help` works.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Thanks, I'll do it in this PR: the root package `_ch_rust_workspace` built once through Corrosion with one feature per enabled member, the wrappers as `["staticlib", "lib"]`, and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` in the common environment. I'll post the build times here with the push.

issue.title: Fix MongoDB pushdown for Boolean and numeric comparisons

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Connectivity to external databases (ODBC/JDBC, MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.).

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
Comparisons such as `flag = 1` on a `Bool` column and `n = true` on a `UInt8` column sent constants with the wrong BSON type to MongoDB, silently discarding matching rows.

Exclude `Bool` from the numeric implicit-conversion shortcut and distinguish it from `UInt8` even though their ClickHouse types compare equal, for single comparisons and for `IN`/`NOT IN` lists. Bypass the equivalent source-type hint when necessary so strict conversion still rejects non-Boolean bounds instead of turning them into incorrect filters. For `=` and `!=`, an integer bound that no `Bool` value equals keeps its own BSON type, because a BSON number stored in a `Bool` column is read as it is: `flag = 2` pushes `{"$eq": 2}`. Other unrepresentable bounds retain the existing unsupported-query handling.

The reader accepts both BSON bools and BSON numbers for `Bool` and numeric columns, so a comparison between a `Bool` and a number matches both encodings of the bound: `flag = 1` pushes `{"$in": [true, 1]}`, and a range pushes an `$or` of both bounds.

Reproduced on Azure with real MongoDB: both new regression cases failed before the fix and passed afterward. They cover `Bool` and `Nullable(Bool)`, the `MongoDB` engine and `mongodb` table function, inverted comparisons, numeric columns compared with Boolean constants, and out-of-range bounds, as well as documents that store BSON numbers in the `Bool` column and BSON bools in the numeric column. Five existing MongoDB integration tests also passed.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127736
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127602

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fix incorrect empty results when comparing Boolean columns with numeric constants, or numeric columns with Boolean constants, in the `MongoDB` table engine and `mongodb` table function.

comment.body:
I reran `c2767485` against MongoDB 6.0 with the same layouts as before, for `Bool` and `Nullable(Bool)`, through the `mongodb` table function and the `MongoDB` engine. The four predicates return the right counts with the filters you describe, `flag != 0.5` and `flag < -1` are still refused, and next to a build of `d8dc5cdb` only `=` / `!=` with an integer constant that has no `Bool` value changed. Looks good to me.

issue.body:
Fix a race condition where ClickHouse could load a mismatched certificate and key if its reloader runs between the replacement of the cert and key during credential rotation. Every handshake failed until the other file was replaced and ClickHouse reloaded it. See https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/129614 for issue details and test case.

The cause was that `CertificateReloader` published a new `Data` as soon as the certificate and key files parsed, without checking that they were a valid pair. If only one file of a rotation had been replaced, the mismatched pair still replaced the previous, working, pair.

To fix, check that the key matches the leaf certificate when building `Data`, so a mismatched pair is rejected. The active pair is not replaced until the candidate pair has passed validation.

Also name the prefix and the empty option in the message logged when `certificateFile` or `privateKeyFile` is empty, and log at debug level when neither is configured.

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)

-->
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/126230
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129160


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Backward Incompatible Change


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `vector_similarity` index can no longer be created (`CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE ... ADD INDEX`, `CREATE INDEX`) on a `MergeTree`-family engine other than `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`, e.g. `ReplacingMergeTree` or `CollapsingMergeTree`, because `SELECT ... FINAL` that uses such an index may return row versions that were already replaced or deleted. Existing tables keep working. To create such an index anyway, set the MergeTree setting `allow_vector_similarity_index_in_specialized_merge_tree = 1` (or `compatibility` to `26.10` or lower in the default profile).

### Description

The vector index selects candidates in each part before `FINAL` merges the row versions across parts, so on engines whose merges combine rows a newer version that is not a candidate of its own part is dropped and an older one is returned (#126230; reproduced on 26.8-26.10 with default settings). As agreed on the issue, such tables now refuse the index instead of the read path being changed.

The check runs at `CREATE TABLE` and at `ALTER TABLE ... ADD INDEX` (which `CREATE INDEX` becomes), only for an index the statement introduces. It never runs for `ATTACH`, server startup, `RESTORE`, `Replicated` database replay or replica recovery, so existing tables, and replicas applying DDL already committed by an older initiator, are not affected. Two paths that re-create an existing table do run it and need the setting: the `CREATE OR REPLACE` with which a refreshable materialized view without `APPEND` replaces its target on each refresh, and a `CREATE TABLE` that adds a replica to an existing `ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree` (or similar) table. The new MergeTree setting `allow_vector_similarity_index_in_specialized_merge_tree` (default `false`; `true` when the default profile has `compatibility <= 26.10`) restores the old behaviour. Five existing tests now set it.

Validation: the new test fails on master and passes with the change; removing either check makes it fail at the matching statement; 50 of 50 randomized runs pass. A table created by master still loads and accepts other `ALTER`s, and in a `Replicated` database a master replica's `CREATE` and `ADD INDEX` replay on an upgraded one.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed reading an ORC struct whose requested `Tuple` has none of the struct's fields (for example after schema evolution): such a list or map no longer loses its elements or crashes, the struct keeps its `NULL`s, and the requested fields are filled with default values.

### Description

On 26.10, `SELECT m FROM file('t.orc', ORC, 'm Map(String, Tuple(c Nullable(String)))')` over a `map<string, struct<a, b>>` column crashes, and `l Array(Tuple(d Nullable(Int32)))` over a list of such structs returns `[]` for every row. The same happens for a struct map key, nested lists and maps, dotted subcolumns and flattened `Nested` subcolumns.

`updateIncludeTypeIds` selects only the struct fields the requested `Tuple` names. When it names none, nothing is selected: the ORC reader drops the list and keeps a map with one child, which the MAP read indexes out of bounds. Selecting a field alone is not enough, because the final `CAST` converts named tuples with no element names in common by position, so the field's values would end up in the requested elements.

Now a requested struct with nothing selected under it has its narrowest field selected, only for its size and null map: the read skips that field, so its values are not converted. After the read, the struct fields are matched to the requested `Tuple` elements by name, through `Nullable`, `Array` and `Map`, and the requested elements that were not read are filled with defaults, as the Arrow reader does. The read keeps the file's shape, so a struct read once for several requested columns (a column and its subcolumns) serves each of them. Unnamed tuples are still matched by position.

The fix is kept inside the ORC reader to be easy to backport. How the Arrow, ORC and Parquet copies of this rule could be unified is described in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130259#issuecomment-6771235736.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... ADD ENUM VALUES` executed through an `Alias` table overwriting the enum values that a concurrent `ALTER` of the target table had added. Both queries succeeded, but the target's values were lost, and with `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query = 0` the target table could no longer be attached after a restart.

### Description

On 26.10.2.103, two concurrent `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN e ADD ENUM VALUES (...)`, one through an `Alias` table and one on its target, both succeed, but the values added on the target are lost. With `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query = 0` the target also gets a `MODIFY COLUMN` mutation written without a type, and after a restart the table cannot be attached (`MODIFY COLUMN mutation command doesn't specify type`, `LOGICAL_ERROR`). Found while answering https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130322#discussion_r4513071544.

Root cause: `InterpreterAlterQuery` validates and prepares the commands under the alias's locks, and `StorageAlias::alter` locks the target only afterwards. For `ADD ENUM VALUES`, `AlterCommands::prepare` stores the complete merged enum type, computed from the column type read before that lock, so it overwrites any value that a direct `ALTER` of the target committed in between. This does not depend on the query metadata cache that #130322 clears.

Change: after locking the target, `StorageAlias::alter` prepares a copy of the commands again against the target's current metadata and runs the target's `checkAlterIsPossible` on it. `prepare` now gives `createEnumAdd` a copy of the `ADD ENUM VALUES` list, which it numbers in place, so a second `prepare` does not read those numbers as explicit.

`validate` still runs before the target's lock, since it needs the unprepared commands.

Validation: `05618` races 20 `ADD ENUM VALUES` through an `Alias` against 20 on the target. On master it loses the target's values in 10 of 10 runs; with the fix it passes 50 of 50 randomized runs, also with the setting forced to 0 and to 1. `05619` checks that values added without a number through an `Alias` follow the target's largest value. Also checked: ReplicatedMergeTree and Memory targets, and a restart on the raced data.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `UNION ALL` branch or subquery whose filter becomes always false after filter push-down (for example an outer `WHERE tag = 'y'` over branches that select the literal tags `'x'`, `'y'` and `'z'`) no longer builds the sets of its `IN (subquery)` conditions or reads its input. The query from #130319 now peaks at 1.2 GB instead of 4.0 GB and runs 2.3 times faster. Closes #130319.


### Description

On 26.10 the query from #130319 (three `UNION ALL` branches `SELECT '<tag>' AS c10, ... WHERE c1 IN (SELECT ... FROM cte)`, outer `c10 = 'y'`) peaks at 4.0 GB instead of 1.0 GB on 26.8; bisected to #105987.

Push-down gives each branch `materialize('<tag>') = 'y'`, and since #105987 the `x` and `z` branch filters fold to `0`, so nothing there uses their `IN` sets. Their `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` still holds the sets, so `addStepsToBuildSets` builds four dead sets, each running the CTE's two `t2 x t3` joins. Before #105987 they were built one at a time during planning (part pruning of the unfolded filter); now `CreatingSetsTransform` builds them concurrently with each other and with the main query.

`addStepsToBuildSets` looks below each `DelayedCreatingSetsStep`. If the steps there are only expressions, filters and the set steps of nested scopes, and one filter's column is a constant the runtime treats as always false, no row reaches a user of the scope's sets: that filter's input becomes `ReadNothingStep` and the sets are detached. An input that can produce totals is kept: totals pass a filter unfiltered (`canProduceTotals` moves to `Optimizations/Utils` from the constant-false JOIN short-circuit). A query failing only in the subquery of such a filtered-out branch now succeeds. Not changed: the subquery of a `GLOBAL IN` against `remote()` still runs while the shard query is built, and `make_distributed_plan` (private preview) plans still build these sets, attached above the distributed source.

Validation (RelWithDebInfo, the issue's data, 5 interleaved runs): 4.03 GB / 5.3-5.9 s -> 1.20-1.21 GB / 2.3-2.6 s, same result checksum. The new test fails on master and passed 50/50 with randomized settings; the new performance test goes from 0.41 s to 0.08 s. About 200 related stateless tests show no new failures.

### Changelog category (leave one):

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... ADD ENUM VALUES` executed through an `Alias` table overwriting the enum values that a concurrent `ALTER` of the target table had added. Both queries succeeded, but the target's values were lost, and with `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query = 0` the target table could no longer be attached after a restart.

### Description

On 26.10.2.103, two concurrent `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN e ADD ENUM VALUES (...)`, one through an `Alias` table and one on its target, both succeed, but the values added on the target are lost. With `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query = 0` the target also gets a `MODIFY COLUMN` mutation written without a type, and after a restart the table cannot be attached (`MODIFY COLUMN mutation command doesn't specify type`, `LOGICAL_ERROR`). Found while answering https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130322#discussion_r4513071544.

Root cause: `InterpreterAlterQuery` validates and prepares the commands under the alias's locks, and `StorageAlias::alter` locks the target only afterwards. For `ADD ENUM VALUES`, `AlterCommands::prepare` stores the complete merged enum type, computed from the column type read before that lock, so it overwrites any value that a direct `ALTER` of the target committed in between. This does not depend on the query metadata cache that #130322 clears.

Change: after locking the target, `StorageAlias::alter` prepares a copy of the commands again against the target's current metadata and runs the target's `checkAlterIsPossible` on it. `prepare` now gives `createEnumAdd` a copy of the `ADD ENUM VALUES` list, which it numbers in place, so a second `prepare` does not read those numbers as explicit.

`validate` still runs before the target's lock, since it needs the unprepared commands.

Validation: `05618` races 20 `ADD ENUM VALUES` through an `Alias` against 20 on the target. On master it loses the target's values in 10 of 10 runs; with the fix it passes 50 of 50 randomized runs, also with the setting forced to 0 and to 1. `05619` checks that values added without a number through an `Alias` follow the target's largest value. Also checked: ReplicatedMergeTree and Memory targets, and a restart on the raced data.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

issue.body:
A processor that executes a pipeline, like `dictGet` on a `direct` dictionary, does it on the thread of the outer executor, which already holds a CPU slot. The nested executor requested a slot for its first thread from the same workload, and with `cpu_slot_preemption = false` and `max_concurrent_threads = 1` it waited forever for the slot held by the thread itself, ignoring `KILL QUERY`.

The executor now publishes the slot of the thread while it executes processors, and an execution started on a thread with a slot runs its first thread on a noncompeting slot. Its other threads still compete for slots of the workload. Covered by `05615_nested_pipeline_executor_cpu_slot`.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130300

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed reading an ORC struct whose requested `Tuple` has none of the struct's fields (for example after schema evolution): such a list or map no longer loses its elements or crashes, the struct keeps its `NULL`s, and the requested fields are filled with default values.

### Description

On 26.10, `SELECT m FROM file('t.orc', ORC, 'm Map(String, Tuple(c Nullable(String)))')` over a `map<string, struct<a, b>>` column crashes, and `l Array(Tuple(d Nullable(Int32)))` over a list of such structs returns `[]` for every row. The same happens for a struct map key, nested lists and maps, dotted subcolumns and flattened `Nested` subcolumns.

`updateIncludeTypeIds` selects only the struct fields the requested `Tuple` names. When it names none, nothing is selected: the ORC reader drops the list and keeps a map with one child, which the MAP read indexes out of bounds. Selecting a field alone is not enough, because the final `CAST` converts named tuples with no element names in common by position, so the field's values would end up in the requested elements.

Now a requested struct with nothing selected under it has its narrowest field selected, only for its size and null map: the read skips that field, so its values are not converted. After the read, the struct fields are matched to the requested `Tuple` elements by name, through `Nullable`, `Array` and `Map`, and the requested elements that were not read are filled with defaults, as the Arrow reader does. The read keeps the file's shape, so a struct read once for several requested columns (a column and its subcolumns) serves each of them. Unnamed tuples are still matched by position.

The fix is kept inside the ORC reader to be easy to backport. How the Arrow, ORC and Parquet copies of this rule could be unified is described in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130259#issuecomment-6771235736.

issue.title: Merge Iceberg manifests on append

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with some performance improvements

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Data lake table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) integration.

issue.body:
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/98178

Every `INSERT` into an Iceberg table adds new manifests and carries all the manifests of the parent snapshot forward, so the number of manifests grows with the number of inserts. Reading manifests is a large part of the work of every query, and for many small manifests it is pure startup delay and cost, while it is easy to avoid: manifests are small, so merging them is cheap. `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... MANIFEST` (#98178) does this only on request and as a separate snapshot.

Like other Iceberg writers (`MergeAppend` in the reference implementation), `INSERT` now merges the small data manifests of the parent snapshot into fewer ones as part of the same commit, without any experimental setting. The new `append` snapshot lists the same data files as EXISTING entries keeping their snapshot ids, sequence numbers, statistics and partition tuples, so no data is read and no separate snapshot is created; older snapshots keep their own manifests.

- The merge happens when the new snapshot would have more small data manifests than the table property `commit.manifest.min-count-to-merge`, or, when it is not set, the `iceberg_manifest_min_count_to_compact` setting (default `100`).
- Merged manifests span partitions (otherwise a table with one insert per partition would never shrink), ordered by partition so the manifest-list partition bounds stay narrow, and hold up to the entries that fit in `commit.manifest.target-size-bytes` (default 8 MiB). Manifests that already hold at least half of that are carried forward as they are, so the cost of a merge stays bounded.
- `commit.manifest-merge.enabled` = `false` disables it. It is done only for format version 2, and skipped (not failed) for encrypted data files and for partition values that cannot be written (including `binary` and nested partition source columns); delete manifests are always carried forward unchanged.
- `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION` rewrites a data manifest that also lists files of other partitions (such as a merged one) without the dropped files, instead of failing. The full `OPTIMIZE TABLE` compaction rejects, before writing anything, a history where a data file is listed in several manifests (a merged one and the originals kept by older snapshots).

The collection and rewriting of data manifests moves from `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... MANIFEST` into a shared `DataManifestsRewriter`; `OPTIMIZE` keeps writing one manifest per partition, or one per partition spec and schema with `iceberg_insert_single_manifest_for_all_partitions` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128880). The manifest-list partition summary as a range and per-file partition tuples in `generateManifestFile` come from that PR. A manifest written with that setting can now also be handled by `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128880

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`INSERT` into an Iceberg table merges the small manifest files of the current snapshot within the same commit when there are more than `commit.manifest.min-count-to-merge` (or the `iceberg_manifest_min_count_to_compact` setting, 100 by default) of them, so the number of manifests a query has to read no longer grows with the number of inserts. The merge can be disabled with the table property `commit.manifest-merge.enabled` = `false`.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `UNION ALL` branch or subquery whose filter becomes always false after filter push-down (for example an outer `WHERE tag = 'y'` over branches that select the literal tags `'x'`, `'y'` and `'z'`) no longer builds the sets of its `IN (subquery)` conditions or reads its input. ### Description

On 26.10 the query from #130319 (three `UNION ALL` branches `SELECT '<tag>' AS c10, ... WHERE c1 IN (SELECT ... FROM cte)`, outer `c10 = 'y'`) peaks at 4.0 GB instead of 1.0 GB on 26.8; bisected to #105987.

Push-down gives each branch `materialize('<tag>') = 'y'`, and since #105987 the `x` and `z` branch filters fold to `0`, so nothing there uses their `IN` sets. Their `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` still holds the sets, so `addStepsToBuildSets` builds four dead sets, each running the CTE's two `t2 x t3` joins. Before #105987 they were built one at a time during planning (part pruning of the unfolded filter); now `CreatingSetsTransform` builds them concurrently with each other and with the main query.

`addStepsToBuildSets` looks below each `DelayedCreatingSetsStep`. If the steps there are only expressions, filters and the set steps of nested scopes, and one filter's column is a constant the runtime treats as always false, no row reaches a user of the scope's sets: that filter's input becomes `ReadNothingStep` and the sets are detached. An input that can produce totals is kept: totals pass a filter unfiltered (`canProduceTotals` moves to `Optimizations/Utils` from the constant-false JOIN short-circuit). A query failing only in the subquery of such a filtered-out branch now succeeds. Not changed: the subquery of a `GLOBAL IN` against `remote()` still runs while the shard query is built, and `make_distributed_plan` (private preview) plans still build these sets, attached above the distributed source.

Validation (RelWithDebInfo, the issue's data, 5 interleaved runs): 4.03 GB / 5.3-5.9 s -> 1.20-1.21 GB / 2.3-2.6 s, same result checksum. The new test fails on master and passed 50/50 with randomized settings; the new performance test goes from 0.41 s to 0.08 s. About 200 related stateless tests show no new failures.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`CREATE TABLE` no longer returns `CANNOT_UNLINK` for a table it has created when the file system fails the removal of a `<table>.sql.detached` flag that does not exist (for example, with an I/O error or after a read-only remount). The flag is removed only if it exists.

### Description

After `CREATE TABLE` commits (the table is attached and `<t>.sql.tmp` is renamed to `<t>.sql`), `DatabaseOnDisk::removeDetachedPermanentlyFlag` unlinked `<t>.sql.detached` unconditionally and relied on `ENOENT` to mean "no flag". Any other errno (`EIO`, `EROFS`) was returned as the error of the committed `CREATE`: the client got `Code: 458 (CANNOT_UNLINK)` while the table existed, and the message claimed the table would not be reattached on restart, which was false.

The flag is now removed only if `existsFile` reports it, the same predicate the loader (`DatabaseOrdinary::loadTablesMetadata`) and `checkMetadataFilenameAvailability` use to decide whether a table is permanently detached. When a flag exists nothing changes: it is removed, and a failure is still reported with a message that is then true. The same helper serves the short and full `ATTACH TABLE`, a `RENAME` that involves an `Ordinary` database, and `DatabaseReplicated` (its override calls the base).

Validation: the new test puts a directory at `t1.sql.detached` in a private `clickhouse-local` path (`unlink()` fails with `EISDIR`) and a real leftover flag for `t2`. On master it fails (`Code: 458 ... Is a directory`, and `db.t2` is missing after a restart); with the fix it passes, 50/50 randomized runs. The issue's `strace` EIO injection returns `exit code: 202` on master and `0` with the fix, which no longer calls `unlink` on the flag at all.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
An `INSERT` into Google Cloud Storage with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` no longer fails when the file is larger than `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`.

### Description

On master, an `INSERT` into GCS with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` fails with `Code: 499 ... GCS conditional create of <key> must be a single PUT` as soon as the object exceeds `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`, even for the first write to a new key. #114995 made the new-file write conditional (`If-None-Match: *`), and #128866 makes `WriteBufferFromS3` refuse a conditional multipart upload to GCS, because GCS evaluates no precondition on an XML API multipart upload. Neither change is in a release.

The sink now marks its `If-None-Match` as best-effort (`object_storage_write_if_none_match_best_effort` in `WriteSettings`). For such a write, a GCS multipart upload goes ahead unconditionally, as before #114995, and the GCS `CompleteMultipartUpload` request carries no `If-None-Match` (GCS ignores it, and rejects its `x-goog-if-generation-match` translation). Single-part GCS writes stay conditional, other S3 providers keep the condition on `CompleteMultipartUpload`, and the strict callers (Iceberg metadata, backups, the Iceberg REST catalog) are still refused. So two concurrent same-name inserts can race again on GCS objects above the single-part limit, as agreed in #130282.

Reverting #114995 would also remove the error, but it would bring back the silent overwrites and the data race that PR fixed. A conditional GCS path exists (upload into a temporary key, then `compose` with `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`), but it leaves a visible temporary object in the user's prefix and cannot be tested in CI.

Validation: a new `test_storage_s3` case reaches MinIO as `storage.googleapis.com` (plain and partitioned `INSERT`, 1 MiB single-part limit); it fails on master with `Code: 499` and passes with the fix. Two gtests pin the strict refusal and the unconditional best-effort request.

issue.title: Iceberg: wrong ORDER BY ... LIMIT result with read-in-order when a table has more data files than read streams

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: To be reviewed by developers and confirmed/rejected.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Data lake table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) integration.

issue.body:
### Company or project name

ClickHouse

### Describe what's wrong

When every data file of an Iceberg table carries the table's `sort_order_id`, `IcebergMetadata::isDataSortedBySortingKey` returns true and `optimizeReadInOrder` reads the table in order: the sort only merges the read streams (`MergingSortedTransform`), assuming each stream is sorted.

`ReadFromObjectStorageStep::initializePipeline` creates `min(num_streams, number of files)` sources that all pull from one shared file iterator. With more files than streams, one source returns several files back to back, so its output is not sorted, and `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` returns wrong rows.

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Reproduced on master (`6e962c3b7e0`, 26.11). Not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

The table needs data files tagged with `sort_order_id`. ClickHouse's own `INSERT` does not tag files today, so this is hit by tables written by an engine that does, e.g. Spark with a table sort order (`ALTER TABLE t WRITE ORDERED BY x`, then several `INSERT`s). I reproduced it by writing the table with a local ClickHouse build that tags inserted files, and reading it with a master build:

```sql
-- written with a build that tags files: 4 data files, sort_order_id = 1 on each
CREATE TABLE t (x Int64) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/path/t') ORDER BY x;
INSERT INTO t SELECT number * 4 + 0 FROM numbers(1000);
INSERT INTO t SELECT number * 4 + 1 FROM numbers(1000);
INSERT INTO t SELECT number * 4 + 2 FROM numbers(1000);
INSERT INTO t SELECT number * 4 + 3 FROM numbers(1000);

-- read with master
SELECT x FROM icebergLocal('/path/t') ORDER BY x LIMIT 8 SETTINGS max_threads = 1;
```

| Read settings | Result |
|---|---|
| `max_threads = 1` | `0 4 8 12 16 20 24 28` |
| `max_threads = 2` | `0 1 4 5 8 9 12 13` |
| `max_threads = 4` (one file per stream) | `0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7` |
| `max_threads = 1, optimize_read_in_order = 0` | `0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7` |

### Expected behavior

`0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7` for every `max_threads`. When reading in order, each stream should read one file (or the files of a stream should be merged), as MergeTree does for parts.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

None; the result is silently wrong.

### Additional context

`initializePipeline` also forces a single stream when `estimatedKeysCount()` returns ≤ 1, which would hit the same problem; not reproduced separately.

comment.body:
This is fixed by #113095 (mine, open); it is the same defect as #112981. When reading in order, `ReadFromObjectStorageStep::initializePipeline` builds one source per data file (as `ReadFromMergeTree` does per part) instead of `num_streams` sources sharing one iterator, so every port of the merge above it carries a sorted run. Above `read_in_order_two_level_merge_threshold * max_threads` files it adds a preliminary merge per group. That branch does not depend on `num_streams`, so the `estimatedKeysCount() <= 1` single-stream case is covered too. `test_read_in_order_more_files_than_streams` reads six overlapping files with `max_threads` 1, 2, 4 and 6, and it passed in CI at the PR head (7f67ed3).

The PR has merge conflicts with master now; I'll resolve them and link this issue from its description.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The connection string of the `odbc` and `jdbc` table functions and of the `ODBC` and `JDBC` table engines, password included, is no longer shown in cleartext in the bridge request URL quoted by errors, `system.query_log`, the server log and `system.schema_inference_cache`. The query itself already showed it as `[HIDDEN]`.

### Description

On 26.8.28.14-lts, and on master after #120407, a failed bridge request quotes its URL with the password while the logged query shows `odbc('[HIDDEN]', 'db', 't')`:

```
SELECT * FROM odbc('DSN=nonexistent_dsn;PWD=SEKRIT_ODBC_p0', 'db', 't')
Code: 86. DB::HTTPException: Received error from remote server http://127.0.0.1:60245/columns_info?use_connection_pooling=1&version=1&connection_string=DSN%3Dnonexistent_dsn%3BPWD%3DSEKRIT_ODBC_p0&schema=db&table=t&...
```

The same URL reaches `system.query_log.exception`, the server log, `system.schema_inference_cache.source` after a successful read, and the `remote_url_allow_hosts` rejection. With a named collection, a user who cannot read `system.named_collections` gets its password this way.

The server sends the connection string to the bridge as the `connection_string` query parameter, and `maskURICredentials`, which all these renders call since #120407, masks only the userinfo and the presigned-URL parameters.

`maskPresignedURLParameters`, which `maskURICredentials` and `RemoteHostFilter::checkURL` call, now also hides the whole value of `connection_string`: its grammar belongs to the driver, so the password cannot be located inside it. Its other callers hide it too (for example, `url('http://h/?connection_string=...')` in the logged query text). The bridge protocol does not change, so older external bridges keep working.

`05404_xdbc_connection_string_masked` checks the client error, `system.query_log` and an `ODBC` engine insert, and a new `test_allowed_url_from_config` case checks the URL rejection; both fail without the change. The test uses a DSN that does not exist, because a read that really connects crashes the external bridge when the flaky check runs the test in parallel; the success path (`system.schema_inference_cache`) was checked locally against the CI bridge.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view queried by its own definer is no longer read as an opaque step, so the optimizations of the query apply to it again, as before 26.10 (for example, `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` reads in order through it). Other users, and sessions of the definer that are limited by the `GRANTS` of their authentication method or use other roles, still read such a view sealed, and such sessions of the definer no longer bypass the check that hides its plan in `EXPLAIN`.

### Description

On 26.10, `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` over a `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view that filters rows reads the whole table: 3,001,000 rows instead of 43,688 in #130316. Since #122330, every `DEFINER` / `NONE` view that can hide rows is read through the opaque `ReadFromSealedView` step, so read-in-order, top-N and the outer predicate for index analysis cannot see through it. The seal keeps hidden rows away from the invoker, but in the report the invoker is the definer.

`StorageView::isReadByDefiner` holds when the query runs with exactly the identity of the view's own query: an initial query of the definer (compared by UUID), with the definer's default roles (current and external), no `GRANTS` limit from the authentication method, and no row policy on the view itself. Such a query can read everything the view hides, so `readImpl` and the `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` pushdown into views no longer seal the view for it. The same check replaces the name-only definer shortcut that decides whether `EXPLAIN` shows the hidden plan. Secondary queries, other users, other role sets and `NONE` views stay sealed. The parallel-replicas carrier, the `Distributed` pushdown and `analyzer_inline_views` keep the structural check.

Reverting #122330 is not proposed: it would reopen the row leak it fixed.

Validation on a debug build: the issue's query reads 43,688 rows as the definer (3,001,000 on master) and still 3,001,000 as another user. The new test fails on master, and each of the six conditions was removed in a separate build, each caught by the test. All 58 tests with `DEFINER` / `NONE` views pass; 05257, 05407 and 05331 now test the sealed path through a non-definer or a `NONE` view. A performance test is added.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/129680


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Expanding a sparse `String` column to a full one (for `GROUP BY`, `JOIN`, sorting and most functions) now copies its values in one pass, which makes such queries over mostly-empty `String` columns up to 10% faster.

### Description

A part stores a `String` column as sparse when at least `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization` (0.9375) of its values are empty. Turning it into a full column (`ColumnSparse::convertToFullColumnIfSparse` and the sparse path of `IFunction`) calls `createWithOffsets`. `ColumnVector` and `ColumnNullable` override it; `ColumnString` did not, so the generic `IColumn::createWithOffsets` inserted every value with a virtual `insertFrom` and every run of defaults with `insertManyFrom`, growing `chars` as it went.

`ColumnString::createWithOffsets` sizes the result once. With an empty default the value bytes are copied with one `memcpy` and the offsets are written in one pass; with a non-empty default (a function result such as `s || 'x'`) each row is copied as `insertFrom` does. Every position is checked before it is written. `Nullable(String)` gets it through `ColumnNullable`. `FixedString` and `Decimal` columns still use the generic implementation. The algorithm is the one proposed in #129680.

Local release build, ClickBench `hits` (100M rows, `MobilePhoneModel` 94% empty and sparse), change [95% CI] over 8 / 4 ABBA pairs:

| Query | 8 threads | 1 thread |
|---|---|---|
| `GROUP BY MobilePhoneModel` | -10.0% [-14.2, -5.5] | -8.0% [-8.3, -7.6] |
| same, `WHERE MobilePhoneModel <> ''` | -8.8% [-13.3, -4.1] | -11.0% [-12.2, -9.8] |
| `max(length(MobilePhoneModel \|\| 'x'))` (current head, 8 pairs) | -13.9% [-20.9, -6.2] | -12.8% [-14.3, -11.2] |
| ClickBench Q10 | -3.2% [-4.3, -2.1] | -4.6% [-7.2, -2.0] |
| `SearchPhrase` (not sparse, control) | -1.3% [-5.3, +2.8] | -0.3% [-3.4, +2.9] |

Results are identical on both builds. A new test compares sparse and non-sparse copies of the same data (`String` and `Nullable(String)`, empty and non-empty defaults); mutating either branch of the new function makes it fail, and the `*sparse*` stateless tests give the same results as on master. Two queries are added to `tests/performance/sparse_column.xml`.

issue.title: `IcebergLocal` `INSERT` ignores declared `DEFAULT`s and `CHECK` constraints

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Data lake table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) integration.

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- An `INSERT` into an `IcebergLocal` table writes type defaults for omitted columns and skips `CHECK` constraints that `CREATE` accepted.
- Trigger: columns with `DEFAULT 'x'` and `DEFAULT k * 100` plus `CHECK k > 0`, then `INSERT` with only `k`.
- `MergeTree` writes `x` and `k * 100` and rejects -1 with `VIOLATED_CONSTRAINT`; Iceberg stores empty string and 0 and accepts -1.
- No error is raised and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` still shows the defaults, while `DESCRIBE` and `system.columns` show none.

Root cause: Before taking the metadata snapshot, `updateExternalDynamicMetadataIfExists` rebuilds metadata via `buildStorageMetadataFromState` from Iceberg schema names and types only, and `StorageObjectStorage.cpp:681` replaces the `CREATE`-time metadata with it. Iceberg's `shouldReloadSchemaForConsistency` always returns `true`, so declared defaults and constraints are dropped on every query.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1547` calls `updateExternalDynamicMetadataIfExists` before it takes the metadata snapshot. `StorageObjectStorage.cpp:678-681` asks `shouldReloadSchemaForConsistency`, and Iceberg always returns `true` (`IcebergMetadata.cpp:1996`). `buildStorageMetadataFromState` (`IcebergMetadata.cpp:1964`) builds `ColumnsDescription` from the Iceberg schema's names and types only. `new_metadata = *metadata_snapshot` then replaces the `CREATE`-time metadata, which carried the defaults (`:389`) and the constraints (`:416`). The `INSERT` pipeline gets built from metadata that has neither.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:681`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2170ef336e0/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp#L681) — `new_metadata = *metadata_snapshot` drops the CREATE-declared defaults and constraints
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/IcebergMetadata.cpp:1964`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2170ef336e0/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/IcebergMetadata.cpp#L1964) — `buildStorageMetadataFromState`: columns from the Iceberg schema names and types only
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/IcebergMetadata.cpp:1996`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2170ef336e0/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/IcebergMetadata.cpp#L1996) — `shouldReloadSchemaForConsistency` always `true` for Iceberg
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:873`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2170ef336e0/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp#L873) — same rebuild on the `read` path when the state is not pinned
- [`tests/performance/scripts/iceberg_engine.py:184`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2170ef336e0/tests/performance/scripts/iceberg_engine.py#L184) — PR harness forwards `DEFAULT` to Iceberg tables

Impact: Rows written to ClickHouse-created Iceberg tables silently carry `''`/`0`/`NULL` instead of the declared `DEFAULT`s, and values that violate a `CHECK` constraint are accepted. Nothing errors, and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` suggests the defaults apply. In #128261 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause)'s CI, `array_index_low_cardinality_strings` in `iceberg_local`/`iceberg_s3` measures `has(arr, ...)` over empty arrays. On 100k rows, `has(arr, 'asdf337')` matches 0 rows on Iceberg vs 10 on `MergeTree`. That test is row 277 of `iceberg_vs_mergetree.md` (Iceberg 0.12x/0.14x of `MergeTree`).

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master` (`2f186f9854ea`); not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Requires `allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1`.

```bash
# Test: an INSERT into an Iceberg table fills the omitted columns with their DEFAULT and checks the CONSTRAINT of the table.

ICEBERG_TABLE_PATH="/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/lakehouses/default_t_defaults"
rm -rf "${ICEBERG_TABLE_PATH}"

clickhouse-client --allow_insert_into_iceberg=1 --query "
    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_defaults;
    CREATE TABLE t_defaults (k Int32, s String DEFAULT 'x', e Int64 DEFAULT k * 100, CONSTRAINT k_positive CHECK k > 0) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('${ICEBERG_TABLE_PATH}');
    INSERT INTO t_defaults (k) VALUES (1), (2);
"
clickhouse-client --allow_insert_into_iceberg=1 --query "INSERT INTO t_defaults (k) VALUES (-1)" 2>&1 | grep -o -m1 'VIOLATED_CONSTRAINT'
clickhouse-client --query "SELECT * FROM t_defaults ORDER BY k"

clickhouse-client --query "DROP TABLE t_defaults"
rm -rf "${ICEBERG_TABLE_PATH}"
```

Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`2f186f9854ea`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

Omitted columns get their declared `DEFAULT` values (rows `1 x 100`, `2 x 200`) and inserting -1 fails with `VIOLATED_CONSTRAINT`.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
VIOLATED_CONSTRAINT
1	x	100
2	x	200
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

Rows are stored as `-1 '' 0`, `1 '' 0`, `2 '' 0` with no error.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`2f186f9854ea`):

```
-1		0
1		0
2		0
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Two options. (a) In `updateExternalDynamicMetadataIfExists` and the matching rebuild in `read` (`StorageObjectStorage.cpp:871-876`), carry the declared defaults (by column name, when the type is unchanged), constraints and comment over to the rebuilt metadata. (b) Reject `DEFAULT`/`CONSTRAINT` at Iceberg `CREATE`, as `DeltaLakeMetadataDeltaKernel` does for catalog tables. Trade-off: (a) can attach a stale default to a column that was renamed or retyped outside ClickHouse; (b) breaks DDL that is accepted today. Harness, until then: treat `DEFAULT` like `MATERIALIZED` in `iceberg_engine._rewrite_column`, or skip-list `array_index_low_cardinality_strings`.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- `StorageObjectStorage::alter` (`StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1402-1422`) applies the `ALTER` to the reloaded in-memory metadata and persists it. Any `ALTER` on such a table probably erases the `DEFAULT`s from the stored definition too. Not tested.
- The table `COMMENT` set at `StorageObjectStorage.cpp:417` is dropped from the in-memory metadata by the same line. Not tested.

Found during automated review of [PR #128261](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128261); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr128261_001`

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
delta-kernel-rs and chdig are built as members of the Rust workspace in `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace`, with one `Cargo.lock`, one cargo target directory and features resolved once for all members, so the crates they share with the other Rust libraries are compiled once, in one parallel cargo run.

### Description

Step 3 of the layout in #86562, after #130348 (step 2).

- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs-cmake` and `contrib/chdig-cmake` get one-line wrapper crates (`pub use delta_kernel_ffi;`, `pub use chdig;`), imported through the workspace manifest like the other six.
- One environment for every member (`clickhouse_config_crate_env`: OpenSSL variables, `CFLAGS` with `-I contrib/openssl/include`, `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): build scripts track their environment, so any difference rebuilds shared crates every build.
- `resolver.feature-unification = "workspace"`: corrosion runs one `cargo rustc` per package, and cargo otherwise resolves features per package.
- The workspace manifest is also a root package, `_ch_rust_workspace`, with one feature per member. `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace/CMakeLists.txt` builds it with the enabled members' features before their runs, which then compile only their wrapper. Not with LTO, where each member's run does its own code generation. The wrappers are plain libraries imported with `OVERRIDE_CRATE_TYPE <crate>=staticlib`, so the root run writes no unused archives.
- `Cargo.lock` is resolved offline from `contrib/rust_vendor` (no `rust_vendor` change); delta-kernel-rs and chdig take the workspace's semver-compatible versions.
- The `aws-lc-sys` `LDFLAGS` workaround goes: the crate left the graph.
- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` moves to the merge commit of ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#22: the pin of #130062 plus `crate-type = ["lib"]`.

Rust-only cold build, `-j48`: Debug 200 s / 1027 s CPU on master, 108 s / 779 s here. With ThinLTO 13.2 min on master, 18.4 min here: the members' LTO runs queue on the one target directory.

Validation, x86_64 Debug:
- 1240 compile units in 3 target directories before, 799 in one after, no crate built with two feature sets.
- Build and link pass; a no-op build compiles nothing, also alternating between members; the member archives are the same cargo units as without the root package.
- Delta Lake stateless tests 77/77; prql, pco, polyglot, vortex and wasm tests 98/99 (the other fails on master too); `chdig --help` works.

Replaces the C++ `DWARF` input format parser (`DWARFBlockInputFormat`, `DB::Elf`, `llvm::DWARFContext`) with a Rust crate in `contrib/dwarf-cmake` (`ch_rust::dwarf`) built on the already-vendored `gimli 0.33.0`, `object 0.39.1`, and `memchr 2.8.3` crates (no `contrib/rust_vendor` changes).

`DWARFBlockInputFormat` keeps ownership of the `MMappedFile` / `PODArray<char>` input buffer and the worker queue. Rust parses the ELF64 header, debug sections, compilation units, DIEs, line tables, and range lists (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in all parser modules, `unsafe` only in `ffi.rs` with `catch_unwind`), and writes batches directly into ClickHouse `PODArray` column buffers via reserve/cancel callbacks. `ENABLE_DWARF_PARSER` is also decoupled from `contrib/llvm-project-cmake`, so enabling `DWARF` alone no longer builds or links `LLVMDebugInfoDWARF`.

30-run ABBA results on `c7i.4xlarge` (5.09 GB `clickhouse` binary, 140.2M rows, `FORMAT Null`):
```text
SELECT ranges (t=8):                    7.58s -> 6.10s (0.81x time, 0.60x instructions)
SELECT offset (t=1 / t=2 / t=8):       36.42s -> 28.00s / 17.30s -> 13.25s / 7.24s -> 6.05s (0.77x-0.83x time, 0.61x instructions)
SELECT tag, ancestor_* (t=8):           7.86s -> 6.58s (0.84x time, 0.74x instructions)
SELECT name, linkage_name, decl_* (t=8):7.56s -> 6.40s (0.85x time, 0.71x instructions)
SELECT attr_* (t=8):                    8.70s -> 7.75s (0.89x time, 0.86x instructions)
SELECT * (t=8 / t=16):                 10.79s -> 10.06s / 11.07s -> 10.38s (0.93x-0.94x time, 0.99x instructions)
Stripped binary / .text delta:         -363.6 KiB / -380.1 KiB
```

Valid fixture outputs match the old parser bit-for-bit across the 85-file differential corpus (`02225`, `02896`, `04340`, `05139`, `05507` pass; 89 Rust tests pass under Miri, ASan, and TSan; 23.2M ASan libFuzzer runs on `format_fuzzer` and `dwarf_abi_fuzzer` with 0 crashes). Intentional rejections of malformed/non-ELF64-LE inputs that the old parser accepted or truncated (such as `E-02`/`E-03`/`E-06`/`E-11`, `U-01`/`U-07`/`U-08`/`U-10`/`U-15`/`U-16`, `F-16`, and `L-03`/`L-05`) are documented in `contrib/dwarf-cmake/COMPATIBILITY.md`.

Two things to confirm with maintainers:
- Preliminary cross-targets with `ENABLE_RUST=OFF` (`riscv64`, `loongarch64`, `illumos`) have `USE_DWARF_PARSER` off (`s390x`, `ppc64le`, `x86_64`, and `aarch64` build with `ENABLE_RUST=ON`).
- Malformed unit headers (including raw `SHF_COMPRESSED` `.debug_info` where the old parser logged a stderr warning and returned 0 rows) and the other tightened cases in `COMPATIBILITY.md` now return `CANNOT_PARSE_ELF` or `CANNOT_PARSE_DWARF`.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

issue.body:
### Company or project name

ClickHouse

### Describe what's wrong

`CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Iceberg... ORDER BY x` writes the sort order with `"null-order": "nulls-first"` (hardcoded in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp`), while ClickHouse sorts rows by that key with NULLs last for `ASC` (`sortBlockByKeyDescription`, nulls direction 1).

The table metadata therefore describes a different order than the one ClickHouse writes. Data files written by ClickHouse are not tagged with `sort_order_id` today, so nothing relies on it yet, but:
- another engine writing sorted files to this table follows `nulls-first`, while ClickHouse's in-order read assumes NULLs last for the same key (not checked);
- tagging ClickHouse-written files as sorted would claim an order they do not have.

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Reproduced on master (`6e962c3b7e0`, 26.11). Not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (x Nullable(Int64)) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/path/t') ORDER BY x;
INSERT INTO t SELECT if(number % 3 = 0, NULL, number) FROM numbers(9) SETTINGS max_threads = 1, max_insert_threads = 1;
SELECT x FROM file('/path/t/data/*.parquet', Parquet);
```

- Stored rows: `1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, NULL, NULL, NULL` (NULLs last).
- `metadata/v2.metadata.json`: `"sort-orders": [{"fields": [{"direction": "asc", "null-order": "nulls-first", "source-id": 1, "transform": "identity"}], "order-id": 1}]`.

### Expected behavior

The written `null-order` matches what ClickHouse sorts: `nulls-last` for `ASC`, `nulls-first` for `DESC` (or the sort follows the declared `null-order`).

### Error message and/or stacktrace

None.
