issue.title: Refuse to run with shared objects injected by `/etc/ld.so.preload` and other means

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Server wire protocols + request/response handling (native TCP, HTTP, MySQL/PostgreSQL wire protoc...

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with backwards incompatible changes

issue.body:
At startup, ClickHouse removes `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `LD_AUDIT` and similar variables from the environment and re-executes itself. That does not protect against the other ways to inject code into the process. This PR extends the check, `checkHarmfulEnvironment` (formerly `checkHarmfulEnvironmentVariables`), with three more steps that run on Linux with glibc after the environment is clean:

1. **`/etc/ld.so.preload`**: the dynamic loader loads every object listed in this file into every process, the same as with `LD_PRELOAD`, and re-executing does not help. If the file has any entries (comments with `#` are ignored), ClickHouse prints the entries and exits.
2. **Loaded shared objects**: `dl_iterate_phdr` lists everything in the loader's main namespace. Each object must be the main executable, the vDSO, or a transitive `DT_NEEDED` dependency of the executable, matched by `DT_SONAME`. The closure is read from the in-memory dynamic sections, so the allowed set follows from the binary itself (today that's `libc`, `libm`, `libpthread`, `librt`, `libdl` and the loader) and there's no hardcoded per-architecture list. This catches `ld.so --preload` and anything else that slips past the environment check.
3. **Executable file mappings**: auditing libraries (`LD_AUDIT`, `ld.so --audit`) live in a separate loader namespace, which `dl_iterate_phdr` doesn't report. So every file-backed executable mapping in `/proc/self/maps` must belong to the same file (device + inode) as the mapping of one of the expected objects. If `/proc` is not mounted, this step is skipped.

The check runs at the start of `main`, before glibc loads its own plugins on demand (NSS modules, `libgcc_s`).

Tested with a dynamically linked test program built against this file, and with the `clickhouse` binary:
- `server`, `local`, `client` and `keeper` start normally; later on-demand loading by glibc (NSS for name resolution) is not affected;
- plain start, `LD_PRELOAD`/`LD_AUDIT` in the environment (stripped and re-executed as before), and starting through the loader explicitly (`ld.so ./clickhouse`): all start normally;
- `ld.so --preload lib.so`: refused because of the unexpected loaded object;
- `ld.so --audit lib.so`: refused because of the unexpected executable mapping;
- `/etc/ld.so.preload` (tested in a private mount namespace with an overlay on `/etc`): an empty file or one with only comments is accepted, while real or nonexistent entries are refused.

Note: some monitoring agents (e.g. Dynatrace OneAgent) install themselves in `/etc/ld.so.preload`. On such hosts ClickHouse will now refuse to start, so this is marked as a backward-incompatible change.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Backward Incompatible Change


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
ClickHouse refuses to start if shared objects are injected into its process with `/etc/ld.so.preload`, `ld.so --preload`, or auditing libraries. Previously only the `LD_PRELOAD` and similar environment variables were handled, by removing them and re-executing.

issue.title: Refreshable materialized view in a Replicated database fails to load if Keeper is unreachable at startup; the failed load job is never retried, and the database's DDL and the DDL worker stay broken until a restart

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Confirmed user-visible misbehaviour in official release

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Refreshable materialized views: scheduled/periodic refresh, refresh state machine, refresh orches...

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
### Company or project name

Halter https://github.com/halter-corp

### Describe what's wrong

If the server starts while Keeper is not reachable yet, attaching a refreshable materialized view in a `Replicated` database fails (`Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes`). The failed load job is never retried after Keeper becomes reachable. The jobs that depend on it stay `CANCELED`: `startup table` of the view, `startup ddl worker`, and on 25.8 also the view's target table.

As a result, until the server is restarted:

- DDL in that database waits 300 s and fails with `Cannot enqueue query on this replica, most likely because replica is busy with previous queue entries. (UNFINISHED)`;
- `SELECT` from the view's target table fails with `Waited job failed` (25.8.33; works on 26.10.3.7);
- in a cluster, `ON CLUSTER` queries time out on the other replicas with `is not finished on 1 of 2 hosts (0 of them are currently executing the task, 0 are inactive)`.

The server itself stays up and answers other queries, so health checks keep passing. A restart (with Keeper reachable) fixes it.

We hit this in production on Kubernetes when an upgrade restarted ClickHouse and Keeper pods at the same time: one replica started in the same second as the first Keeper pod, before Keeper had a quorum, and stayed in this state for about 2.5 hours until we restarted it.

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes. Same result on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.10.3.7` with `clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper:26.10.3.7` (the `latest` images), with one difference: `SELECT` from the view's target table works there, because the target table is no longer cancelled with the view. The view, `startup ddl worker` and DDL in the database stay broken until a restart. On 26.10 the load error reads `Cannot resolve any of provided ZooKeeper hosts due to DNS error` (the stopped Keeper container's name does not resolve), on 25.8 `Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes`.

### How to reproduce

Versions: `altinity/clickhouse-server:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable` with `altinity/clickhouse-keeper:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable` and `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.10.3.7` with `clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper:26.10.3.7`. One server, one Keeper, default settings.

`keeper_config.xml` (copied to `/etc/clickhouse-keeper/keeper_config.xml`):

```xml
<clickhouse>
  <listen_host>0.0.0.0</listen_host>
  <keeper_server>
    <tcp_port>9181</tcp_port><server_id>1</server_id>
    <log_storage_path>/var/lib/clickhouse-keeper/log</log_storage_path>
    <snapshot_storage_path>/var/lib/clickhouse-keeper/snapshots</snapshot_storage_path>
    <raft_configuration><server><id>1</id><hostname>keeper</hostname><port>9234</port></server></raft_configuration>
  </keeper_server>
</clickhouse>
```

`server.xml` (copied to `/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/server.xml`):

```xml
<clickhouse>
  <zookeeper><node><host>keeper</host><port>9181</port></node></zookeeper>
  <macros><shard>01</shard><replica>r1</replica></macros>
</clickhouse>
```

Steps:

```sh
docker network create repro
docker create --name keeper --network repro --network-alias keeper altinity/clickhouse-keeper:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable
docker cp keeper_config.xml keeper:/etc/clickhouse-keeper/keeper_config.xml
docker create --name server --network repro altinity/clickhouse-server:25.8.33.10003.altinitystable
docker cp server.xml server:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/server.xml
docker start keeper server
```

```sql
CREATE DATABASE db ENGINE = Replicated('/clickhouse/databases/db', '{shard}', '{replica}');
CREATE TABLE db.target (id UInt64, v UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree(v) ORDER BY id;
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW db.mv REFRESH EVERY 1 HOUR APPEND TO db.target AS
    SELECT number AS id, 1 AS v FROM numbers(10);
```

Restart the server while Keeper is down, then bring Keeper back:

```sh
docker stop server keeper
docker start server     # Keeper is still down
sleep 20
docker start keeper     # Keeper reachable again
sleep 30
```

```sql
SELECT job, status, exception FROM system.asynchronous_loader WHERE status != 'OK';
SELECT count() FROM db.target;
CREATE TABLE db.after_keeper (id UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree ORDER BY id;
```

### Expected behavior

Once Keeper is reachable, the view is attached (the load job is retried), or at least the database and the DDL worker recover without a server restart.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

`system.asynchronous_loader`, 30 s after Keeper is back (unchanged later):

```
load table db.mv        FAILED    Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table db.mv' failed: Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes: Cannot attach table `db`.`mv` from metadata file store/…
startup ddl worker      CANCELED  Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup ddl worker' -> Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table db.mv' failed: …
startup table db.mv     CANCELED  Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.mv' -> Code: 695. …
startup table db.target CANCELED  Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.target' -> Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.mv' -> …
```

DDL in the database (after 300 s):

```
Code: 341. DB::Exception: Timeout: Cannot enqueue query on this replica, most likely because replica is busy with previous queue entries. (UNFINISHED)
```

`SELECT count() FROM db.target` (25.8.33 only; works on 26.10.3.7):

```
Code: 722. DB::Exception: Waited job failed: Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.target' -> Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table db.mv' -> Code: 695. …
```

In the two-replica production cluster, the affected replica logged every few seconds:

```
<Error> DDLWorker(<db>): Error on initialization of <db>: Code: 722. DB::Exception: Waited job failed: Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table <db>.<target>' -> Code: 696. DB::Exception: Load job 'startup table <db>.<mv>' -> Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table <db>.<mv>' failed: Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: Cannot use any of provided ZooKeeper nodes: Cannot attach table …
```

and `ON CLUSTER` DDL from the other replica failed with `Code: 159 … is not finished on 1 of 2 hosts (0 of them are currently executing the task, 0 are inactive)`.

After a server restart (Keeper reachable): no failed load jobs, `SELECT` returns 10, DDL succeeds.

### Additional context

Possibly related, but with different causes: #89693 (`There is no a local address in host list` on a fresh pod), #124717, #126745.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `DeltaLake` queries hanging forever, without reacting to `KILL QUERY`, when delta-kernel could not create the thread that hands a result back (for example at a container PID limit).


### Description

On 26.3.12.3, a `DeltaLake` query hangs forever and ignores `KILL QUERY` when the server cannot create a new thread: in #128033 a `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = DeltaLake` run by `DDLWorker` blocked for 26 hours at a Kubernetes PID limit and stalled the distributed DDL queue. Master and 26.8 to 26.10 pin the same kernel code.

Cause: delta-kernel's `block_on` handed every result back through `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. When no thread can be created, tokio panics after queueing the closure that owns the result sender, so the sender is never dropped and the caller's `recv()` waits forever. Every synchronous kernel call goes through `block_on`.

Change: `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` moves from `88ff5a94` to `86762ee5`, the merge commit of ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#19 (a cherry-pick of delta-io/delta-kernel-rs#3202), which sends the result directly from the async task. It touches only `kernel/src/engine/default/executor.rs`, with no Cargo manifest or lock change. The fork branch tip carries unrelated changes, so the pin is the fix commit, not the tip.

Validation: a standalone kernel program that lowers `RLIMIT_NPROC` before calling `block_on` hangs on `88ff5a94` (panic `OS can't spawn worker thread`, caller blocked in `futex_wait`) and returns the result on `86762ee5`, in 6 of 6 runs each. The server builds with the new pin, and 59 local DeltaLake stateless tests pass. No ClickHouse test is added: running a server out of threads at exactly this point is not deterministic in a functional test.

#130062 moves the pointer to `c694ca3e`, which already contains this commit.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

issue.body:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/121039


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Backward Incompatible Change


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `text` index `preprocessor` or `postprocessor` expression that contains a subquery or a table reference in `IN` is now rejected, including when a table is loaded. Besides `IN (SELECT ...)`, which failed on every `INSERT` with a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, this rejects forms that worked, such as a scalar subquery or `IN` over a `Set` table: drop or rewrite such an index before upgrading, otherwise its table fails to load.

### Description

A `text` index whose transform contains `IN (SELECT ...)` is accepted at `CREATE TABLE`, then fails on the
first `INSERT` and aborts debug and sanitizer builds.

**Root cause.** `buildActionsDAGFromAST` compiles the transform through `ExpressionAnalyzer`, which
allocates a throwaway `PreparedSets` and still runs `makeSet`, so `IN (SELECT ...)` enters the DAG as a
`FutureSetFromSubquery` nothing ever fills; the index-build path has no `CreatingSetStep`, so the build
reaches `FunctionIn::executeImpl` with an unbuilt set.

**Change.** Reject it at DDL time with the guard the tree already has for this class,
`checkExpressionDoesntContainSubqueries` (`7896defecb553`, whose comment names this failure mode).
`IndexDescription::getIndexFromAST` applied it to the index *expression* only; it now also checks the
`preprocessor` and `postprocessor` type arguments, right after expanding their aliases. The helper takes a
`subject` so the message names the context, and the three existing call sites keep byte-identical messages.

Building the set instead would be wrong: it is recorded nowhere in the part, and the transform is rebuilt
where no query exists (`IMergeTreeDataPart::removeIfNeeded` re-analyses it, failing `UNKNOWN_TABLE` once the
referenced table has shut down), so postings would silently disagree with the predicate.

**Compatibility.** The check runs wherever the index definition is parsed, including table load, like the
existing check on the index expression. So a table created by an older version with such a transform fails to
load after upgrade, including forms that worked: on master a scalar subquery
(`concat(val, assumeNotNull((SELECT 'x')))`) or `IN` over a `Set` table writes and searches correctly. The
rest of the server starts, but `system.tables` and `DROP TABLE` wait on that table and fail. Dropping the
index before upgrading avoids it.

**Validation.** Deterministic repro both directions, `CREATE` and `ALTER ... ADD INDEX` cases in the two
negative blocks, the text index test family green, and the two edited tests 90/90 with
randomization on and off.

issue.body:
Closes #123744

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123834
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125652
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125713

`-0.0 = 0.0`, but a `bloom_filter` index holds the hash of each value's bits, which differ for the two zeros. On master, a lookup of one zero skips the granules holding the other, so `f = 0` returns `[3]` with the index and `[1,3]` without (#123744).

#123834 fixed this and was reverted in #125652, because `05325_bloom_filter_signed_zero` failed with randomized `map_serialization_version_for_zero_level_parts = 'with_buckets'`. The cause was in the bucketed `Map`, not in the index: `m[0.0]` did not find a `-0.0` key, which #125713 fixes. This PR reintroduces #123834 (commit "Reintroduce looking up both signed zeros in a `bloom_filter` index") and keeps the follow-up below.

## Change

- **A zero is looked up as both `0.0` and `-0.0`** (#123834). `hashWithFieldAndOtherZero` adds the hash of the other zero for `=`, `has`, `hasAny`, `mapContainsKey`, `mapContainsValue`, `mapKeys`, and, on a bucketed `Map`, `m[k] = v` and `m[k] IN (...)`. `IN` on a float column compares bits, so it still looks up only the given zero.
- **`hasAll` with a float zero keeps pruning.** #123834 makes `hasAll` with a zero element not use the index, because `FUNCTION_HAS_ALL` needs every hash in the granule while one of the two zeros is enough. A granule matches only if every predicate entry matches, and under `FUNCTION_HAS_ANY` an entry matches if any of its hashes does. So one entry per element, with both hashes for a zero, is exactly `hasAll`.
- **`arrayJoin(col) = constant` uses the index for float elements.** `bloomFilterHashDomainMatches` excluded floats because `-0.0` equals `0.0` but hashes apart. With both zeros looked up through `hashWithFieldAndOtherZero`, the `equals` arm now allows a float element with an integer or float constant. `convertFieldToType` converts it exactly or returns Null, in which case the index is not used, for example `0.1` against `Float32`. The `IN` arm still excludes floats.
- **`LEFT ARRAY JOIN` padding.** `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` pads an empty array with the default value, which the index does not hold. A constant equal to that value, such as `0.0` or `-0.0` for a float element, does not use the index.

On the 103 rows of `05327` with `index_granularity = 1`, the bloom filter selects these granules:

| Query | master | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `has(a, 0)` | 5, returns `[0,101]` instead of `[0,100,101]` | 12 |
| `hasAll(a, [-0.0])` | 7, returns `[100]` instead of `[0,100,101]` | 12 |
| `hasAll(a, [0.0, 42.0])` | 1, returns `[101]` instead of `[100,101]` | 2 |
| `arrayJoin(a) = 42` | not used (103) | 11 |
| `arrayJoin(a) = 0.0` | not used (103) | 12 |
| `arrayJoin(b) = 0.5`, `Float32` | not used (103) | 4 |
| `arrayJoin(b) = 0.1`, `Float32` | not used (103) | not used (103) |

`05325_bloom_filter_signed_zero` compares each zero lookup with and without the index, including `m[0.0] = 'x'` and `m[0.0] IN ('x')` on a table pinned to bucketed `Map` serialization, which return `[3]` instead of `[1,3]` on master. `05327_bloom_filter_signed_zero_has_all_array_join` does the same for `hasAll`, `hasAny` and `arrayJoin(col) = c`, including `-0.0`/`0.0`, `Float32` and the inexact `0.1`, and checks with `force_data_skipping_indices` and `max_rows_to_read` that the index prunes. Both fail on master and pass here, also under randomized settings, and the bucketed `m[0.0]` queries give `[1,3]` with `enable_analyzer = 0` and `1`. Over 111 `arrayJoin(col) = c`, `hasAll` and `hasAny` queries on `Array(Float64)`, `Array(Float32)` and `Array(LowCardinality(Float64))`, with constants such as `-0.0`, `nan`, `inf`, `0.1`, `16777217`, `9007199254740993`, `NULL` and integers of different widths, the result with the index equals the result without it.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `bloom_filter` index lookup of `0.0` or `-0.0` no longer skips granules that hold the other zero, which returned wrong results, for example for `WHERE f = 0` over a `-0.0` value. The index is also used for `arrayJoin(arr) = constant` on a float array column, and keeps skipping granules for `hasAll` with a zero element, such as `hasAll(arr, [0.0, 42.0])`.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/122437

<!--

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- New Feature


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Statistics can be declared on `JSON` columns (for example `j JSON STATISTICS(uniq_v2)`): they are built for every path of the column, including dynamic paths and paths stored in shared data, and are used to estimate filters on paths. `uniq` and `uniq_v2` can be declared on `Dynamic` columns, and a filter comparing a `Dynamic` column with literals of different types no longer fails with `Cannot compare` during query planning. Closes #125450.

### Description

Only `basic` was accepted on a `JSON` column (`Code: 708`), so filters on paths got default constants. In #122437 every filter of a 4-table join is on paths: `x1` is estimated at 0.1% of its rows, so join reordering hashes a 3M-row intermediate result.

**Change.** Statistics declared on a `JSON` column are built for each path: typed, dynamic and in shared data. A path gets the declared types that support its type, plus `basic`, which counts the rows without the path as `NULL`; `uniq` and `uniq_v2` do not count `NULL` of `Dynamic` (`Dynamic STATISTICS(uniq_v2)` is accepted too). `auto_statistics_types` are not built per path: only explicit declarations change, including an existing `JSON STATISTICS(basic)`. `Nullable(JSON)` and typed paths of type `JSON` are not covered, and part pruning does not use path statistics. Literals compared with one `Dynamic` value may differ in type, so an equality on it is estimated alone, other comparisons get constants. This also fixes `Cannot compare` at planning on plain `Dynamic` columns (26.8, 26.10).

Path statistics live in the column's statistics, so files, cache, merges, mutations and renames stay keyed by the column. Older servers skip them in parts (a reserved mask bit of the V4 layout), but reject the new declarations. Paths read from disk stay serialized until a query uses them.

**Validation.** The test is the #122437 reproducer at 1/100 scale, a path in shared data, a path missing from a part (also after a merge and a mutation), literals of two types on one path, `IS NULL` on a typed path; master fails at `CREATE`. Release build, full-scale #122437: 4.1-4.6 s before, 0.26-0.32 s with `STATISTICS(uniq_v2)`, same result. Costs: inserting 1M rows with ~105 paths per row takes 3.2-4.0 s instead of 2.1-2.4 s; planning a filter over 100 parts of 2000 paths, 5-6 ms warm.

issue.title: Do not infer join conditions through constant join keys in join reordering

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with some performance improvements

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Query plan optimization: physical plan steps, plan-level rewrites and optimizations (QueryPlan pa...

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Allows running workflows for external contributors

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Join reordering no longer treats a join key that holds the same constant in every row (for example `materialize('x') AS src` in each joined subquery) as a key: it infers no join conditions through it and costs a join on it as the cross product it is, so it no longer joins two tables on that key alone. Such a join could turn a query that takes a second into a `max_execution_time` timeout.

### Description

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128041

With `enable_join_transitive_predicates` (default since 26.6), `p.src = w.src` and `p.src = r.src`, where `src` is `materialize('wlr')` in every CTE, connected `w` and `r`. Without an NDV for `src`, `w JOIN r` was priced as a key join (`max(|w|, |r|)`), so as the smallest tables they were joined first, on the synthesized `w.src = r.src` alone. With default settings on master, tables of 1M / 100k / 100k rows hit `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` after 60 s at 126M join rows, versus `1000000` in 0.7 s with the setting off.

An equality with a constant side links no two relations. `buildColumnEquivalences` now skips equalities on a column holding one value in every row (literals and deterministic functions of them, UNION ALL branches with the same literal, GROUP BY keys, sorting, DISTINCT, LIMIT/OFFSET output, the preserved side of a sub-join; a miss keeps today's plan), and `computeSelectivity` no longer counts a written one as a key: only a real NDV of the other side gives its selectivity, else its join is costed as a cross product, except an `ANY`, semi or anti join. Written equalities still link their relations; DPsub interesting orders skip an equality of two constants, so a constant key next to a sorted key still allows a sort-merge join. Results cannot change. `one_thousand_joins` (666 joins on `1`) now plans as with the setting off (debug: 3.8 s vs 3.7 s; 2.5 s before).

The new test has 16 `EXPLAIN` checks failing on master, passing with the fix (all four algorithms, randomized estimates, each handled case, written constant keys), an NDV check and six controls; `05480` gains two sort-merge cases. Removing any handled case fails its checks; 50 randomized runs pass. On @ den-crane's 40-seed repro, 13-15 of 40 plans per algorithm joined on `src` only before, 0 after.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed a view that reads a temporary table by its unqualified name failing with `UNKNOWN_TABLE` (or reading a table of the same name in the view's database) after a server restart or `ATTACH DATABASE`, because the name was qualified with the view's database when the view was loaded. Closes #129449.

### Description

On 26.10.2.103-stable, a view that reads a session temporary table by its unqualified name fails with `UNKNOWN_TABLE` after a server restart (#129449), or reads a table of that name in the view's database.

Caused by #114923 (CI build of its merge `659cc1c2` fails, of its first parent `f75df105` passes): `qualifyNamesFromLegacyMetadata`, which repairs names that SQL UDF expansion left bare in older metadata, also qualified an ordinary view's SELECT with the view's database on load, where no session exists. `CREATE VIEW` leaves a temporary table's name unqualified on purpose.

`StorageView` now does that repair itself and keeps the SELECT as stored. When the reading query has temporary tables, the stored SELECT is re-qualified under that query, so a temporary table of the session takes precedence, as at `CREATE`. Otherwise the name resolves to the view's database, as on 26.10, also in another table's `CONSTRAINT` evaluated at attach. `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` and `NONE` views always use the repaired SELECT, since they run without the reader's temporary tables. Materialized views, column defaults, constraints and the dependency graphs are unchanged.

Validation: the test reloads views with `DETACH`/`ATTACH DATABASE`. Eight read temporary objects (FROM, JOIN, `IN`, scalar subquery, `dictGet`, a temporary view, a view over a view, a temporary table named like a table of the view's database): each fails on master and passes with the fix, also with randomized settings, as does the issue's repro across a real restart. Passing on both: six controls (materialized views, dictionary, `ReplicatedMergeTree`, `Replicated` database), a table whose `CONSTRAINT` reads such a view attaching (it failed on the previous head of this PR), and `DEFINER`/`NONE` views and a reader without the temporary table reading the view's database, also after an `ALTER` from a session that has it.

On 26.3, 26.8 and 26.10, `toString(k) = '999999999999999999'` over a `UInt64` key returns 0 instead of 1 when one granule holds 999999999999999999 and 1000000000000000000. `ToStringMonotonicity` compared `floor(log10(x))` in `double`, which gives `n` for `x = 10^n - 1` from 15 digits on, so such a range counted as monotonic although its texts are in the opposite order. The digit count is now exact (`common::digits10`); 0 stays apart from 1..9 as before, because a `Bool` renders them as configurable strings.

Since #118957 (26.10), `toString(k) IN (SELECT <integers>)` over an integer sorting key reads every granule, where 26.8 pruned (#130315). #118957 declines a non-`String` set element over a string column, because `IN` parses the column (`'02'` and `'2'` are both `2`) while the index renders the element. When the string is the text that the key's own chain computes from a native integer (`toString`, `CAST`/`_CAST` to `String`), it holds only canonical numerals, so the set and the index agree; the same holds for `Date`. The decline now exempts exactly that case; types with a custom serialization (`Bool`, also inside `SimpleAggregateFunction`) stay declined. This path needs the exact digit count: 26.8 pruned it with the same wrong result. Reverting #118957 would bring back the wrong results it fixed (`s IN (SELECT toUInt8(2))` over a `String` key holding `'02'`).

Validation: on the issue's setup the first parent of #118957 and this PR select 1186/3668 granules, master 3668/3668, 39 rows on all. Both tests fail on master; every indexed count matches a full-scan `countIf`, and `max_rows_to_read` checks pin the pruning, also for 19-digit keys. 50 randomized runs pass.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130317
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117248


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `FINAL` query on a table whose row policy compares `ORDER BY` columns with a value computed once per query, such as `currentUser()`, `now()` or an `IN (subquery)` set, applies the policy before the merge again, as in 26.8, instead of reading and merging every row first. Closes #130317.

### Description

Since 26.9 a row policy like `c2 = substring(currentUser(), 1, 3)` on an `ORDER BY` column is applied after `FINAL`, and PREWHERE with it, so the whole table is read and merged before the policy filters it. On the query in #130317 this costs 9.7x memory and 2.7x time with the same result. Policies using `now()`, `currentDatabase()` or `IN (subquery)` are deferred too.

#117248 added `node->isDeterministic()` to `isNodeDeterministic`, the gate of `isRowPolicyDeferredAfterFinal`. For a `COLUMN` node it returns `is_deterministic_constant`, which the analyzer sets to false for a constant folded from a non-deterministic function. Applying the policy before `FINAL` only needs every version of one key to get the same verdict, and a constant has one value for the whole query, so it cannot split a dedup group. Only a lambda folded into a constant is evaluated per row, and `allNodeFunctions` still checks its body, so the cases #117248 fixed stay deferred (05141, 05182). This PR removes that check; the flag itself stays, the query condition cache needs it. I do not propose reverting #117248: it fixes wrong results (#117016).

On a `GraphiteMergeTree` table such a policy is again applied before the rollup, as a literal policy already is (26.8 behaviour, see #112817).

Validation: new test `05616_row_policy_after_final_query_constant` fails on master (the policy is deferred) and passes 50/50 with random settings, in the parallel-replicas flavour and with `serialize_query_plan = 1`. New performance test `final_row_policy_query_constant`. On the master release build, the issue's data, the `currentUser()` policy (the plan master uses) against the same policy as a literal (the plan this PR restores): 0.093 s / 1.20 GiB against 0.029 s / 288 MiB, and 0.183 s / 3.47 GiB against 0.033 s / 453 MiB with `compatibility = '24.0'` (medians of 10).

-->
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/125279
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115551

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Backward Incompatible Change


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The session form of `EXECUTE AS` now starts from the server default settings, so a setting changed before it is kept only where the target user may change it. A `NULL` value of a custom setting is now checked against the settings constraints like any other value. Added `EXECUTE AS user SETTINGS name = value`, which gives a custom setting that a settings profile of the user declares `CONST` without a value (such as a row policy key) a value the following queries cannot change, also on the remote nodes of distributed queries over clusters with `<secret>`. Off by default; enabled by the server setting `access_control_improvements.allow_execute_as_settings`. Closes #125279.

### Description

Option D, as @ pufit decided on #125279: a gateway impersonating a user gives it a value the forwarded SQL cannot change. A profile declares the setting `CONST` without a value (`CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE p SETTINGS SQL_tenant CONST`); `EXECUTE AS target SETTINGS SQL_tenant = 'acme' [query]` supplies the value after the target's profiles, so `CONST` refuses `SET`, `SET x = DEFAULT`, `SET profile` and query `SETTINGS`. Refused: the server setting off; a builtin or repeated name; a setting the target does not declare exactly `CONST` without a value, or gives a value (even `''`); a `users.xml` target; a value the caller could not set itself. Nested `EXECUTE AS` keeps the values.

Distributed reads over `<secret>` carry them in a new `ClientInfo` field (protocol 54497) covered by the secret hash; the remote node re-checks them (refused with the setting off); the sender refuses an older node. `Distributed` inserts, `ON CLUSTER` and `Replicated` DDL, `QueryRunner` jobs and background operations do not carry them (at most as an ordinary setting).

Two changes with the setting off, each in its own commit:
- Session-form `EXECUTE AS` starts from the server defaults, like the query form: before, `SET SQL_tenant = 'acme'; EXECUTE AS qu` kept `acme` although `qu` declares it `CONST`. A value set earlier now survives only where the target may change it (for a `readonly = 1` target, almost none); `clickhouse-client` resends it with every query and then gets the constraint error.
- `SET` or `SETTINGS` with a `NULL` custom setting value skipped the constraint checks, changing a `CONST` one and working with `readonly = 1` (subquery `SETTINGS` dropped it). It is now handled like any other value.

Validation: `05427_execute_as_settings` (50/50 randomized, fails on master) and `test_execute_as_settings` (setting off, `settings_constraints_replace_previous = false`, remote nodes with it off or on 25.3).

-->

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122358


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `hasAnyTokens`, `hasAllTokens` and `hasPhrase` on `m['key']` returning too few rows when a text index on `mapValues(m)` over `FixedString` values has a `postprocessor` or a tokenizer that keeps zero bytes: a row without the key reads the value type's default, which the index tokenizer and postprocessor can turn into a matching token, but the index skipped that row.

### Description

On 26.8 (26.8.10.6), the query below returns `[]`, and `[1]` with `SETTINGS use_skip_indexes = 0`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32, m Map(String, FixedString(6)),
    INDEX tix mapValues(m) TYPE text(tokenizer = ngrams(3), postprocessor = if(match(mapValues(m), '[a-z]'), mapValues(m), '#')))
ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 1;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, map()), (2, map('k', 'hello'));
SELECT groupArray(id) FROM (SELECT id FROM t WHERE hasAnyTokens(m['k'], '123') ORDER BY id);
```

For these three functions the plan rewrites the predicate with the index tokenizer and postprocessor. Row 1 has no key `k`, so `m['k']` is six zero bytes, whose `ngrams(3)` token `'\0\0\0'` the postprocessor maps to `'#'`, as it maps `'123'`: the rewritten predicate is true for that row. `mapValues(m)` stores nothing for it, yet index analysis used the atom for granule pruning and the direct-read hint.

`MergeTreeIndexConditionText` now computes the terms the index tokenizer and postprocessor give the map value type's default. When the needle's tokens are among them, the atom on `m['k']` is unknown for pruning and gets no hint, but keeps its search query, so the rewrite still applies. An index with a preprocessor, and `hasPhrase` with a postprocessor, keep such rows whenever the default yields a term, as does a postprocessor rejecting the default; a needle equal to the default is never preprocessed. Needles the default does not produce prune as before, and `Nullable` values are unchanged (an absent key reads `NULL`). #122358 covers `LIKE` and `match`, which the plan evaluates as written; this PR covers the functions it rewrites.

The new test covers `FixedString` and `LowCardinality(FixedString)` values, `hasPhrase` with and without `support_phrase_search`, and pruning controls. It fails on master and passes with the fix; 242 related text-index tests show no new failures.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... ADD ENUM VALUES` executed through an `Alias` table overwriting the enum values that a concurrent `ALTER` of the target table had added. Both queries succeeded, but the target's values were lost, and with `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query = 0` the target table could no longer be attached after a restart.

### Description

On 26.10.2.103, two concurrent `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN e ADD ENUM VALUES (...)`, one through an `Alias` table and one on its target, both succeed, but the values added on the target are lost. With `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query = 0` the target also gets a `MODIFY COLUMN` mutation written without a type, and after a restart the table cannot be attached (`MODIFY COLUMN mutation command doesn't specify type`, `LOGICAL_ERROR`). Found while answering https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130322#discussion_r4513071544.

Root cause: `InterpreterAlterQuery` validates and prepares the commands under the alias's locks, and `StorageAlias::alter` locks the target only afterwards. For `ADD ENUM VALUES`, `AlterCommands::prepare` stores the complete merged enum type, computed from the column type read before that lock, so it overwrites any value that a direct `ALTER` of the target committed in between. This does not depend on the query metadata cache that #130322 clears.

Change: after locking the target, `StorageAlias::alter` prepares a copy of the commands again against the target's current metadata and runs the target's `checkAlterIsPossible` on it. `prepare` now gives `createEnumAdd` a copy of the `ADD ENUM VALUES` list, which it numbers in place, so a second `prepare` does not read those numbers as explicit.

`validate` still runs before the target's lock, since it needs the unprepared commands.

Validation: `05618` races 20 `ADD ENUM VALUES` through an `Alias` against 20 on the target. On master it loses the target's values in 10 of 10 runs; with the fix it passes 50 of 50 randomized runs, also with the setting forced to 0 and to 1. `05619` checks that values added without a number through an `Alias` follow the target's largest value. Also checked: ReplicatedMergeTree and Memory targets, and a restart on the raced data.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed partition pruning of `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` on `ReplicatedMergeTree` when the predicate computes a function named like a stored column, for example ``toYYYYMM(d) = 202401 AND `toYYYYMM(d)` = 7``: a partition was skipped, or the `ALTER` failed with `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` when the column and the function have different types.


### Description
On 26.10.2.103 and 26.9.25.15 this `ALTER` succeeds but leaves the row (#130256):
```sql
CREATE TABLE t (d Date, `toYYYYMM(d)` UInt32) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{database}/t', '1') PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(d) ORDER BY tuple();
INSERT INTO t VALUES ('2024-01-01', 7);
ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE toYYYYMM(d) = 202401 AND `toYYYYMM(d)` = 7 SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2;
SELECT count() FROM t; -- 1, expected 0
```
With a `String` column of that name and ``length(`toYYYYMM(d)`) = 1``, it fails with `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` on 26.10.2.103 (without pruning, the row is deleted).

The mutation pruning DAG uses plain names, and the planner reuses a node by name. With the function first, the column reference `` `toYYYYMM(d)` `` resolves to the function node: the #130196 check in `KeyCondition` sees no input of that name, so the two atoms contradict on the partition key; with different types, building the DAG throws.

The change: before the DAG is built, if a function of the resolved predicate has the action name of a storage column, pruning is skipped and all partitions are mutated, as with `optimize_mutations_with_partition_pruning = 0`. The cost: on such a table, `DELETE WHERE toYYYYMM(d) = 202401` is no longer pruned. #125723 (mine, open) fixes the naming in the planner itself, mutation filter included.

Not covered: the mutation execution side (a part where only some rows match, `ALTER UPDATE`, lightweight `DELETE` still keep the rows, with or without pruning) and statistics part pruning in `SELECT`. On 26.9 and 26.10 the example's row stays even without pruning; master deletes it.

issue.body:
### Company or project name

ClickHouse

### Describe what's wrong


When uploading a file to minio in multipart upload in chunks, if the server returns 404 error, ClickHouse keeps retrying. The default retry attempts are configured as 500.  During every retry, Clickhouse logs broken pipe or connection closed errors, and does not recognize 404 error.

404 errors could happen, if there are huge uploads running, which could take more than 24hrs(some config limit), in which case object storage can garbage collect and remove the temporary uploaded files.

 ClickHouse writes the whole body before it reads any response and does not send "Expect: 100-continue", so the   write fails with "Broken pipe" / "Connection reset by peer". It never reads the 404, records the failure as a retryable network error, and retries (s3_retry_attempts + 1)^2 times (the SDK retry loop is nested inside   ClickHouse's own retry loop). issue.title: Do not kill a mutation whose transaction is past its commit point

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with some product improvements

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: ALTER UPDATE/DELETE and mutation execution over parts (including lightweight updates/deletes).

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Allows running workflows for external contributors

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: PR origin: delegated from the OranjeAI sibling fleet

issue.body:
### Changelog category (leave one):
- Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`KILL MUTATION` now reports `cant_cancel` for a mutation whose transaction has already passed its commit point, instead of removing state that the `COMMIT` still needs, which aborted the server with `LOGICAL_ERROR: Cannot find mutation`. Transactions are experimental (`allow_experimental_transactions`).


### Description

`StorageMergeTree::killMutation` erased the `current_mutations_by_version` entry and removed
`mutation_*.txt` **before** resolving the owning transaction, calling
`TransactionManager::rollbackTransaction` only afterwards. Past the commit point that rollback is a
no-op: `rollback` CASes `csn` `UnknownCSN -> RolledBackCSN`, which fails once `beforeCommit`
stored `CommittingCSN`, so `rollbackTransaction` early-returns. The erase, however, is permanent. The
committing thread then reached `afterCommit` -> `setMutationCSN`, could not find the entry, and
threw `LOGICAL_ERROR "Cannot find mutation"` from a `noexcept` function, aborting the server.

The fix resolves the transaction first and claims the cancellation through `rollback`'s `csn` CAS
before destroying anything. That CAS contends with `beforeCommit`'s
`UnknownCSN -> CommittingCSN` CAS on the same atomic, so exactly one wins and the decision is
atomic with respect to the commit point. When the commit wins, `killMutation` returns
`CancelCannotBeSent` (`cant_cancel`) and changes nothing. Reading the CSN is not enough:
the commit does not take `currently_processing_in_background_mutex`, so read-then-erase is a
TOCTOU that reproduces the same abort.

Refusing loses no work, because `beforeCommit` waits for every mutation of the transaction before
its CAS, and it matches how `executeRollback` and `KILL TRANSACTION` already treat a committing
transaction. The non-transactional path is unchanged, and `setMutationCSN` is
untouched: an early return there would silently drop a committed mutation's CSN.

Reaching this requires the experimental `allow_experimental_transactions`, hence `Improvement`.

Validation: the new stateless test drives the race deterministically with three new pauseable
failpoints, including a lost Keeper commit response that `runUpdatingThread` finalizes later; it
aborts the server without the fix and passes with it. 50/50 randomized and 50/50
plain runs pass, and a scope over every `KILL MUTATION` test plus the transaction-isolation
families shows no new failure against the unmodified build.

`afterCommit` remains `noexcept` with no internal guard, so any other future throw there is still
fatal; that is the #45736 family, for a separate change.

No related open issue found.

### Describe what's wrong

- A `text` index whose `postprocessor` expression contains `IN (SELECT ...)` is accepted at `CREATE TABLE`, but the first `INSERT` fails with `Logical error: 'Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in''` (`LOGICAL_ERROR`). On a debug or sanitizer build the server aborts.

Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126184#discussion_r4293581009: `maskedURL` in `MetadataStorageFromIndexPages.cpp` duplicated `maskedURI` in `ReadWriteBufferFromHTTP.cpp`.

`src/Common/maskURIPassword.h` gets `[[nodiscard]] std::string maskURICredentials(std::string_view)`, the existing in-place masking applied to a copy. A non-const `std::string` lvalue still resolves to the in-place `bool` overload, so the in-place callers are unchanged; const lvalues and rvalues get the copy. `[[nodiscard]]` makes a call that expects in-place masking of a const string a build error.

review.body:
I applied this PR to master `2170ef3` and compared it with a master debug build (`41a73de`, same `ShellCommandSource.cpp`).

`05453_executable_pool_unread_reply` fails on master for both `check_exit_code` values (`after LIMIT 0  [1]  1`, the previous request's row) and passes with the PR. It is deterministic: each table has its own pool, `pool_size = 1` gives it a single worker, and 48 parallel runs passed (about 1.6 s per run on a debug build). `04143_executable_storage_read_coverage` still passes.

What I checked:
- The new `executor` condition only changes the result when `generate` never ran, i.e. the reply header was never read. Once the header is read, the row comparison is the same as before, so fully read replies are still reused, including zero-row ones (`reused empty worker  [5]  2`).
- Keeping `prepare` unchanged is right. With `check_exit_code = 1` and `LIMIT 0`, `prepare` still sees `0 >= 0` and does not wait, and `cleanup` then drops the worker. The `check_exit_code = 1` pass of the test finishes right away.
- Executable dictionaries and executable UDF pools do not have this bug. They set `number_of_rows_to_read` from the input row count before the source is created, so an unread reply already leaves `current_read_rows < number_of_rows_to_read` and the existing check drops the worker. Only `StorageExecutable` sets `read_number_of_rows_from_process_output`.

Not caused by this PR, but it is the `prepare` wait the description mentions: [`prepare`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2170ef336e0d9cdedbffcd33da5a629a3ac464c5/src/Processors/Sources/ShellCommandSource.cpp#L749-L751) already blocks on a live pooled worker whenever the reply is only partly read. With `check_exit_code = 1`, a reply split into several chunks and a `LIMIT` that stops after the first chunk, the query never returns, and `max_execution_time` does not stop it. Same on master and with this PR:

```sql
-- echo_pool.sh from 05453
CREATE TABLE src (x UInt64) ENGINE = Memory;
CREATE TABLE t (x UInt64, request UInt64) ENGINE = ExecutablePool('echo_pool.sh', 'TSV', (SELECT x FROM src))
SETTINGS send_chunk_header = 1, pool_size = 1, check_exit_code = 1;
INSERT INTO src SELECT number + 1 FROM numbers(100);
SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 1 SETTINGS input_format_max_block_size_bytes = 16, max_execution_time = 3;
-- hangs in ShellCommandSource::prepare -> ShellCommand::wait -> wait4 (the worker's stdin is still open)
```

With `check_exit_code = 0` the same query returns and the next query gets fresh rows from a new worker. `cleanup` drops such a worker anyway, so `prepare` should not block on it while its stdin is open. That is a separate fix.

<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109377
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129640
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110435

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`CREATE`, `ALTER`, full `ATTACH` and table function structures now reject an `ALIAS` column that reads its own subcolumn, directly or through other `ALIAS` columns (for example `c String ALIAS c.size`), with `CYCLIC_ALIASES`. Before, such a definition was accepted and failed only when the column was read.

### Description
On master, `CREATE TABLE t (x UInt8, c0 Nullable(IPv6) ALIAS c0.null) ENGINE = Memory` is accepted, and `SELECT c0 FROM t` fails with `CYCLIC_ALIASES` (#129640). On 26.10.2.103 the same read runs the server out of memory. Found by BuzzHouse: [`OOM in dmesg` on #109377](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=109377&sha=7d1025c0f6eee9fe97ff605d40703b543d2e737b&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20(amd_debug)). Such a definition [should fail at `CREATE`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129640#issuecomment-6680749296).

Root cause: the definition-time cycle check binds an identifier to a column only by its whole name, so `c0.null` is not seen as reading `c0`.

Change: `ColumnsDescription::checkAliasColumnsAreNotCyclic` builds the graph of `ALIAS` columns, with an edge when an expression (subqueries included) reads another `ALIAS` column by name, through a subcolumn (bound the way `tryGetSubcolumnInfo` binds it) or as a member of a `Nested` prefix, and rejects a cycle with the existing DFS (factored out of `detectRecursiveDefaultCycles`, whose `DEFAULT` rule is unchanged). It runs for column lists and table function structures, full `ATTACH` / `AS` / `CLONE AS`, and the post-`ALTER` metadata. `05546_alias_column_reads_itself` (#129640) now expects `CYCLIC_ALIASES` at its cyclic `ATTACH` statements.

SQL UDF bodies are not followed: a cycle hidden in one fails with `CYCLIC_ALIASES` when the column is read. Metadata already stored with such a column still loads and fails the same way on read; further `ALTER`s on it are rejected until `MODIFY COLUMN ... REMOVE ALIAS`.

#127018 makes the existing `DEFAULT` cycle check follow compound subcolumn references such as `c0.null`; that check does not run for a full `ATTACH`, this one does.

Validation: the new test `05339_alias_column_cyclic_subcolumn` and the adapted `05546` fail on master; `05339_alias_column_cyclic_subcolumn_udf` checks the read of UDF-hidden cycles; randomized runs pass; stateless tests that use `ALIAS` or SQL UDFs show no new failures.

Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/124850](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F124850+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

comment.body: Answering my own question above: I dropped UDF bodies from the check in 45a7ecff2ced8. Since #129640 such a cycle fails with `CYCLIC_ALIASES` when the column is read instead of running the server out of memory, so following UDFs only moved that error earlier and kept rejecting valid structures. I also merged master to resolve the conflict and adapted the `ATTACH` statements of #129640's test; the changelog category is now Improvement.

issue.title: Faster builds: no-op rebuild 21 s → 1.4 s, header edits up to −72%, clean build −21% (10 build-system, include and PCH patches)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Build system (CMake, compilation, platform builds).

issue.body:
### Describe the situation

Small edits rebuild far more than they need: each ClickHouse build reruns cargo and rewrites the Rust archives, so clickhouse relinks, and settings files and core headers pull thousands of files into the rebuild. These patches remove most of that work; precompiled headers speed up clean builds.

Median seconds from an edit (or empty tree) to a linked clickhouse, RelWithDebInfo: master + patch 1 vs patches 1–9, 2–3 interleaved pairs.

| Scenario | x86, 32 vCPU: before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] | ARM, 16 vCPU: before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| No-op rebuild | 20.8 → 1.36 | **−93.4%** [−93.5%, −93.4%] | 23.5 → 1.76 | **−92.5%** [−93.1%, −92.0%] |
| Edit a leaf `.cpp` (getClusterName.cpp) | 23.5 → 11.8 | **−49.8%** [−52.2%, −48.6%] | 27.9* → 15.6 | **−44.1%** [−73.0%, −13.1%] |
| Edit `Settings.cpp` | 53.9 → 26.6 | **−50.7%** [−51.9%, −49.3%] | 71.0 → 34.6 | **−51.2%** [−51.8%, −50.8%] |
| Edit `ServerSettings.cpp` | 47.7 → 33.9 | **−28.9%** [−30.1%, −27.3%] | 60.2 → 44.5 | **−26.1%** [−29.2%, −24.5%] |
| Edit `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` | 39.9 → 19.6 | **−51.0%** [−52.4%, −48.9%] | 51.3 → 24.9 | **−51.5%** [−56.4%, −44.9%] |
| CMake re-run (touch `CMakeLists.txt`) | 34.1 → 9.60 | **−71.8%** [−76.8%, −68.2%] | 47.5* → 11.8 | **−75.2%** [−92.6%, −45.6%] |
| Edit `ProtocolDefines.h` | 311 → 155 | **−50.2%** [−51.0%, −49.3%] | 441 → 203 | **−53.9%** [−59.4%, −47.7%] |
| Edit `FormatSettings.h` | 1,546 → 440 | **−71.5%** [−71.5%, −71.5%] | 2,290 → 631 | **−72.4%** [−78.5%, −64.6%] |
| Edit `ISerialization.h` | 1,543 → 1,142 | **−26.0%** [−26.3%, −25.7%] | 2,324 → 1,678 | **−27.8%** [−33.1%, −22.1%] |
| New build directory, warm ccache | 437 → 275 | **−37.2%** [−41.3%, −32.7%] | 564 → 443 | **−21.5%** [−43.2%, +8.4%] |
| Clean build, empty ccache | 3,104 → 2,446 | **−21.2%** [−21.8%, −20.6%] | 4,641 → 3,689 | **−20.5%** [−25.5%, −15.2%] |

Before: master with patch 1, the link fix that master needed to link in these builds; after: all default-build patches (1–9). Change is the ratio of the medians; brackets give the 95% interval of the paired geometric-mean ratio. * On ARM the first master run after an idle period was slow (cold page cache: 42.3 s for the leaf edit, 93.0 s for the CMake re-run); the medians use all runs. Costs of the precompiled headers (patch 9) alone: a CMake re-run takes about 1 s longer (x86 8.6 → 9.5 s; ARM 10.8 → 12.2 s) and a new build directory with a warm ccache 4% longer on x86 (264.6 → 274.7 s; no measurable change on ARM), and 0.9 GB of PCH files in the build directory; with all patches applied no scenario got slower. Patch 10 adds an opt-in `-DSPLIT_DWARF=ON` (default off): on x86 a leaf edit took 13.0 → 10.1 s (−22%) and a `Settings.cpp` edit 43.4 → 40.1 s (−8%) compared with the same tree without it; split builds keep file and line in stack traces but show no inlined frames in-process (`addressToLineWithInlines` gave 45 frames for 45 stack addresses, against 118 in a default build).

<details><summary>What each patch changes, per-patch measurements and checks</summary>

1. **Link fix.** In our default RelWithDebInfo builds with clang/lld 21.1.8, master's `clickhouse` failed to link: `localize_rust_c_symbols.sh` rewrites the Rust archives with `llvm-objcopy` (`llvm-objcopy-21`, the `CMAKE_OBJCOPY` of these builds), which leaves `.llvm_addrsig` sections with `sh_link=0` in the objects where it localizes a symbol; lld's `--icf=safe` warns about them and `--fatal-warnings` fails the link. #126478 alone does not fix these builds: it makes CMake pass the LLVM objcopy instead of GNU objcopy, and these builds already used it. With `-Wl,--no-fatal-warnings` in the linker flags the link succeeds; we did not try CI's toolchain. The patch removes `.llvm_addrsig` there, as `strip_rust_symbols.sh` does since #122904; this works with GNU objcopy too. Patch 1 is a link fix that both measured trees contain; it is not measured on its own.
2. **Build system and settings.** Today every build runs the cargo builds and rewrites the copied Rust archives in place (`localize_rust_c_symbols.sh`, `strip_rust_symbols.sh`), so the copy never matches cargo's output, is rewritten again and `clickhouse` relinks even when nothing changed; every library linking a crate also waits for all cargo builds before compiling anything. The patch (a) runs each post-processing step as a custom command that writes a new archive only when its input changed (the approach of #119121); (b) builds the workspace crates with one `cargo build`, so they no longer wait for each other on cargo's target-directory lock, and skips cargo when no input of the Rust libraries changed (`cmake/cargo_if_changed.sh`, which checks cargo's dep-info files and falls back to running cargo); (c) links the crates through imported targets without the cargo dependency, so C++ compiles run in parallel with cargo and only the sources including `delta_kernel_ffi.hpp` wait for the delta-kernel build; (d) on a CMake re-run, rewrites configure-time generated files only when their content changes, lists licenses without a fork per vendored crate and keeps `git status` out of submodule work trees; (e) for the settings files, replaces per-setting template code with table-driven accessors in `BaseSettings.h` and shared field operations, includes `FormatFactorySettings.h` only where it is used and moves the disk checks of `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` to `MergeTreeSettingsDisks.cpp` (no more `MergeTreeData.h`, `ZooKeeper.h`, `ASTFunction.h`). Measured separately on x86, part (a) alone took the no-op rebuild from 21.1 to 4.4 s and the rest of the build-system changes to 1.3 s; part (e) alone took a `Settings.cpp` edit from 42.8 to 28.2 s. One `cargo build` for all workspace crates unifies the features of the dependencies they share, as `cargo build --workspace` does, so the linked Rust code changes slightly: on an earlier master this change alone made the binary 0.3 MB smaller, while the 136 exported Rust FFI symbols and the outputs of PRQL, polyglot, PCO and Vortex smoke queries stayed identical; skim and wasmtime were linked but not run.
3. **ProtocolDefines.h and friends.** The parallel-replicas protocol versions move to `ParallelReplicasProtocolDefines.h`, so `RequestResponse.h` (and everything including it) no longer depends on `ProtocolDefines.h`; `FileCachePolicy` moves to `Core/FileCachePolicy.h`, so `FileCache_fwd.h` no longer includes `SettingsEnums.h`; `ActionsDAG.h` and `IQueryPlanStep.h` are replaced by forward declarations where one suffices. A `ProtocolDefines.h` edit recompiles 115 files instead of 278.
4. **Direct includes.** 87 files that used `FormatSettings` (and a few other headers) through transitive includes include them directly. Patch 4 only adds the direct includes that patch 5 needs; it is not measured on its own.
5. **FormatSettings.h out of common headers.** `ReadHelpers.h`, `WriteHelpers.h`, `FormatFactorySettings.h`, `SettingsEnums.h` and `Context.h` included the whole `FormatSettings.h`. The CSV/JSON enums they need move to `FormatSettingsEnums.h` and the JSON number writers to `writeJSONNumber.h`/`WriteHelpers.cpp`: a `FormatSettings.h` edit recompiles 1,203 files instead of 3,222.
6. **FormatSettings.h out of the remaining wide headers.** `NativeWriter.h`, `DateTimeTransforms.h`, `FunctionBinaryArithmetic.h`, `convertFieldToType.h`, `convertColumnToType.h`, `VirtualColumnUtils.h` and a few others stop including it: 708 files instead of 1,203.
7. **Operators.h and IDataType.h.** `IO/Operators.h` no longer includes `IO/ReadHelpers.h` (a `ReadHelpers.h` edit: 1,338 files instead of 2,002, 1,147 → 933 s (−19%) when measured alone), and `IDataType.h` no longer includes `ISerialization.h`; the substream types it needs move to `SerializationSubstream.h` (an `ISerialization.h` edit: 2,286 files instead of 3,218, 1,516 → 1,267 s (−16%) alone).
8. **Unit-test include.** One unit test used `ISerialization.h` through `IDataType.h`. Patch 8 only adds an include to one unit test; it is not measured on its own.
9. **Precompiled headers.** `cmake/precompiled_headers.cmake` adds per-target PCHs of stable standard-library, fmt, magic_enum, `base/` and third-party headers to the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries, with `-fno-pch-timestamp` so ccache still hits in a new build directory. Earlier attempts found little gain: #9162 (2020) measured a clean build of 74 minutes with PCH against 76 without, and the `dbms`-only PCH listed in #96721 saved 5.9 s, about 3% of CPU time, at 192 cores. Patch 9 covers far more of the build, including the contrib sources that mostly parse their library headers: on these 16-core hosts it cut clean-build CPU time by 19% (x86) and 18% (ARM) and wall time by 18.8% and 17.5%, with the same `.text` size. Compiler caches stay correct: after a change of only the PCH content, sccache 0.19, chcache and ccache 4.9.1 all missed, because the headers inside the PCH are part of what each cache hashes; ccache gets the `pch_defines,time_macros` sloppiness it needs only for the targets with a PCH. We did not measure CI builds with sccache, where every fresh build directory builds the PCHs again.
10. **Opt-in SPLIT_DWARF.** A `SPLIT_DWARF` CMake option (`-gsplit-dwarf -gno-gnu-pubnames`) keeps most debug information out of the objects the linker reads. `Dwarf.cpp` accepts the skeleton units (`DW_TAG_skeleton_unit`) so stack traces keep file and line, and one test that reads the binary's DWARF is skipped in split builds, as it is for `-g0`.

Each patch measured on its own on x86 (interleaved pairs; "before" is the tree with the earlier patches, for patch 10 the same tree built without the option; IDs name host, patch and scenario):

| Patch | Scenario ID | Before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] | Pairs |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| 2 | x86-BS3-noop | 20.6 → 1.34 | **−93.5%** [−93.8%, −93.2%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-leaf | 23.7 → 13.1 | **−44.8%** [−46.3%, −41.7%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-serversettings | 48.1 → 34.3 | **−28.6%** [−32.3%, −24.2%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-settings | 54.8 → 27.4 | **−50.0%** [−52.4%, −46.6%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-mtsettings | 39.9 → 21.4 | **−46.4%** [−48.2%, −43.9%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-cmake | 34.0 → 8.61 | **−74.7%** [−75.2%, −74.1%] | 3 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-warmfresh | 443 → 266 | **−40.0%** [−48.0%, −30.9%] | 2 |
| 2 | x86-BS3-formatfactorysettings | 197 → 105 | **−46.5%** [−54.2%, −37.6%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-protocoldefines | 300 → 163 | **−45.7%** [−47.5%, −43.9%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-settingsenums | 1,079 → 772 | **−28.4%** [−29.7%, −27.2%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-actionsdag | 799 → 711 | **−11.0%** [−19.8%, −1.2%] | 2 |
| 3 | x86-H1-iqueryplanstep | 490 → 292 | **−40.3%** [−42.4%, −38.3%] | 2 |
| 5 | x86-FSb-formatsettings | 1,517 → 797 | **−47.4%** [−48.2%, −46.7%] | 2 |
| 6 | x86-H4-formatsettings | 797 → 478 | **−40.0%** [−43.9%, −35.8%] | 2 |
| 7 | x86-H56-readhelpers | 1,147 → 931 | **−18.8%** [−19.7%, −17.9%] | 2 |
| 7 | x86-H56-iserialization | 1,518 → 1,265 | **−16.7%** [−18.3%, −15.1%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-clean | 3,012 → 2,446 | **−18.8%** [−19.3%, −18.2%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-warmfresh | 265 → 275 | **+3.8%** [−6.2%, +14.9%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-leaf | 12.8 → 11.9 | **−7.1%** [−11.0%, −3.0%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-settings | 27.1 → 26.3 | **−3.0%** [−9.7%, +4.1%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-cmake | 8.56 → 9.53 | **+11.3%** [+4.1%, +19.0%] | 2 |
| 9 | x86-CB1-formatsettings | 477 → 441 | **−7.5%** [−11.4%, −3.4%] | 2 |
| 10 | x86-U6-leaf | 13.0 → 10.1 | **−22.4%** [−28.0%, −17.2%] | 3 |
| 10 | x86-U6-settings | 43.4 → 40.1 | **−7.5%** [−10.7%, −5.6%] | 3 |

Checks: master and patched binaries return identical `system.settings`, `system.server_settings`, `system.merge_tree_settings`, `system.licenses`, `system.formats`, `system.functions` and `system.table_engines`, sample values and Native output on both hosts; `system.build_options` differs only in the git fields. `unit_tests_dbms` passes with all patches on both hosts (x86: 30,289 tests, 25,497 passed, the rest skipped, none failed; ARM: 30,265 tests, 25,469 passed, 4,796 skipped, none failed, the same counts as master). Clean, new-directory and incremental builds all succeeded, every incremental scenario recompiled the edited file and relinked, and each binary answered a query. The binaries are not byte-identical: the header cuts move code between translation units, the single cargo build of patch 2 unifies Rust dependency features (see patch 2), and the PCHs change debug type information (with and without patch 9: same `.text`, `.rodata` and `.data` sizes on x86 and same `.text` size on ARM; `.debug_info` 3.6% (x86) and 3.8% (ARM) smaller from fewer duplicated type entries; equivalent symbolization of 3,000 sampled functions on ARM). On ARM, Time/DateTime conversions, uniqExact and general queries ran at the same speed with and without the patches (within ±0.7%, except a +1.8% uniqExact difference of the size that rebuilding identical sources also produces).

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?

<details><summary>Tested versions and source commits</summary>

Measured on master 64576f956c6b (2026-11-03) with the patches applied in order. A three-way merge of the patches onto master 46ab3dad27eb (2026-11-07) conflicts only in `FormatSettings.h` and `ActionsDAG.cpp`, next to edited lines. Since the base, upstream changed only other lines of the build files these patches edit (source lists in `src/CMakeLists.txt`, OSS-Fuzz options in `CMakeLists.txt`), not the Rust, cargo, license or PCH steps. We did not rebuild on the newer master: new code that relies on an include these patches remove would need a direct include, as in patch 4.

</details>

### How to reproduce

<details><summary>Hosts, configuration and measurement procedure</summary>

- Hosts: x86, AWS r6i.8xlarge (16 cores / 32 vCPU, 247 GiB); ARM, AWS r7g.4xlarge (16 vCPU Graviton3, 123 GiB); Ubuntu 24.04.
- Toolchain: clang/lld 21.1.8 from apt.llvm.org, CMake 3.28.3, Ninja 1.11.1, ccache 4.9.1, Rust nightly-2026-03-22 as pinned by `contrib/corrosion-cmake`.
- Configuration (both arms): `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-21 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-21`, then `ninja -C build clickhouse` (default parallelism, ccache through `COMPILER_CACHE=auto`). Patch 10 is measured with `-DSPLIT_DWARF=ON` against the same tree without it.
- Trees: one source checkout and one `CCACHE_DIR` per arm, never shared. Before each incremental run the tree is synced with two no-op `ninja` runs.
- Scenarios, each timed from the edit to the finished `clickhouse` binary:
  - no-op: `ninja` on the synced tree;
  - leaf, `Settings.cpp`, `ServerSettings.cpp`, `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` and header edits: append a unique comment line to the file, `ninja`, then restore the file (the next sync rebuilds it);
  - CMake re-run: `touch CMakeLists.txt`, `ninja`;
  - new build directory with warm ccache: delete the build directory, `cmake` + `ninja`;
  - clean build: delete the build directory and the arm's ccache directory, `cmake` + `ninja`.
- Order: arms interleaved per scenario (A,B,B,A or A,B,B,A,A,B), 2 pairs for scenarios over 5 minutes, 3 for the others; the table shows medians and the 95% interval of the paired geometric ratio. The arm for patch 9 alone (all patches except 9 vs all patches) was interleaved with the same runs on x86.
- Patch application: 1 → 9 in order on master 64576f956c6b; patch 10 applies on top.

</details>

### Expected performance

<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A rebuild should cost about as much as the change: no cargo run, archive rewrite or relink when no Rust input and no object changed; after a header edit, recompiling only the files that use the header; after a CMake re-run with no real change, no regenerated file that forces recompiles. Clean builds should not parse the same large third-party headers in every translation unit.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests

<details><summary>Related work</summary>

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/96721 collects build-speed work. Patches 3 and 5–7 cut transitive header dependencies so that a header edit recompiles fewer files, which Algunenano suggested there for local development; patch 9 extends the `dbms`-only PCH commit listed there (not merged) to per-target PCHs for the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/9162 (2020, closed) tried CMake's precompiled headers and measured a clean build of 74 minutes with them against 76 without; the description of patch 9 says what differs here.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122904 removed `.llvm_addrsig` in `strip_rust_symbols.sh`; patch 1 does the same in `localize_rust_c_symbols.sh`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126478 (open) fixes the same link error where CMake picks GNU objcopy, by passing the LLVM objcopy instead; patch 1 removes the section, so it also fixes builds like ours that already use `llvm-objcopy-21`, and the two changes do not conflict.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/124645 took the cargo builds out of Ninja's console pool; as it notes, the workspace crates still wait for each other on cargo's target-directory lock, which patch 2(b) removes by building them with one `cargo build`.

**Patch 1: link fix for the localized Rust archives**

```diff
diff --git a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
index 61cf95aa9c8..4ef48524c02 100755
--- a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
+++ b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
@@ -125,12 +125,15 @@ if [ -s "$LOCALIZE_FILE" ]; then
     # Some Rust archives contain non-ELF members (e.g. debug metadata objects)
     # that cause llvm-objcopy to fail.  In that case, fall back to extracting
     # individual members, processing only valid ELF objects, and repacking.
-    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
+    # Also drop .llvm_addrsig: objcopy leaves its sh_link at 0, and lld --icf=safe then warns that it ignores it
+    # (an error with --fatal-warnings). Without the table lld treats these objects conservatively, as it does
+    # when it ignores the table. See strip_rust_symbols.sh.
+    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
         WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
 
         (cd "$WORK_DIR" && "$AR" x "$LIB_PATH")
         for obj in "$WORK_DIR"/*.o; do
-            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
+            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
         done
         "$AR" rcs "$LIB_PATH" "$WORK_DIR"/*.o
     fi
```
