```diff
+    ranges syncstream coroutine semaphore expected flat_map flat_set mdspan sanitizer/asan_interface.h
+    logger.hxx event_awaiter.hxx context.hxx rpc_cli_factory.hxx)
+set (CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_google_cloud_cpp_common
+    string cstddef clocale cstdlib typeinfo cerrno ratio ctime array optional source_location type_traits
+    utility atomic cassert functional vector ios streambuf bitset variant span cmath istream sstream memory
+    ostream chrono)
+set (CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_TARGETS _s2 google_cloud_cpp_storage _hdfs3 _libprotobuf _ch_contrib_antlr4_cpp_runtime _azure_sdk _icui18n _parquet flatc _icuuc _arrow_flight google_cloud_cpp_rest_internal _nuraft google_cloud_cpp_common)
+
+if (NOT ENABLE_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS OR ENABLE_CLANG_TIDY OR CMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS OR NOT CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang")
+    set (ENABLE_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS OFF)
+    set (ENABLE_CONTRIB_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS OFF)
+    message (STATUS "Precompiled headers: OFF")
+else ()
+    message (STATUS "Precompiled headers: ON, contrib: ${ENABLE_CONTRIB_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS}")
+    # Without a timestamp, the PCH does not change when a checkout only touches the headers, so ccache keeps hitting.
+    list (APPEND CMAKE_CXX_COMPILE_OPTIONS_CREATE_PCH -Xclang -fno-pch-timestamp)
+endif ()
+
+# clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (target [SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES] {HEADERS header... | REUSE_FROM other_target})
+# SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES: sources in the target's own CMake directory (for contrib: stubs, generated parsers and
+# version files kept next to contrib/<library>-cmake/CMakeLists.txt) are compiled as before.
+function (clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers target)
+    cmake_parse_arguments (PCH "SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES" "REUSE_FROM" "HEADERS" ${ARGN})
+    if (PCH_REUSE_FROM)
+        target_precompile_headers (${target} REUSE_FROM ${PCH_REUSE_FROM})
+    else ()
+        set (headers)
+        foreach (header IN LISTS PCH_HEADERS)
+            list (APPEND headers "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:<${header}$<ANGLE-R>>")
+        endforeach ()
+        target_precompile_headers (${target} PRIVATE ${headers})
+    endif ()
+    # Keep template instantiation in the translation units, so the generated code does not change.
+    set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES PCH_INSTANTIATE_TEMPLATES OFF)
+
+    get_target_property (source_dir ${target} SOURCE_DIR)
+    get_target_property (binary_dir ${target} BINARY_DIR)
+    get_target_property (sources ${target} SOURCES)
+    foreach (source IN LISTS sources)
+        if (source MATCHES "^\\$<" OR NOT source MATCHES "\\.(cpp|cc|cxx)$")
+            continue ()
+        endif ()
+        # Resolve like CMake does: relative to the target's source directory, else its binary directory (generated files).
+        if (IS_ABSOLUTE "${source}")
+            set (path "${source}")
+        elseif (EXISTS "${source_dir}/${source}")
+            set (path "${source_dir}/${source}")
+        else ()
+            set (path "${binary_dir}/${source}")
+        endif ()
+        if (PCH_SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES)
+            string (FIND "${path}" "${source_dir}/" pos)
+            if (pos EQUAL 0)
+                set_source_files_properties ("${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} PROPERTIES SKIP_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS ON)
+                continue ()
+            endif ()
+        endif ()
+        foreach (property COMPILE_FLAGS COMPILE_OPTIONS COMPILE_DEFINITIONS)
+            get_source_file_property (value "${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} ${property})
+            if (value)
+                set_source_files_properties ("${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} PROPERTIES SKIP_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS ON)
+                break ()
+            endif ()
+        endforeach ()
+    endforeach ()
+
+    get_target_property (launcher ${target} CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER)
+    list (FILTER launcher INCLUDE REGEX "(^|/)ccache$")
+    if (launcher)
+        execute_process (COMMAND ${launcher} --get-config sloppiness
+            OUTPUT_VARIABLE sloppiness OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE ERROR_QUIET RESULT_VARIABLE rc)
+        if (NOT rc EQUAL 0)
+            set (sloppiness "")
+        endif ()
+        string (REPLACE " " "" sloppiness "${sloppiness},pch_defines,time_macros")
+        string (REGEX REPLACE "^," "" sloppiness "${sloppiness}")
+        get_target_property (launcher ${target} CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER)
+        set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER "env;CCACHE_SLOPPINESS=${sloppiness};${launcher}")
+    endif ()
+endfunction ()
+
+function (clickhouse_add_precompiled_headers)
+    if (NOT ENABLE_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS)
+        return ()
+    endif ()
+
+    foreach (target IN LISTS CLICKHOUSE_PCH_TARGETS)
+        if (TARGET ${target})
+            clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_PCH_HEADERS})
+        endif ()
+    endforeach ()
+
+    if (NOT ENABLE_CONTRIB_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS)
+        return ()
+    endif ()
+
+    if (TARGET _aws)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_aws SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__aws})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET grpc)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (grpc SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_grpc})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _rocksdb)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_rocksdb SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__rocksdb})
+    endif ()
+    # The LLVM libraries share their compile flags, so they share one PCH, built by LLVMCore. The libraries below the IR
+    # (and two YAML/DWARF readers) declare their own Argument, Value, Type, CallingConv or isDigit, which clash with the
+    # IR headers of that PCH, so they are compiled as before.
+    set (llvm_pch_exclude LLVMDemangle LLVMSupport LLVMBinaryFormat LLVMRemarks LLVMBitstreamReader LLVMTextAPI
+        LLVMTargetParser LLVMObjectYAML LLVMDebugInfoDWARF LLVMDebugInfoDWARFLowLevel)
+    if (TARGET LLVMCore)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (LLVMCore SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_LLVM})
+        get_property (llvm_targets DIRECTORY "${ClickHouse_SOURCE_DIR}/contrib/llvm-project-cmake" PROPERTY BUILDSYSTEM_TARGETS)
+        foreach (target IN LISTS llvm_targets)
+            get_target_property (type ${target} TYPE)
+            if (target MATCHES "^LLVM" AND type STREQUAL "STATIC_LIBRARY" AND NOT target STREQUAL "LLVMCore"
+                AND NOT target IN_LIST llvm_pch_exclude)
+                clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES REUSE_FROM LLVMCore)
+            endif ()
+        endforeach ()
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _mongocxx)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_mongocxx SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__mongocxx})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _xgboost)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_xgboost SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__xgboost})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _arrow)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_arrow SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__arrow})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _libprotoc)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_libprotoc SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__libprotoc})
+    endif ()
+    if (TARGET _vectorscan)
+        clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (_vectorscan SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS__vectorscan})
+    endif ()
+    foreach (target IN LISTS CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_TARGETS)
+        if (TARGET ${target})
+            clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers (${target} SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES HEADERS ${CLICKHOUSE_CONTRIB_PCH_HEADERS_${target}})
+        endif ()
+    endforeach ()
+endfunction ()
```

**Patch 10: opt-in SPLIT_DWARF**

```diff
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index de1e90421fd..46c90840490 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -515,6 +515,22 @@ if (NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE_UC STREQUAL "RELEASE")
     set(DEBUG_INFO_FLAGS "${DEBUG_INFO_FLAGS} -gdwarf-aranges")
 endif ()
 
+# Keep most debug info out of every link: each object file writes its DWARF to a .dwo file next to it
+# (-gsplit-dwarf), and only skeleton units, line tables and address ranges reach the binary. Links of
+# builds with debug info get much faster and the binary much smaller, but debuggers read the .dwo files
+# from the build directory (resolved against DW_AT_comp_dir), the in-process symbolizer cannot show
+# inlined frames, and the DWARF input format sees only the skeleton units. For local development builds only.
+option (SPLIT_DWARF "Write DWARF debug info to .dwo files in the build directory instead of the binary (-gsplit-dwarf), for faster development links" OFF)
+if (SPLIT_DWARF AND NOT DISABLE_ALL_DEBUG_SYMBOLS)
+    if (COMPILER_CACHE STREQUAL "chcache")
+        # chcache stores and restores only the object file, so a cache hit would leave its .dwo file missing or stale.
+        message (FATAL_ERROR "SPLIT_DWARF does not work with COMPILER_CACHE=chcache, which does not cache .dwo files (use ccache or sccache)")
+    endif ()
+    # With -gsplit-dwarf clang also emits GNU pubnames, which only serve a linker-built .gdb_index (not built
+    # here) and would be more than half of the debug sections left in the binary.
+    set(DEBUG_INFO_FLAGS "${DEBUG_INFO_FLAGS} -gsplit-dwarf -gno-gnu-pubnames")
+endif ()
+
 # Compress DWARF debug sections (`.debug_*`) in object files with -gz=zlib to shrink the build dir
 # (debug info dominates it). Compile-only via add_compile_options, so binaries stay uncompressed and
 # the symbolizer is unaffected. Defaults on where the compiler supports it (probed above).
diff --git a/src/Common/Dwarf.cpp b/src/Common/Dwarf.cpp
index 91863199fec..f1087d23f7d 100644
--- a/src/Common/Dwarf.cpp
+++ b/src/Common/Dwarf.cpp
@@ -76,6 +76,7 @@
 #define DW_FORM_addrx4 0x2c
 
 #define DW_TAG_compile_unit 0x11
+#define DW_TAG_skeleton_unit 0x4a
 #define DW_TAG_subprogram 0x2e
 #define DW_TAG_try_block 0x32
 #define DW_TAG_catch_block 0x25
@@ -828,7 +829,7 @@ Dwarf::CompilationUnit Dwarf::getCompilationUnit(uint64_t offset) const
     }
 
     Die die = getDieAtOffset(cu, cu.first_die);
-    if (die.abbr.tag != DW_TAG_compile_unit)
+    if (die.abbr.tag != DW_TAG_compile_unit && die.abbr.tag != DW_TAG_skeleton_unit)
     {
         return cu;
     }
@@ -1071,8 +1072,9 @@ bool Dwarf::findLocation(
     bool assume_in_cu_range) const
 {
     Die die = getDieAtOffset(cu, cu.first_die);
-    // Partial compilation unit (DW_TAG_partial_unit) is not supported.
-    SAFE_CHECK(die.abbr.tag == DW_TAG_compile_unit, "expecting compile unit entry");
+    // Partial compilation unit (DW_TAG_partial_unit) is not supported. A skeleton unit (split DWARF, -gsplit-dwarf)
+    // has the line table and address ranges of its compilation unit, but its other entries are in a .dwo file.
+    SAFE_CHECK(die.abbr.tag == DW_TAG_compile_unit || die.abbr.tag == DW_TAG_skeleton_unit, "expecting compile unit entry");
 
     // Offset in .debug_line for the line number VM program for this CU
     std::optional<uint64_t> line_offset = 0;
diff --git a/tests/queries/0_stateless/03641_clickhouse_prefer_symbols_from_contrib_over_rust_crates.sh b/tests/queries/0_stateless/03641_clickhouse_prefer_symbols_from_contrib_over_rust_crates.sh
index de5462ed704..94a406552c7 100755
--- a/tests/queries/0_stateless/03641_clickhouse_prefer_symbols_from_contrib_over_rust_crates.sh
+++ b/tests/queries/0_stateless/03641_clickhouse_prefer_symbols_from_contrib_over_rust_crates.sh
@@ -13,6 +13,11 @@ if [ $($CLICKHOUSE_LOCAL -q "SELECT value LIKE '%-g0%' FROM system.build_options
     echo "@@SKIP@@: No debug symbols"
     exit 0
 fi
+# With split DWARF (SPLIT_DWARF) the binary has only skeleton units, the other entries are in .dwo files
+if [ $($CLICKHOUSE_LOCAL -q "SELECT value LIKE '%-gsplit-dwarf%' FROM system.build_options WHERE name = 'CXX_FLAGS'") -eq 1 ]; then
+    echo "@@SKIP@@: Split DWARF"
+    exit 0
+fi
 # MacOS does not have file:line (backtrace_symbols() does not provide this info)
```

Current state of my part, as of 2026-11-10 17:00 UTC. Since snelheidai's summary above, #130176, #130229 and #130240 were merged and #130277 changed, so this replaces the PR part of that summary.

**Needs review**
- #130180: the Rust localize and strip steps become ordinary build rules that run only when their input changes, so a no-op `ninja clickhouse` no longer re-runs 12 steps and relinks (40.5 s to 4.6 s, Debug). Not reviewed yet. Its only red check, AST fuzzer (oracle), is a master bug with its own open fix, #107127.
- #130277: compiler-rt is now compiled with the build path mapping flags too, so its objects no longer embed the absolute checkout path (41 of 234 before, 0 after). The ccache part was dropped after @ rschu1ze's review, so cache reuse across worktrees is not taken. Waiting for his re-review.
- #130545 (new): installs `pigz` in `clickhouse/binary-builder`, so release jobs compress the `.tgz` packages in parallel. The tarballs take 248 s of the 282 s `Build Packages` step in a master `amd_release` job; locally `clickhouse-common-static` takes 2.1 s instead of 25.0 s. Needs a review and the `can be tested` label, which I cannot add.

**Approved, auto-merge on**: #130218 (the only red check is the private CH Inc sync, which I cannot see) and #130183 (it needs the master merge @ azat asked for, which is on my side).

**Decisions, unanswered**

A. Rust and cargo (my question to @ Algunenano). Every `ninja` run starts all 8 cargo builds (about 3.3 s, serialized by cargo's lock), and the C++ libraries that link a Rust crate wait for them before compiling. Options:
- (a) skip a crate's cargo run when none of its inputs changed, with an in-tree script that copies cargo's freshness check (it must also watch vendored build-script inputs such as the OpenSSL headers, path packages outside the workspace and `.cargo/config.toml`), behind a `RUST_SKIP_UNCHANGED_CARGO` option;
- (b) only link the Rust archives through imported targets, so C++ compiles run while cargo works; cargo still runs every time and decides what to rebuild;
- (c) neither, until Corrosion supports it (corrosion-rs/corrosion#206).

`ninja clickhouse` on top of #130180, 16-vCPU ARM: no-op 5.25 s, 5.22 s with (b), 1.91 s with (a) and (b); one `.cpp` edit 21.33 s, 18.33 s with (b), 17.89 s with both. I recommend (b), as snelheidai does: most of the edit gain, and no risk of skipping a cargo run that was needed. It builds on #130180.

B. Precompiled headers, patch 9 of the issue description (my question to @ alexey-milovidov; either of you can decide). It gives the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries a PCH: a clean build from an empty cache takes 2,446 s instead of 3,012 s (x86, 16 cores). In CI, sccache preprocesses each object together with its PCH headers, so a fully cached build gets slower: a build breaks even at about 160 cache misses, the median PR build has 143 and master builds almost none. Measured the way CI builds, with only the `src` PCHs: fully cached +1.9%, a `Context.h` change -4.5%, empty cache -6.9%. Options:
- (a) the whole patch, with the contrib PCHs off in CI except in one build, which keeps compiling their header lists (a submodule update can break one);
- (b) only the `src` PCHs, everywhere;
- (c) neither.

I recommend (a).

**Not PRs yet**: snelheidai's other patches. I am verifying the seven without a trade-off, one PR each; the four with a cost are described in its summary above (section C).

issue.title: Performance regression: primary-key analysis of a bare UInt8 filter (`WHERE flag`) grows with the number of marks on 26.8 (index_granularity = 8192)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: MergeTree* family: parts, merges, primary index, column statistics, background data transformation.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Regression found by chReplay production query replay

issue.body:
Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/89603

### Description

Since 26.8, a filter on a bare UInt8 column that is part of the primary key (`WHERE flag`) is used in primary-key analysis; 26.6 ignored it. When that column is not the first key column and the first key column changes every few hundred granules, the generic exclusion search splits the part into many ranges, and its cost grows with the number of marks. A `LIMIT 0` query that took a few ms on 26.6 now takes hundreds of ms on a 244k-mark part, and seconds on a production table with about 79M marks at the default `index_granularity = 8192`.

Reproduces on master `26.11.1.1374` (`d29c1d95f608`), 26.8.35.29 and 26.8.1.515. Not reproduced on 26.6.9.19 or 26.6.1.2370.

`WHERE flag != 0` already took this path on 26.6. The regression is that a bare `WHERE flag` now does too.

### How to reproduce

The table uses the default `index_granularity = 8192`. Each `c1` value covers about 1.73M rows (about 211 granules), and `c2` is split 50/50 inside each `c1` value. One part, 2B rows, 244141 marks, about 1 GB on disk.

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (c1 DateTime, c2 UInt8, c3 LowCardinality(String), c4 UInt32)
ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY toDate(c1) PRIMARY KEY (c1, c2, c3) ORDER BY (c1, c2, c3, c4)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192;

INSERT INTO t SELECT toDateTime('2026-08-01 00:00:00') + 30 * intDiv(number, 1730000), (number % 1730000) >= 865000, concat('ex', toString(cityHash64(number) % 20)), toUInt32(cityHash64(number, 1) % 50) FROM numbers(2000000000);

OPTIMIZE TABLE t FINAL;

SELECT c1, c4 FROM t WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2 LIMIT 0 SETTINGS compatibility = '25.12';
```

### Performance

`clickhouse local`, 6 runs of each query in one process (first run, then the warm range):

| Query | 26.6.9.19 | 26.8.35.29 | master d29c1d95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2`, `compatibility = '25.12'` | 32 ms, then 8 ms | 316 ms, then 114-196 ms | 295 ms, then 54-74 ms |
| `WHERE c4 = 1 AND c2` | 17 ms, then 6-25 ms | 276 ms, then 59-184 ms | 295 ms, then 50-106 ms |
| `WHERE c2`, `compatibility = '25.12'` | 20 ms, then 6-17 ms | 218 ms, then 35-84 ms | 305 ms, then 90-175 ms |
| `WHERE c2 != 0`, `compatibility = '25.12'` | 91 ms, then 26-43 ms | 307 ms, then 35-103 ms | 308 ms, then 58-177 ms |

Primary-key selection for `WHERE c2`: 26.6 reads `244141/244141 marks from 1 ranges`; 26.8 and master read `123212/244141 marks from 1156 ranges`.

The cost grows with the number of marks: the same layout with 500M rows (61036 marks, 289 ranges) takes about 6 ms on 26.6 and 20-50 ms on master.

The production table this was found on has about 79.3M marks in 519 parts at `index_granularity = 8192` (about 8177 rows per mark) and the same key layout. A `LIMIT 0` query on it took 41 ms on 26.6.1.2370 and 6278 ms on 26.8.1.515.

### Expected behavior

Primary-key analysis on a bare boolean column should not add seconds of planning time when it prunes little, and a `LIMIT 0` query should stay near-instant as it is on 26.6.

### Note on the previous repro

The earlier repro in this issue used `index_granularity = 1` with 2M rows to get 2M marks cheaply. The affected table uses the default `index_granularity = 8192`, so a fix that only bounds the search for small `index_granularity` (for example https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126096) would not help it.

issue.title: Apply `additional_table_filters` keyed on a view when `analyzer_inline_views` is enabled

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Semantic analysis + logical/physical planning + rewrites (Analyzer and Planner modules).

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Allows running workflows for external contributors

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca

issue.body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN   (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Experimental Feature


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
An `additional_table_filters` entry keyed on a view (by its name, `db.name` or alias) is now applied when the experimental setting `analyzer_inline_views` is enabled. Before, such a view was inlined and the entry was ignored, so the query returned rows the filter excluded.

### Description

With the experimental `analyzer_inline_views = 1` (measured on 26.8.34.13, 26.10.2.103 and master):

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x;
INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(10);
CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT x FROM t;
SELECT count() FROM v SETTINGS additional_table_filters = {'v': 'x = 1'}, analyzer_inline_views = 1; -- 10, expected 1
```

The same happens for the `db.name` and alias keys, for a view over the keyed view, and for a view on a JOIN side.

`QueryAnalyzer::inlineViewSubqueryIfNeeded` replaces the view's `TableNode` with its body, while the planner attaches `additional_table_filters` only to `TableNode` / `TableFunctionNode` table expressions, so after inlining the entry keyed on the view matches nothing.

The inliner now leaves such a view as a table, as it already does for a sealed view or a missing `SELECT` grant, and the planner applies the filter exactly as with `analyzer_inline_views = 0`. The matching rule moves from `parseAdditionalFilterAstIfNeeded` into `getAdditionalTableFilter` in `Planner/Utils`, which both call, so the two cannot diverge. Only the keyed view loses inlining: entries on other tables, including the view's own underlying tables, keep it, and the test checks that with `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE`.

Validation: the new test fails on master and passes with the change, also in 50 randomized runs and with parallel replicas; the stateless tests that use `additional_table_filters` and the inline-view tests pass.

I found this while reading the inliner for #130316, which is a different defect; no issue exists for this one.

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`uniqExact` (and `count(DISTINCT)`) over one `String`, `FixedString` or `IPv6` argument is up to 2.7 times faster with `GROUP BY`. The serialized states do not change.

### Description

`uniqExact` stores `sipHash128Padded` of each value, and it hashed one row at a time. Now each chunk of 256 rows first chooses the rows that get a key, as before. One call of the functions of #129204 then hashes those rows, 8 side by side on AVX2 and NEON. The keys are inserted in the same order as before. Fewer than 8 chosen rows are hashed one at a time, as are all rows on builds without AVX2 or NEON.

Each cell is the time with this PR divided by the time on master (below 1 is faster), x86 with AVX2: the median of 3 rounds, each running every query on master and then on this PR, 3 times after a warm-up. The first three columns range over `String` of 0-15, 16-64 and 0-300 bytes, `FixedString(16)` and `FixedString(64)`.

| shape | 1 thread | 16 threads | all threads | `IPv6`, 1 thread | 16 | all |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GROUP BY, no repeats | 0.37-0.55 | 0.57-0.86 | 0.52-0.91 | 0.41-0.58 | 0.60-0.78 | 0.58-0.79 |

| `-If` 1-50%, GROUP BY | 0.85-1.02 | 0.87-1.05 | 0.87-1.04 | 0.82-1.00 | 0.93-1.05 | 0.94-1.03 |
| no key, no repeats | 0.66-1.00 | 0.73-0.98 | 0.76-1.02 | master's code | | |
| GROUP BY with repeats | 0.84-0.97 | 0.94-1.01 | 0.79-0.98 | 0.96 | 0.97 | 0.98 |

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130319
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
A `UNION ALL` branch or subquery whose filter becomes always false after filter push-down (for example an outer `WHERE tag = 'y'` over branches that select the literal tags `'x'`, `'y'` and `'z'`) no longer builds the sets of its `IN (subquery)` conditions or reads its input. The query from #130319 now peaks at 1.2 GB instead of 4.0 GB and runs 2.3 times faster. Closes #130319.


### Description

On 26.10 the query from #130319 (three `UNION ALL` branches `SELECT '<tag>' AS c10, ... WHERE c1 IN (SELECT ... FROM cte)`, outer `c10 = 'y'`) peaks at 4.0 GB instead of 1.0 GB on 26.8; bisected to #105987.

Push-down gives each branch `materialize('<tag>') = 'y'`, and since #105987 the `x` and `z` branch filters fold to `0`, so nothing there uses their `IN` sets. Their `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` still holds the sets, so `addStepsToBuildSets` builds four dead sets, each running the CTE's two `t2 x t3` joins. Before #105987 they were built one at a time during planning (part pruning of the unfolded filter); now `CreatingSetsTransform` builds them concurrently with each other and with the main query.

`addStepsToBuildSets` looks below each `DelayedCreatingSetsStep`. If the steps there are only expressions, filters and the set steps of nested scopes, and one filter's column is a constant the runtime treats as always false, no row reaches a user of the scope's sets: that filter's input becomes `ReadNothingStep` and the sets are detached. An input that can produce totals is kept: totals pass a filter unfiltered (`canProduceTotals` moves to `Optimizations/Utils` from the constant-false JOIN short-circuit). A query failing only in the subquery of such a filtered-out branch now succeeds. Not changed: the subquery of a `GLOBAL IN` against `remote()` still runs while the shard query is built, and `make_distributed_plan` (private preview) plans still build these sets, attached above the distributed source.

Validation (RelWithDebInfo, the issue's data, 5 interleaved runs): 4.03 GB / 5.3-5.9 s -> 1.20-1.21 GB / 2.3-2.6 s, same result checksum. The new test fails on master and passed 50/50 with randomized settings; the new performance test goes from 0.41 s to 0.08 s. About 200 related stateless tests show no new failures.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/130282
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114995
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128866


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
An `INSERT` into Google Cloud Storage with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` no longer fails when the file is larger than `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`.

### Description

On master, an `INSERT` into GCS with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` fails with `Code: 499 ... GCS conditional create of <key> must be a single PUT` as soon as the object exceeds `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`, even for the first write to a new key. #114995 made the new-file write conditional (`If-None-Match: *`), and #128866 makes `WriteBufferFromS3` refuse a conditional multipart upload to GCS, because GCS evaluates no precondition on an XML API multipart upload. Neither change is in a release.

The sink now marks its `If-None-Match` as best-effort (`object_storage_write_if_none_match_best_effort` in `WriteSettings`). For such a write, a GCS multipart upload goes ahead unconditionally, as before #114995, and the GCS `CompleteMultipartUpload` request carries no `If-None-Match` (GCS ignores it, and rejects its `x-goog-if-generation-match` translation). Single-part GCS writes stay conditional, other S3 providers keep the condition on `CompleteMultipartUpload`, and the strict callers (Iceberg metadata, backups, the Iceberg REST catalog) are still refused. So two concurrent same-name inserts can race again on GCS objects above the single-part limit, as agreed in #130282.

Reverting #114995 would also remove the error, but it would bring back the silent overwrites and the data race that PR fixed. A conditional GCS path exists (upload into a temporary key, then `compose` with `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`), but it leaves a visible temporary object in the user's prefix and cannot be tested in CI.

Validation: a new `test_storage_s3` case reaches MinIO as `storage.googleapis.com` (plain and partitioned `INSERT`, 1 MiB single-part limit); it fails on master with `Code: 499` and passes with the fix. Two gtests pin the strict refusal and the unconditional best-effort request.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issue.title: FINAL without rescoring returns stale row versions in vector search

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Vector similarity index in MergeTree: ANN/HNSW index build/query, usearch integration, vector ind...

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- Under FINAL, vector search without rescoring can return a row version a newer insert already replaced.
- Trigger: querying with `FINAL` and `ORDER BY` a distance function with `vector_search_with_rescoring = 0` and `use_skip_indexes_if_final = 1`.
- Expected the latest version of each key, but the old version (or a deleted row with `is_deleted`) comes back instead.
- Impact: silent wrong top-k results for `ReplacingMergeTree` tables with a `vector_similarity` index until parts merge.

Root cause: `optimizeVectorSearchWithVectorIndexSecondPass` in `useVectorSearch.cpp:433` enables the no-rescoring `_distance` rewrite even under `FINAL`, only disabling the rescoring row filter for `FINAL` at line 437. `MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp:1742` now always applies the candidate filter per block before the `FINAL` merge, so a newer version not in its part's candidate set never reaches the merge and the older candidate wins.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: - `optimizeVectorSearchWithVectorIndexSecondPass` keeps the no-rescoring `_distance` rewrite under `FINAL` (`useVectorSearch.cpp:433`); only the rescoring row filter is switched off for `FINAL` (`useVectorSearch.cpp:437`).
- The reader then cuts each part's block down to that part's index candidates (`MergeTreeRangeReader::executePrewhereActionsAndFilterColumns` -> `ReadResult::optimize`, `MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp:1742`) before the `FINAL` merge. The newer version of a key that is not a candidate in its own part never reaches the merge, so the older candidate version wins.
- #126135 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) made that filter mandatory. Before it, blocks where >= 60% of rows were candidates parked the filter in `final_filter` and never applied it, so `FINAL` saw every version. 26.3.34.136 and 26.6.8.7 return the correct `2 1, 3 1, 4 1` for the repro below.
- Blocks with < 60% candidates were filtered before #126135 too: the `index_granularity = 1` variant already returns the stale row on 26.6.8.7.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/useVectorSearch.cpp:433`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8aa46590c607e/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/useVectorSearch.cpp#L433) — no-rescoring rewrite enabled under FINAL; only the rescoring row filter at :437 checks isQueryWithFinal
- [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp:1742`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8aa46590c607e/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp#L1742) — this PR: candidate filter now always applied in the reader, before the FINAL merge

Impact: Silent wrong top-k under `FINAL`. A replaced row version (or an `is_deleted` row) comes back, with its old payload, for `ReplacingMergeTree` tables that have a `vector_similarity` index. Trigger: an update moves a key's vector out of its part's candidate set while an older version is still a candidate in an unmerged part (for example, re-embedding a document). It lasts until the parts merge. Before #126135 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) only blocks with < 60% candidates were affected; now every block is.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master` (`c4a9337df880`); not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Requires `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` so the old and new versions stay in separate unmerged parts.

[▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/35c14ea0-1070-4fa8-bd71-863cf9de82aa)

```sql
-- Test: vector search without rescoring under FINAL must not return a row version replaced by a newer one.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tab;
SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0;
SET vector_search_with_rescoring = 0;
SET use_skip_indexes_if_final = 1;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tab;

CREATE TABLE tab (id UInt64, ver UInt64, vec Array(Float32), INDEX idx vec TYPE vector_similarity('hnsw', 'L2Distance', 2) GRANULARITY 100000000)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(ver) ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 4;

SYSTEM STOP MERGES tab;

INSERT INTO tab VALUES (1, 1, [0, 0]), (10, 1, [50, 0]), (11, 1, [60, 0]), (12, 1, [70, 0]);
-- Moves id 1 away from the reference vector.
INSERT INTO tab VALUES (1, 2, [100, 0]), (2, 1, [1, 0]), (3, 1, [2, 0]), (4, 1, [3, 0]);

SELECT id, ver FROM tab FINAL ORDER BY L2Distance(vec, [0., 0.]) LIMIT 3;
SELECT id, ver FROM tab FINAL ORDER BY L2Distance(vec, [0., 0.]) LIMIT 3 SETTINGS use_skip_indexes = 0;

DROP TABLE tab;
```

Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`c4a9337df880`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

FINAL queries with vector search should return the latest non-deleted version of each row regardless of whether rescoring is enabled.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
2	1
3	1
4	1
2	1
3	1
4	1
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The no-rescoring candidate filter is applied under FINAL too, so a superseded or deleted row version can be returned instead of the current one.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`c4a9337df880`):

```
1	1
2	1
3	1
2	1
3	1
4	1
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Turn off the no-rescoring rewrite under `FINAL`: `bool optimize_plan = !settings.vector_search_with_rescoring && !read_from_mergetree_step->isQueryWithFinal();`. `FINAL` vector queries then take the path `vector_search_with_rescoring = 1` already takes under `FINAL` (exact distance over the selected granules, no row filter), which returns the correct rows in the repro. Trade-off: `FINAL` loses the `_distance` shortcut and reads the vector column. The control `FINAL, no PREWHERE, no rescoring: the vector column is replaced` in `02354_vector_search_final_prewhere.sql` asserts the current rewrite and has to flip. The repro fits next to the rescoring `FINAL` case in `02354_vector_search_rescoring.sql`.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- Backporting #126135 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) to 26.7/26.8/26.9 without the `FINAL` guard carries the dense-block variant to those branches as well (26.3 does not apply the `_distance` rewrite under `FINAL`).

Found during automated review of [PR #126135](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126135); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr126135_001`

comment.body: Acknowledged. I'm working on the PR that rejects `vector_similarity` indexes on non-plain MergeTree engines, with a MergeTree setting that restores the old behaviour; I'll post the link here.

An Iceberg `timestamp` stores a wall-clock reading, but it was mapped to a zone-less `DateTime64(6)` (`timestamp_ns` to `DateTime64(9)`), so values were rendered and literals parsed in the session time zone. The mapping in `IcebergSchemaProcessor::getSimpleType` (all engines, table functions and catalogs) now adds `'UTC'`, where the stored ticks and their rendering coincide, as Paimon maps `TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE` and the Parquet reader treats `isAdjustedToUTC = false`. `timestamptz` is unchanged. `DESCRIBE` shows the new type; under a UTC session values and filters are unchanged. issue.title: 26.3: S3 table with `role_arn` spends ~77 s in STS retries on CREATE and at every server start

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Object storage connectivity (S3/GCS/Azure) including credentials, retries, multipart, etc.

issue.body:
On 26.3, `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = S3(..., extra_credentials(role_arn = ...))` takes about 77 s when STS refuses connections, and every server start pays the same for each such table. `AwsAuthSTSAssumeRoleCredentialsProvider::create` still gives the STS client the AWS SDK default retry strategy (11 attempts, about 25.6 s), and building the S3 client fetches credentials three times. On master and 26.7+ this is bounded by 66039ce735fe8 from #106855.

The same statement in CI, query 2 of `04510_s3_explicit_url_named_secret_mask` (its `role_arn` case reached 26.3 with the backport of #109768):

- 26.3: `Processed in 77.434 sec`, 3 x 11 AssumeRole attempts ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=26.3&sha=9daca7e1368bad4855184174705d0e415e976056&name_0=ReleaseBranchCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_asan%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F2%29))
- master: `Processed in 1.430 sec`, 3 x 4 attempts ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b453ca5f61971938eb03cbbc27c79b15e829767f&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_asan_ubsan%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20parallel%29))
- 04510 median over 30 days in the asan distributed-plan lane: 81.6 s on 26.3 (194 runs), 5.5 s on 26.7, 8.3 s on 26.8.

An interrupted 04510 in a stress run leaves `t_04510` behind, and the post-stress restart loads it. Two leftovers load one after the other (they share the cached credentials provider), about 154 s, which misses the 140 s start budget: [Stress test (amd_msan)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=26.3&sha=31a2be4e8c6f9463d82d4d28910ab79d49643321&name_0=ReleaseBranchCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29) today reports `Cannot start clickhouse-server` while the server is alive and still retrying AssumeRole. 26.6 failed the same way twice in the last month.

@alexey-milovidov, which do you prefer: (A) backporting 66039ce735fe8 alone to 26.3 (`Credentials.cpp` only, its STS hunk applies as is; the label on #106855 would bring the whole PR, which is `pr-backward-incompatible`), or (B) a test-only change to 04510 on master, labeled for 26.3, so an interrupted run cannot leave a table that needs STS at startup? (B) removes only the stress failure, and 26.3 would still spend about 77 s per such table, so I lean to (A).

comment.body: Closing then, thanks. Since this was filed it has not turned a 26.3 stress run red again (the two later 26.3 `Cannot start clickhouse-server` failures have unrelated causes).

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
`INSERT INTO FUNCTION viewIfPermitted(... ELSE f(...))` now requires the write grant of `f` (for example `WRITE ON URL`), as an insert into `f` directly does. Before, only the read grant was checked, so a user with `READ ON URL` and no `WRITE ON URL` could make the server send an insert to a URL. Also fixed `Logical error: 'Unexpected table function name: viewIfPermitted'` when reading through the `ELSE` function with parallel replicas enabled; reading through an explicit cluster function after `ELSE` (`urlCluster`, `s3Cluster`, ...) now fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

### Description

Reported privately; there is no public issue.

On 26.3.60.2 and 26.10.2.103, a user with `READ ON URL` but no `WRITE ON URL` is refused `INSERT INTO FUNCTION url(...)`, yet the same insert through `viewIfPermitted(SELECT ... ELSE url(...))` succeeds when the user cannot run the `SELECT`, and the server sends the rows to the URL. This is the wrong privilege on a request the server originates; the destination's own authentication still applies.

`TableFunctionViewIfPermitted::executeImpl` passed `is_insert_query` to the structure lookup of the `ELSE` function but not to its `execute`, so `ITableFunction::execute` checked `READ` instead of `WRITE` on its source; every `ELSE` function with a source grant (`file`, `s3`, ...) goes through this call. It is now forwarded, as `loop` does for its inner function. The structure check from #116793 stays a read check.

Under parallel replicas, `parallel_replicas_for_cluster_engines` also turned the `ELSE` `url` into a `*Cluster` storage, which cannot rewrite a query that names `viewIfPermitted` and failed with a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (26.3.60.2, 26.10.2.103; an abort in debug builds), hit in [`Stateless tests (arm_binary, ParallelReplicas, s3 storage, parallel)`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=129756&sha=adff553c61e5df82002bb6e5ff710fe6117d0292&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20ParallelReplicas%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29). The `ELSE` function now runs with that setting disabled. An explicit `*Cluster` function after `ELSE` has the same problem (`urlCluster` and `fileCluster` fail the same way, `s3Cluster` edits the arguments of `viewIfPermitted`), so reading one now fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

Validation: the new test (insert denied with only `READ ON URL`, allowed with `WRITE ON URL`; `SELECT` through the fallback allowed, also with parallel replicas; `urlCluster` after `ELSE` rejected) fails 50/50 on master and passes 30/30 with randomized settings; its `urlCluster` case aborts master's debug build.

ELSE urlCluster(...))` and `ELSE fileCluster(...)` abort with that `LOGICAL_ERROR` (signal 6, local 2-shard cluster); a release build returns `Code: 49`. `ELSE s3Cluster(...)` does not reach `ITableFunctionCluster.h:46` at all: `StorageObjectStorageCluster::updateQueryToSendIfNeeded` does not check the name and rewrites the arguments of `viewIfPermitted` as if they were `s3` arguments.

issue.title: 26.10: `toString(key) AS key ... WHERE key IN (subquery)` prunes fewer marks (regression from #118957)

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Query plan optimization: physical plan steps, plan-level rewrites and optimizations (QueryPlan pa...

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Regression found by chReplay production query replay

issue.body:
Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/118957 (automated bisect over master builds narrowed to its merge; the adjacent candidate commit has no CI build, was built from source with the CI recipe and measured good)

### Description

A SELECT aliases the UInt64 sorting-key column as `toString(key) AS key`, then filters with `key IN (subquery)`. On 26.10 primary-key analysis no longer uses this condition (Condition: true), so every granule is read. 26.8 prunes with `toString(key) in N-element set`. Results are identical.

Regression between `26.8.1.672` (OLD) and `26.10.2.142` (NEW).

### How to reproduce

Run the setup once, then measure only the SELECT on each version.

```sql
CREATE TABLE default.t1 (c1 UInt64, c2 Nullable(String), c3 UInt64, c4 DateTime64(3), c5 UInt64) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(c4) ORDER BY c1;
INSERT INTO default.t1 SELECT cityHash64(number) % 2000000000000000000, hex(cityHash64(number, 1)), number % 100003, toDateTime64('2026-01-01 00:00:00', 3) + number, 1000 FROM numbers(30000000);
SELECT count() AS n FROM (SELECT toString(c1) AS c1, argMax(c2, (c5, c4)) AS c2, argMax(c3, (c5, c4)) AS c3, toString(max(c4)) AS c6 FROM default.t1 WHERE c1 IN (SELECT arrayJoin(arrayMap(x -> toUInt64(x), (SELECT groupArray(toString(c1)) FROM (SELECT c1 FROM default.t1 WHERE (c1 % 1000003) = 7 LIMIT 500))))) GROUP BY c1)
SETTINGS compatibility = '25.8';
```

### Performance

Original query (milliseconds; SQL omitted):

| OLD 26.8.1.672 | NEW 26.10.2.142 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 328 | 4501 | 13.72× |

Synthetic repro above, `SelectedMarks` ProfileEvents count of the SELECT (`system.query_log`; the measured regression):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,737 | 3,981 | 2.29× |

Synthetic repro above, read rows of the SELECT (`system.query_log`):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 14,166,580 | 32,549,428 | 2.30× |

Synthetic repro above (milliseconds):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 30 | 57 | 1.90× |

### Expected behavior

Primary-key pruning on `toString(key) IN (subquery set)` should still select only the matching granules, as it does in 26.8.

comment.body:
Fix: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130537

The cause is #118957: it drops an `IN` set atom whose elements are not `String` over a string key expression, because `IN` parses the string into the element type (`'02'` and `'2'` are both `2`). For `toString(c1)` (or `CAST(c1 AS String)`) of an integer or `Date` key, the text holds only canonical numerals, so the set and the index agree. The PR exempts exactly that case. On the issue's setup it selects 1186/3668 granules, the same as the first parent of #118957 (master: 3668/3668), with the same 39 rows.

Reverting #118957 would also bring the pruning back, but it would bring back the wrong results it fixed too (e.g. `s IN (SELECT toUInt8(2))` over a `String` key holding `'02'`), so I would not revert it.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

`KILL QUERY` and `max_execution_time` now interrupt query analysis while it hashes query tree nodes. A query such as `SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM t) GROUP BY ALL` over a table with thousands of columns could keep being analyzed for minutes after it was killed or timed out.

### Description

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100391 (`Stress test (amd_tsan)` hung check, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=100391&sha=b52383a9d6f22385324c2a19e8de228c73df8b0a&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29)). No related open issue found.

The AST fuzzer query `SELECT * FROM (... FROM merge(REGEXP('^'), '.+')) GROUP BY ALL` was still in analysis after 2304 s with `is_cancelled = 1`, although the in-server fuzzer gives every query a 10 s `max_execution_time`.

**Cause.** The tree hash of a `ColumnNode` includes its column source, so `W` GROUP BY keys over a `W`-column subquery cost O(W^2) in every pass that puts the keys into a hash container. Nearly all of the hung query's analysis time went to `GroupingFunctionsResolvePass`, `AggregateFunctionOfGroupByKeysPass` and `OptimizeGroupByFunctionKeysPass`, and every `trace_log` sample of these passes is inside `IQueryTreeNode::getTreeHash`. Nothing in the analyzer checks for cancellation, so the kill is seen only when the pipeline starts.

**Change.** `getTreeHash` already counts the nodes it visits in a thread-local counter. Each time that counter crosses a multiple of 65536, it now calls `CurrentThread::checkIfNotCancelled()`. Hash values do not change. With `timeout_overflow_mode = 'break'` the query is not killed, so nothing changes there.

**Validation** (debug build, 8000 columns): with `max_execution_time = 1` the query fails after 31.8 s before and 1.6 s after; `KILL QUERY ... SYNC` returns after 31.7 s before and 0.17 s after. The new test checks that the timed-out query never reached planning (not elapsed time); it fails on master and with the check removed, and passes 50/50 with randomized settings. Analysis time without a limit is unchanged (median 2.129 s vs 2.135 s).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

On current master (`41a73dec307`, debug build), `SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM wide) GROUP BY ALL` over an 8000-column table with `max_execution_time = 1` runs 26.5 s before it throws `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` (23.6 s with the keys listed explicitly; creating the table alone takes 0.4 s). Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/126735
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126829


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
The `GROUP BY` top-K optimization (`enable_group_by_top_k_optimization`) now also applies when a matched `GROUP BY` key is sorted with `COLLATE`, e.g. `GROUP BY s ORDER BY s COLLATE 'en' LIMIT 10`.

### Description

The optimization was disabled for a `COLLATE` on a matched key. Now `TopKParams` owns the collators, the heap compares collated keys with `compareAtWithCollation` and keeps keys tied with the boundary, and `Aggregating` step v2 serializes each key's locale (plan version 22; older peers get no collated top-K). A collated first key gets no dynamic filter, whose per-row locale comparison would continue after the heap freezes.

A locale comparison costs more than a hash lookup, so with a collated heap the aggregation loops look a row's key up first: a known key is aggregated without a comparison, and only a new key is compared with the boundary. The serialized method of a composite key still compares first, because its key holder is costly to build twice. Otherwise a collated heap starts and freezes like any other.

Release, 32 threads, 100M `hits` rows (18.3M distinct `URL`), `COLLATE 'en' LIMIT 10`, off -> on, medians of 7 runs (measured for da9874b257c5):

| Query | off | on |
|---|---|---|
| `URL` | 895 ms | 382 ms |
| `URL`, 1 thread | 7312 ms | 5729 ms |
| `URL, b` (serialized method) | 1229 ms | 366 ms |
| 20M unique `toString(number)` | 96 ms | 24 ms |
| 1M keys in descending cycles | 67 ms | 35 ms |
| 300K keys in cycles | 66 ms | 35 ms |

CI runs the `URL`, unique and descending-cycles cases in `topk_aggregation_collate.xml`; `05407_group_by_top_k_collation` checks every case against off, also with `sum`, `uniqExact` and no aggregate functions.
